blocks.en: If you want to get out of your current life situation, you shouldn’t be worried about how long it will take to change it. You have nothing better to do than to work on something meaningful. Who cares if it takes 12 months or 12 years when it's going to be difficult either way.
blocks.zh: 如果你想跳出当前的生活处境，就不该纠结于改变它需要多久。反正你也没什么更好的事可做，不如去做点有意义的事。就算过程无论怎样都不轻松，又何必在意是花12个月还是12年呢。

blocks.en: You have to reach the point where your fear of dying mediocre outweighs your fear of looking like an idiot. The first version of anything you do will be embarrassing, that should be obvious, but too many people let that thought keep them the same for decades on end.
blocks.zh: 你必须走到那一步：对平庸终老的恐惧，超过了对显得像个傻瓜的恐惧。你做的任何事，第一版都会很难看，这道理本该显而易见，可太多人就是被这个念头困住，几十年如一日原地踏步。

blocks.en: An influencer is incentivized by attention, so their content must be optimized to be consumed and forgotten (cheap dopamine).
blocks.zh: 网红的激励来自关注度，所以他们的内容必须优化成可被消费完随即遗忘的东西（廉价多巴胺）。

blocks.en: A personal brand is incentivized by money, so their content must be optimized to move you down their sales funnel.
blocks.zh: 个人品牌的激励来自金钱，所以他们的内容必须优化成推动你走完他们的销售漏斗。

blocks.en: An artisan is incentivized by the satisfaction that comes from the quality of their work. They need attention and money, but for the sole purpose of spending more time on work they enjoy and the impact it has.
blocks.zh: 而匠人的激励来自作品质量本身带来的满足感。他们也需要关注和金钱，但唯一目的是把更多时间花在自己享受的工作及其产生的影响上。

blocks.en: Become an artisan.
blocks.zh: 去做一个匠人。

blocks.en: AI made it so anyone can build anything, but everyone was already distracted, so AI just made it 10x worse. Your competition was non existent to begin with, and your only real competition is your own mind.
blocks.zh: AI让任何人都能创造任何东西，但每个人早已被分心，所以AI只是把情况恶化了10倍。你的竞争对手从一开始就不存在，你唯一真正的竞争是你自己的心智。

blocks.en: Most people who dream of a quiet life without work are just exhausted from work they hate. The reason you get bored on vacation after a week is that you are meant to move, pursue something exciting, and engage your body and mind in something useful. Do whatever it takes to find work that energizes you. It may take years, but it will have the most meaningful effect on your quality of life.
blocks.zh: 大多数梦想着不工作、过安静生活的人，只是被自己厌恶的工作耗尽了。你在度假一周后就感到无聊，是因为你注定要动起来、追求令人兴奋的事物、让身心投入到有用的事情中。不惜一切代价找到能让你充满能量的工作。这可能需要数年，但它会对你的生活质量产生最有意义的影响。

blocks.en: If you want to start writing, the greatest thing you can do is block off 1 hour every morning and stick to it. Absolutely no exposure to other opinions or distractions (social media, messages, phone). You need space for creative ideas and modern life is great at taking that from you.
blocks.zh: 如果你想开始写作，你能做的最好的事，就是每天早上划出一小时，然后坚持下去。绝不接触其他观点，也不受任何干扰（社交媒体、消息、手机）。你需要给创意想法留出空间，而现代生活最擅长的，就是把它从你手里夺走。

blocks.en: You can spend 5 years, working harder than anyone else, writing the best book in the world, but if nobody knows about it, then you will not be a successful author.
blocks.zh: 你可以花5年时间，比任何人都更努力，写出世界上最好的一本书，但如果没人知道它，你就不会成为一位成功的作者。

blocks.en: This is the downfall of most creatives. They hate marketing, but marketing is 80% of their success.
blocks.zh: 大多数创意人的失败就在这里。他们讨厌营销，但营销占了他们成功的80%。

blocks.en: If you get addicted to things easily, you have one of the rarest traits there is.
blocks.zh: 如果你很容易对事情上瘾，那你拥有一种极其罕见的特质。

blocks.en: Most people can't stay interested in anything for more than a week. You can lose 6 hours to something without noticing.
blocks.zh: 大多数人无法对任何事情保持超过一周的兴趣。而你可以不知不觉地在某件事上投入6个小时。

blocks.en: Right now that goes to games, feeds, and whatever hooks you first. That's the only problem.
blocks.zh: 现在，这种特质被用在了游戏、信息流，以及任何最先钩住你的东西上。这就是唯一的问题。

blocks.en: Pick one hard thing actually worth being addicted to. A skill, your body, your work. Give it the same obsession for 2 years and you'll pass people who've been at it for 10.
blocks.zh: 选一件真正值得上瘾的难事。一项技能、你的身体、你的工作。用同样的痴迷投入2年，你就会超过那些已经做了10年的人。

blocks.en: All you have to do is commit for 6 months.
blocks.zh: 你要做的，就是承诺6个月。

blocks.en: That's not a lot. It's actually very little.
blocks.zh: 这不算多。实际上非常少。

blocks.en: 6 months is 1% of 50 years, and most people can't stick to something that will change the trajectory of their life for 2 weeks.
blocks.zh: 6个月只是50年的1%，而大多数人连两周都坚持不了一件会改变自己人生轨迹的事。

blocks.en: You need to be lore-maxxing. Taking risks. Failing miserably. Relentlessly strategizing and experimenting. Nobody wants to die with a story that isn't worth telling.
blocks.zh: 你需要成为“故事最大化”的人。去冒险。彻底失败。不断地制定策略并实验。没有人想带着一个不值得讲述的故事死去。

blocks.en: It sucks to say it, but the default is overweight, dumb, and broke.
blocks.zh: 这话说起来很糟，但默认状态就是超重、愚笨、贫穷。

blocks.en: You don't live in a world where you have to hunt for your food and figure out how to survive.
blocks.zh: 你并不是生活在一个必须打猎觅食、想办法活下去的世界里。

blocks.en: You live in a world where - unless you decide to endlessly practice self-education, because schools do not teach you how to live a good life - you will automatically choose hyperpalatable foods, sit on your couch all day, and get the job that pays enough to survive because that's just what you were supposed to do.
blocks.zh: 你生活的世界里——除非你决定无止境地自我教育，因为学校并不教你如何过好这一生——你会自动选择超适口食物、整天坐在沙发上，找一份收入刚好够生存的工作，因为那本来就是别人期望你做的。

blocks.en: Write more. Write to think. Write until you're no longer confused. Write about the problems you already solved. Write for the person you were 2 years ago. Write so you never lose what took you years to figure out. A simple writing habit can change absolutely everything.
blocks.zh: 多写。通过写作来思考。写到不再困惑为止。写你已经解决过的问题。为你两年前的自己而写。写下来，这样你永远不会丢失花了好几年才想明白的东西。一个简单的写作习惯，可以彻底改变一切。

blocks.en: One of the worst feelings in life is knowing you're meant for more and doing nothing about it.
blocks.zh: 人生中最糟糕的感觉之一，就是知道自己注定不止于此，却对此无动于衷。

blocks.en: If you get addicted to things easily, good, your problem is aim. Point that same obsession at a skill, your body, or your work for 2 years and people will start calling you "disciplined" instead.
blocks.zh: 如果你容易对事物上瘾，很好，你的问题在于瞄准。将同样的痴迷指向一项技能、你的身体或你的工作2年，人们就会开始称你为“自律”而不是其他。

blocks.en: Pick a challenge too big for who you are now.
blocks.zh: 选择一个对现在的你来说过于巨大的挑战。

blocks.en: That's how people change. A challenge above your level drags the new version of you out.
blocks.zh: 人就是这样改变的。一个超出你水平的挑战会拖出新的你。

blocks.en: It will suck. You'll fail constantly. You'll feel like a fraud for months. Your old self will beg you to stay the same.
blocks.zh: 它会很糟糕。你会不断失败。几个月里你会觉得自己像个骗子。旧的你会乞求你不要改变。

blocks.en: But if you can pull this off, 10-20 times throughout your life, you will blow past everyone else.
blocks.zh: 但如果你能在一生中完成10-20次，你将远远超过其他所有人。

blocks.en: There are 3 things you can sell:
blocks.zh: 你可以卖三样东西：

blocks.en:
1) Your time, capped at 24 hours
2) Your things, capped by inventory
3) Your mind, for all of history, capped by how many rooms you could be in
blocks.zh:
1）你的时间，上限24小时
2）你的物品，受库存限制
3）你的思想，贯穿历史，受你能同时身处多少房间的限制

blocks.en: Social media changed that completely. A brain and an internet connection can change your life.
blocks.zh: 社交媒体彻底改变了这一点。一个大脑和一根网线就能改变你的人生。

blocks.en: The most dangerous moment is right after you win.
blocks.zh: 最危险的时刻就在你获胜之后。

blocks.en: You did it. You made the money. You quit your job. You built the physique. You got the girl. Now what? Most people let themselves decline into misery because their driving force has now vanished.
blocks.zh: 你做到了。你赚到了钱。你辞了工作。你练出了体格。你追到了那个女孩。然后呢？大多数人让自己陷入痛苦，因为他们的驱动力消失了。

blocks.en: You need another mountain to climb. You need to understand that it is a gift, not a curse, to always be in the pursuit of your potential - the constant balance of challenge and skill is what makes life meaningful. There is no final top of the mountain.
blocks.zh: 你需要另一座山去攀登。你需要明白，永远在追求自己的潜力是一种礼物，而非诅咒——挑战与技能的持续平衡才是生活有意义的原因。没有最终的山顶。

blocks.en: If you want to make the most progress you've ever made in your life, you need to be alone. You need an extended period of isolation, not influenced by friends or media, spent building your future. You need space to learn, think, experiment, and fail.
blocks.zh: 如果你想取得人生中最大的进步，你需要独处。你需要一段长时间的隔离，不受朋友或媒体影响，用来构建你的未来。你需要空间去学习、思考、实验和失败。

blocks.en: Give yourself 6 months. Focus solely on the development of your mind, body, spirit, and finances. This is how you get ahead of most people.
blocks.zh: 给自己6个月。只专注于发展你的心智、身体、精神和财务。这就是你如何超越大多数人的方法。

blocks.en: "How do I start posting online"
blocks.zh: “我该如何开始在网上发帖”

blocks.en:
- Pick a fucking idea
- Stop trying to find the perfect one
- Write the first thing that comes to mind
- Rewrite it slightly better, then post
blocks.zh:
- 选一个他妈的想法
- 别再试图找到完美的那个
- 写下第一个想到的东西
- 稍微改得更好一点，然后发布

blocks.en: Just get in the habit of writing out interesting ideas and trust that you'll get better over time (you know, how everything else in life works).
blocks.zh: 养成写下有趣想法的习惯，相信你会随着时间变得更好（你知道的，生活中其他事情也是这样运作的）。

blocks.en: If you want to dramatically improve your quality of life, learn to recover your attention quickly after something steals it. Social media arguments, stressful thoughts, minor inconveniences. Most of it is noise that steals hours to days of enjoyment. Breathe and let it go.
blocks.zh: 如果你想大幅提升生活质量，就学会在注意力被偷走后迅速把它收回来。社交媒体上的争论、压力重重的念头、小小的不便。大多数都是噪音，会偷走你数小时乃至数天的快乐。深呼吸，随它去吧。

blocks.en: You don't need a PhD in a topic before you can start doing it. You don't need to watch 10 YouTube videos, 20 podcasts, and read 5 books before you start.
blocks.zh: 你不需要先拿到某个领域的博士学位才能开始做它。你不需要在开始之前先看 10 个 YouTube 视频、20 个播客、读 5 本书。

blocks.en: That only gets you stuck in a cycle of mental masturbation and feeling like you never know enough.
blocks.zh: 那只会让你陷入精神自慰的循环，总觉得自己知道得不够多。

blocks.en: Most people should start learning only after they've started doing the thing.
blocks.zh: 大多数人应该先动手去做，然后再开始学习。

blocks.en: You need to be delusional if you want to be successful because your goals shape what you perceive. You won't notice the rare opportunity or life path if your goal isn't so big that others think you are crazy.
blocks.zh: 想要成功，你得有点妄想，因为目标塑造你的感知。如果你的目标不够大，以至于别人觉得你疯了，你就不会注意到那些罕见的机会或人生道路。

blocks.en: The paradox of life is that everything is a disaster and everything is just fine. The difference is where you put your attention.
blocks.zh: 生活的悖论在于，一切既是灾难，也一切安好。区别只在于你把注意力放在哪里。

blocks.en: AI makes being average at any skill available to everyone, which makes average work worthless. If you take the time to become incredibly good at what you do you won't have to worry about being replaced.
blocks.zh: AI让任何人都能轻易达到平均水准，这使得平庸的工作毫无价值。如果你花时间让自己变得极其擅长你所做的事，你就不必担心被取代。

blocks.en: Patterns I've noticed in people who aren't necessarily unhappy, but aren't going anywhere with their lives:
blocks.zh: 我注意到一些人，他们未必不快乐，但生活毫无进展，他们有这样的模式：

blocks.en:
- Never learn anything new unless they're forced to
- Don't set goals unless their survival / finances make them insecure
- Talk about what's happening in the world rather than what they're working on
- Aren't aware of any of this, and making them aware doesn't hurts more than it helps
blocks.zh:
- 除非被迫，否则从不学习新东西
- 除非生存或财务让他们感到不安，否则不设定目标
- 谈论世界上发生的事，而不是他们正在做的事
- 对此毫无觉察，而让他们觉察到这一点，弊大于利

blocks.en: Hard place to be.
blocks.zh: 处境艰难。

blocks.en: The most interesting people are walking contradictions.
blocks.zh: 最有意思的人，本身就是行走的矛盾体。

blocks.en:
Jacked intellectuals.
Casual billionaires.
Spiritual fighters.
blocks.zh:
肌肉发达的知识分子。
随性自在的亿万富翁。
修习灵性的战士。

blocks.en: Life is better when you can't be shoved in a box that others can easily make sense of.
blocks.zh: 当你无法被别人轻易塞进一个他们一眼就能看懂的盒子里时，你的人生会更精彩。

blocks.en: There will be 3 types of people in the future:
blocks.zh: 未来会有三种人：

blocks.en: The Purists - reject AI and become new-age hippies
blocks.zh: 纯粹主义者——拒绝 AI，成为新时代的嬉皮士

blocks.en: The Automatons - outsource every decision and become machines
blocks.zh: 自动机器——把所有决策都外包出去，沦为机器

blocks.en: The New Renaissance Man - maintains humanity and leverages tech to do what used to be impossible
blocks.zh: 新文艺复兴人——保有人性，同时借助科技去做过去不可能做到的事

blocks.en: When calories became cheap, convenient, and abundant, bodies decayed.
blocks.zh: 当卡路里变得廉价、便捷、唾手可得，身体就开始衰败。

blocks.en: Thinking is now cheap.
blocks.zh: 如今，思考也变得廉价了。

blocks.en: The fastest way to become articulate on a topic is to write until you're no longer confused.
blocks.zh: 想在一个话题上把话说得清楚明白，最快的方法就是一直写，写到不再困惑为止。

blocks.en: We're in the middle of the second renaissance where proof of work replaces the resume, an audience replaces the employer, and taste replaces credentials.
blocks.zh: 我们正处在第二次文艺复兴之中：作品见证取代了简历，受众取代了雇主，品味取代了资历。

blocks.en: Most social media tools suck.
blocks.zh: 大多数社交媒体工具都不太行。

blocks.en: (I've tried them all over 7 years of doing this).
blocks.zh: （这七年里我把它们全都试了一遍。）

blocks.en: They claim to help you go viral.
blocks.zh: 它们声称能帮你爆红。

blocks.en: They claim that you'll grow fast on social media.
blocks.zh: 它们声称能让你在社交媒体上快速涨粉。

blocks.en: They claim that they'll make it easy on you, so you can just grow your following without having any form of skill or understanding.
blocks.zh: 它们声称会把一切都给你安排妥当，让你不需要任何技能或认知，就能把粉丝涨起来。

blocks.en: And now they're trying to go fully agentic, which only works if you know what you're doing (we'll talk about that later, we built the MCP for social media).
blocks.zh: 如今它们还想彻底走向智能代理化，可这东西只有在你清楚自己在干什么时才管用（这个我们稍后再聊，我们已经为社交媒体做了一套 MCP）。

blocks.en: Plus, when everyone has an advantage, it is no longer an advantage.
blocks.zh: 再说了，当每个人都有优势时，优势就不再是优势了。

blocks.en:
I promise you, I love AI, but having it write everything for you, especially as a beginner, is a death sentence.
You may get lucky and have one, two, or three posts do well.
blocks.zh:
我向你保证，我热爱 AI，但让它替你写一切——尤其是作为一个新手——那是死路一条。
你也许能走运，有一篇、两篇、三篇帖子表现不错。

blocks.en: You may gain a lot of followers (because that's what they promise to get you to buy), but then what?
blocks.zh: 你也许能涨很多粉（毕竟这就是他们承诺给你的东西，好让你掏钱），可然后呢？

blocks.en: Can you replicate it?
blocks.zh: 你复现得了吗？

blocks.en: Does your audience actually care about who you are?
blocks.zh: 你的受众真的在意你是谁吗？

blocks.en: Or are you just a one hit wonder like every other creator who tries to get-followers-quick?
blocks.zh: 还是说，你也像其他那些急于涨粉的创作者一样，只是个昙花一现的爆款制造机？

blocks.en: The creators you love... the ones who put out ideas that actually change your life, understand that the creative process (capturing, resurfacing, and synthesizing ideas) is your competitive edge when everyone is racing to put out as much slop as possible.
blocks.zh: 你真正欣赏的创作者……那些能提出真正改变你人生的想法的创作者，都明白一件事：当所有人都在争先恐后地产出大量垃圾内容时，创作过程本身（捕捉、重新发掘、综合想法）才是你的竞争优势。

blocks.en: So we built an actual solution.
blocks.zh: 所以我们打造了一个真正的解决方案。

blocks.en: For the people who know deep down that the toys and gimmicks being marketed to you aren't a long term strategy.
blocks.zh: 它属于那些内心深处明白，推销给你的那些花哨工具和噱头并非长久之计的人。

blocks.en: It's called Eden. The second brain for creators.
blocks.zh: 它叫 Eden。创作者的第二大脑。

blocks.en: It has every scheduling, analytics, auto-dm, and outlier research (for all platforms) features that everyone else has - built by someone who knows what's useful and what's not.
blocks.zh: 别人有的功能它全都有——定时发布、数据分析、自动私信、爆款研究（覆盖所有平台），而且是由一个真正懂得什么有用、什么没用的人打造的。

blocks.en: But it also has the ideation process built in, which cannot be skipped.
blocks.zh: 但它还把构思流程内置其中，而这一步无法跳过。

blocks.en: Here's what it looks like, and how to write a post people actually care about:
blocks.zh: 下面就是它的样子，以及如何写出人们真正在意的帖子：

blocks.en: 1) Save inspiration from anywhere (and read + highlight)
blocks.zh: 1）随时随地保存灵感（并阅读、划线标注）

blocks.en: Capturing ideas, posts, links, and highlights inside of an agent or AI chat sounds like hell.
blocks.zh: 把想法、帖子、链接和划线内容都塞进一个智能体或 AI 聊天界面里，听起来简直是场噩梦。

blocks.en: Not everything needs to, or should be, jammed into a chat UI.
blocks.zh: 不是所有东西都需要、或者说都应该被硬塞进聊天界面里。

blocks.en: In Eden you can:
blocks.zh: 在 Eden 里，你可以：

blocks.en: - Paste any social post link (we transcribe any post)
blocks.zh: - 粘贴任何社交帖子的链接（我们会转录任何帖子）

blocks.en: - Integrate with Kindle, Snipd, or Readwise
blocks.zh: - 接入 Kindle、Snipd 或 Readwise

blocks.en: - Pull in X or Substack bookmarks
blocks.zh: - 导入 X 或 Substack 的书签

blocks.en: - Jot down quick ideas or write inside docs
blocks.zh: - 随手记下快速想法，或在文档里写作

blocks.en: - Open any YouTube transcript or article in Reader mode and highlight it
blocks.zh: - 在阅读器模式下打开任何 YouTube 文字稿或文章，并对其划线标注

blocks.en: We auto-categorize and tag everything for you, so our Deep Synthesis agent can find novel connections and relations across your library - making it easy to surface idaes you thought you lost.
blocks.zh: 我们会自动为你分类并打标签，这样我们的深度综合智能体就能在你的整个素材库中找出新颖的关联和联系——轻松重新发掘你以为早已丢失的想法。

blocks.en: 2) Research what's working, study top creators
blocks.zh: 2）研究什么内容有效，研究顶尖创作者

blocks.en: Outlier tools are the bread and butter for every creator.
blocks.zh: 爆款工具是每个创作者的家常便饭。

blocks.en: When you do research for a YouTube video, you look for high performing titles and thumbnails, and you study what worked for others.
blocks.zh: 当你为一条 YouTube 视频做调研时，你会寻找高表现的标题和缩略图，并研究别人的成功之处。

blocks.en: But what about every other platform?
blocks.zh: 但其他平台呢？

blocks.en: We have a social corpus of 3m+ posts across all platforms and growing.
blocks.zh: 我们拥有一个覆盖所有平台、超过 300 万条帖子的社交语料库，而且还在不断增长。

blocks.en: You can scroll the Discover page for inspiration, search any creator and filter by top posts, or use Deep Social in the AI chat to search across all of them.
blocks.zh: 你可以在 Discover 页面浏览寻找灵感，搜索任意创作者并按热门帖子筛选，或者在 AI 聊天中使用 Deep Social 对所有这些内容进行搜索。

blocks.en: This is what gives the MCP access to trending topics without scraping millions of posts yourself.
blocks.zh: 正是这一点让 MCP 能够获取热门话题，而无需你自己抓取海量帖子。

blocks.en: 3) Create with everything in one place, build swipe files
blocks.zh: 3) 在一处完成全部创作，建立素材库

blocks.en: I don't think I will ever give up writing.
blocks.zh: 我觉得我永远不会放弃写作。

blocks.en: I love sitting down in the morning, opening up a page, researching good ideas, and turning it into something worth sharing.
blocks.zh: 我喜欢清晨坐下来，打开一页纸，研究好的想法，然后把它变成值得分享的内容。

blocks.en: In Eden, you work on Boards.
blocks.zh: 在 Eden 中，你在 Boards 上工作。

blocks.en: You can paste social posts and build shareable swipe files, or you can add your outlines and drafts while having your library, chat, or ideas open right next to it.
blocks.zh: 你可以粘贴社交媒体帖子，建立可分享的素材库；也可以添加大纲和草稿，同时把资料库、聊天或灵感窗口开在旁边。

blocks.en: 4) Chat with anything to get the information you need
blocks.zh: 4) 与任何内容对话，获取你需要的信息

blocks.en: Claude and ChatGPT are essential, but they are blind.
blocks.zh: Claude 和 ChatGPT 不可或缺，但它们是“盲”的。

blocks.en: They can't read social links. They can't see what's trending.
blocks.zh: 它们读不了社交链接，也看不到什么正在流行。

blocks.en: When you're writing scripts, articles, posts, or drafts - you need to be able to pull information from the sources you research. In today's world, that usually means social posts, YouTube videos, and articles.
blocks.zh: 当你写脚本、文章、帖子或草稿时，你需要能够从你研究过的来源中提取信息。在今天，这通常意味着社交媒体帖子、YouTube 视频和文章。

blocks.en: 5) Draft, schedule, and publish to all platforms
blocks.zh: 5) 起草、排期并发布到所有平台

blocks.en: X, Instagram, LinkedIn, Substack, Threads, TikTok, and YouTube shorts.
blocks.zh: X、Instagram、LinkedIn、Substack、Threads、TikTok 和 YouTube Shorts。

blocks.en: And yes, we are one of the first to support article scheduling to X and Substack.
blocks.zh: 没错，我们是最早支持向 X 和 Substack 定时发布文章的工具之一。

blocks.en: You don't have to copy paste to every platform anymore.
blocks.zh: 你不必再复制粘贴到每个平台。

blocks.en: You simply write, schedule, and let it go out to all platforms.
blocks.zh: 你只管写作、排期，然后让它发布到所有平台。

blocks.en: 6) Or do it all from the MCP
blocks.zh: 6) 或者全部通过 MCP 完成

blocks.en: I don't believe that the future of content is fully agentic.
blocks.zh: 我不认为内容的未来会完全由智能体主导。

blocks.en: But, that doesn't mean that AI can't help with researching top posts, ideation, and scheduling content.
blocks.zh: 但这并不意味着 AI 不能在研究热门帖子、构思创意和安排内容发布方面提供帮助。

blocks.en: You do the writing and thinking, let AI handle the busy work and resurfacing of ideas you need to find.
blocks.zh: 你来写作和思考，让 AI 处理繁琐的工作，并帮你重新找出你需要寻找的想法。

blocks.en: With Eden, you don't need to give up your Claude, Hermes, or other agentic workflows. You simply connect the MCP and now you can build your own agentic content system, if that's your cup of tea.
blocks.zh: 有了 Eden，你无需放弃 Claude、Hermes 或其他智能体工作流。你只需连接 MCP，现在就能搭建自己的智能体内容系统——如果你喜欢这种方式的话。

blocks.en: Eden is the Social Media MCP.
blocks.zh: Eden 就是社交媒体 MCP。

blocks.en: You don't have to pay for scrapers anymore.
blocks.zh: 你不必再为抓取工具付费。

blocks.en: You can finally access trends, any social link, and any account.
blocks.zh: 你终于可以访问热门趋势、任意社交链接和任意账号。

blocks.en: You can access your analytics, build content dashboards with our infrastructure (that you don't need to maintain as a full time job), and post.
blocks.zh: 你可以查看分析数据，用我们的基础设施搭建内容仪表盘（无需全职维护），还能发布内容。

blocks.en: We've actually built 4 skills for deep topic research, personal brand strategy, building a content command center, and more - we'll link those below.
blocks.zh: 我们其实已经开发了4项技能，涵盖深度话题研究、个人品牌策略、构建内容指挥中心等——下方会附上链接。

blocks.en: All in all:
blocks.zh: 总而言之：

blocks.en: If you're a creator, Eden is your base.
blocks.zh: 如果你是创作者，Eden 就是你的基地。

blocks.en: It's where you write, research, and publish every single day.
blocks.zh: 你每天都可以在这里写作、研究和发布内容。

blocks.en: Try it free below:
blocks.zh: 免费试用下方链接：

blocks.en: Friendly reminder that you choose your reactions. You don't have to go into a fit of rage when an idiot cuts you off in traffic. You could laugh instead, and if you choose to react that way consistently enough, the quality of your life goes through the roof.
blocks.zh: 友情提醒：你的反应由你选择。当有个白痴在路上别你车时，你不必暴跳如雷。你完全可以一笑置之，而如果你 consistently 选择这样反应，你的生活质量将一飞冲天。

blocks.en: A core sign of low intelligence is not being able to hold two contradictory ideas in your mind at once.
blocks.zh: 智力低下的一个核心标志是，无法同时在头脑中容纳两个相互矛盾的想法。

blocks.en: Most people treat an idea as a team to join.
blocks.zh: 大多数人把某个想法当作一支要加入的队伍。

blocks.en: Once they join that team, the opposing view becomes a threat. You stop thinking and start reacting.
blocks.zh: 一旦加入那支队伍，对立的观点就成了一种威胁。你不再思考，开始条件反射。

blocks.en: The average person does not try to solve their problems or struggles. They get stuck in a routine and live the same day over and over. It does not cross their minds to snap out of it, engage in strategic thinking, and change direction so they can eventually reach a more advantageous position in life.
blocks.zh: 普通人不会试图解决他们的问题或困境。他们陷入常规，日复一日地过着同样的生活。他们根本没想到要摆脱这种状态，进行战略思考，改变方向，从而最终在生活中达到更有利的位置。

blocks.en: If you want to get ahead of 90% of people, all you have to do is pause, think, and actually attempt to overcome the struggle you're faced with.
blocks.zh: 如果你想超越90%的人，你所要做的就是停下来，思考，并真正尝试克服你所面临的困境。

blocks.en: Gentle reminder:
blocks.zh: 温馨提示：

blocks.en: Block out time away from the screen.
blocks.zh: 留出远离屏幕的时间。

blocks.en: Force yourself if you have to.
blocks.zh: 如果需要，强迫自己。

blocks.en: Read a book for once. Hit the coffee shop. Do anything that gives your mind space to process all of the noise you've accumulated.
blocks.zh: 偶尔读本书。去咖啡馆坐坐。做任何能让你大脑空间处理你积累的所有噪音的事情。

blocks.en: You will feel the immense difference in mental clarity.
blocks.zh: 你会感受到思维清晰度的巨大差异。

blocks.en: If you even slightly entertain the thought of failure, you give your mind a chance to start noticing reasons to fail. But if the only option on your mind is to win, then the world seems to conspire in your favor, because your mind will notice opportunities it wouldn't have before. Become delusionally optimistic, not because it's realistic, but because it's effective. It drastically increases your chances of success.
blocks.zh: 如果你哪怕稍微考虑一下失败的想法，你就给了大脑一个机会开始注意到失败的理由。但如果你心中唯一的选择是赢，那么世界似乎会 conspire in your favor，因为你的大脑会注意到以前不会注意到的机会。变得妄想般地乐观，不是因为它现实，而是因为它有效。它极大地增加了你成功的机会。

blocks.en: Your attention works fine. You don't need to "fix" it. You just don't have a target that makes it easy to focus for months on end. You don't have a vision so strong that everything else becomes boring.
blocks.zh: 你的注意力没问题。你不需要去“修复”它。你只是缺少一个能让你轻松连续数月专注的目标。你没有一个足够强大的愿景，让其他一切变得乏味。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to learn, start writing.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道学什么，就开始写作。

blocks.en: Writing teaches you how to think, how to learn, and how to attract an audience that supports your work. Those 3 skills are needed more than ever.
blocks.zh: 写作教你如何思考、如何学习，以及如何吸引支持你工作的受众。这三项技能比以往任何时候都更需要。

blocks.en: You can't focus because you never let yourself be bored. Actually bored. Not "bored" scrolling on your phone taxing your brain into oblivion with more dopamine in 10 minutes than people a thousand years ago would get in an entire month.
blocks.zh: 你无法集中注意力，因为你从不让自己感到无聊。真正的无聊。不是那种“无聊”地刷手机，让大脑在10分钟内接收的 dopamine 比一千年前的人整个月得到的还多，从而把大脑推向 oblivion。

blocks.en: Skills that have nothing to do with money but are worth dedicating an immense amount of practice to:
blocks.zh: 与金钱无关但值得投入大量时间练习的技能：

blocks.en:
- Charisma
- Metacognition
- Critical thinking
- Sitting with discomfort
- Articulating what you believe and why
- Changing your beliefs when presented with new information
blocks.zh:
- 魅力
- 元认知
- 批判性思维
- 与不适共处
- 清晰表达你的信念及其原因
- 面对新信息时改变你的信念

blocks.en: Almost nobody actually practices these and it shows.
blocks.zh: 几乎没有人真正练习这些，而这一点显而易见。

blocks.en: If you don't wake up excited and go to bed tired, drop everything and think of what your future will look like if you keep repeating the same day for the rest of your life. Sit with that discomfort until a new direction appears.
blocks.zh: 如果你早上醒来不兴奋，晚上上床时不觉疲惫，那就放下一切，想想如果你余生都重复同一天，你的未来会是什么样子。与那种不适感共处，直到新的方向出现。

blocks.en: The fastest way to change your life is to rip yourself out of your (physical and digital) environment. Change everything overnight. The places you go, the accounts you follow, the info you consume, etc. It's difficult but it absolutely works.
blocks.zh: 改变人生最快的方法，就是把自己从（现实和数字）环境中连根拔起。在一夜之间改变一切。你去的地方、你关注的账号、你消费的信息，等等。这很难，但绝对有效。

blocks.en: Stress is great for brute-forcing mindless tasks, but it absolutely destroys your ability to think spatially. It destroys your creativity, which is the one thing that will give you a competitive advantage over everyone optimizing for productivity.
blocks.zh: 压力对于强行推进无脑任务很有效，但它绝对会破坏你进行空间思考的能力。它会摧毁你的创造力，而创造力正是让你在所有人都在优化生产力时获得竞争优势的唯一东西。

blocks.en: You only need 1 hour.
blocks.zh: 你只需要1小时。

blocks.en: 1 hour of building. 1 hour of writing. 1 hour of lifting. 1 hour of studying.
blocks.zh: 1小时用来构建。1小时用来写作。1小时用来举铁。1小时用来学习。

blocks.en: 1 hour of any form of bettering yourself, because it quickly compounds.
blocks.zh: 1小时用来做任何形式的自我提升，因为它会迅速产生复利。

blocks.en: 1 hour feels like nothing until you look back 365 hours later and everything's changed.
blocks.zh: 1小时感觉微不足道，直到365小时后你回头看，一切都已经改变。

blocks.en: The most important decision of your life
blocks.zh: 你人生中最重要的决定

blocks.en: If you don't have a goal so meaningful it makes other people's opinions irrelevant, you will lose control of your life. You will adopt the goals assigned to you by your parents, peers, or society.
blocks.zh: 如果你没有一个深刻到让别人的意见变得无关紧要的目标，你就会失去对生活的掌控。你会接受父母、同龄人或社会分配给你的目标。

blocks.en: The 2-4 hours you spend scrolling each day (or 730-1460 hours each year) is more than enough time to write a book, build a business, or get in shape. In the moment, it seems like nothing. That's why it's so dangerous. Your time disappears without you being conscious of it.
blocks.zh: 你每天花2-4小时刷手机（或每年730-1460小时），这时间足够写一本书、建立一项事业或练出好身材。当下，它似乎微不足道。这就是它如此危险的原因。你的时间在不知不觉中消失了。

blocks.en: Yes, anyone can build anything now. We know. But it wasn't that hard to do before. You execute a series of steps toward a goal.
blocks.zh: 是的，现在任何人都能构建任何东西。我们知道。但以前也没那么难。你朝着一个目标执行一系列步骤。

blocks.en: The problem is psychological. Most people will still fail to start, and even more will fail to iterate. Your competition isn't as large as you think.
blocks.zh: 问题在于心理层面。大多数人仍然无法开始，更多的人无法迭代。你的竞争对手并没有你想象的那么多。

blocks.en: How to master any skill fast:
blocks.zh: 如何快速掌握任何技能：

blocks.en:
- stop studying
- outline a project
- start building it
- hit a roadblock
- figure out how to overcome it
- repeat 4 and 5 for the rest of your life
blocks.zh:
- 停止学习
- 规划一个项目
- 开始构建它
- 遇到障碍
- 想办法克服它
- 在余生中重复第4步和第5步

blocks.en: Most people don't get past 1, the rest spiral into complacency after 4.
blocks.zh: 大多数人过不了第1步，其余的人在遇到第4步后就陷入自满。

blocks.en: Normalize disappearing for an extended period of time to do a factory reset on your focus and creativity.
blocks.zh: 让长时间消失成为常态，以便对你的专注力和创造力进行出厂重置。

blocks.en: Most people quit because they forget that you have to be bad at something before you can be good at it. It's so obvious. You suck. Of course you're not going to win in 2 weeks. But if you can learn to enjoy extended periods of failure, you will make it very, very far in life.
blocks.zh: 大多数人放弃，是因为他们忘了：你必须先做得糟糕，才能变得出色。这太明显了。你现在很烂。你当然不可能在两周内获胜。但如果你能学会享受长期的失败，你将在人生中走得非常非常远。

blocks.en: You aren't going to get lucky repeating the same day.
blocks.zh: 重复同一天，你不会走运。

blocks.en: You need to go on more side quests. Weekly. Daily if you can. Even one tiny new decision can substantially increase your chances at luck.
blocks.zh: 你需要进行更多的支线任务。每周。如果可以，每天。即使一个微小的新决定也能大幅增加你获得幸运的机会。

blocks.en: If you feel lost, build something.
blocks.zh: 如果你感到迷茫，就去创造点什么。

blocks.en: A business. Your body. A skill set. Anything that gives you a reason to learn and focus.
blocks.zh: 一门生意。你的身体。一项技能。任何能给你理由去学习和专注的事情。

blocks.en: Don't worry about choosing the right thing. Don't think about how difficult it will be.
blocks.zh: 别担心选不对。别去想会有多难。

blocks.en: Just start moving forward and you'll find a path that feels right
blocks.zh: 只管开始向前走，你会找到一条感觉对的路。

blocks.en: The greatest trait you can acquire is to work with tremendous intensity on things that matter to you, and more importantly, be strangely unbothered when those things don't work out.
blocks.zh: 你能获得的最大特质，是全力以赴地投身于对你重要的事情，更重要的是，当这些事情没有成功时，能出奇地不为所动。

blocks.en: If you want a rare life, you have to be delusional. Doubt can enter your mind, and it can sound reasonable, but if you entertain it too much it will slowly drag you down into stagnation. I'd rather reap the lesson from massive failure than do nothing because it's not "realistic."
blocks.zh: 如果你想拥有非凡的人生，就必须有点妄想。怀疑会闯入你的脑海，听起来还挺合理，但如果你任由它滋生，它会慢慢把你拖入停滞的泥潭。我宁愿从巨大的失败中吸取教训，也不愿因为“不现实”而无所作为。

blocks.en: At some point, usually in your 20s, you'll notice that the people around you stop believing in themselves. And no matter how hard you try, you can't save them. By all means, do not let it infect your mind. Stay on your path.
blocks.zh: 在某个时刻，通常是在你20多岁的时候，你会注意到周围的人开始不再相信自己。无论你多么努力，你也救不了他们。无论如何，千万别让这种情绪感染你的头脑。坚守你的道路。

blocks.en: You need to read more, and you need to consume less. You need to set aside time to do a workout for the mind, and you need to give it time to recover. Especially now that it's so easy for your cognitive capacity to atrophy. Refuse to become mentally obese.
blocks.zh: 你需要多阅读，少摄入信息。你需要留出时间进行思维锻炼，也需要给它恢复的时间。尤其是现在，认知能力是如此容易萎缩。拒绝成为精神上的肥胖者。

blocks.en: If you want to achieve anything great, it needs to become your one true priority. The only thing on your mind. Nobody accidentally got rich from business. Nobody accidentally built a great physique. They were obsessed with it for multiple years until it became their default.
blocks.zh: 如果你想成就任何伟大的事业，它必须成为你唯一的真正优先事项。你脑中唯一想的事。没有人是偶然在商业上发财的。没有人是偶然练出好身材的。他们痴迷于此多年，直到它成为他们的默认状态。

blocks.en: A pattern I've noticed in stuck people:
blocks.zh: 我在困顿的人身上注意到一个模式：

blocks.en: They're always busy. They never stop moving. They have 47 tabs open and a notebook-sized to-do list. But if you ask them what they accomplished this week that actually matters, their mind goes blank.
blocks.zh: 他们总是很忙。他们从不停下脚步。他们有47个打开的标签页和一本笔记本大小的待办事项清单。但如果你问他们这周真正完成了什么重要的事情，他们的大脑会一片空白。

blocks.en: Busyness isn't a badge of honor.
blocks.zh: 忙碌不是荣誉勋章。

blocks.en: If you're a writer, be okay with repeating what's already been said, because most ideas have already been exhausted, and genuinely novel ideas are rare.
blocks.zh: 如果你是一名作家，要能接受重复别人已经说过的话，因为大多数想法都已经被穷尽了，真正新颖的想法很罕见。

blocks.en: Nobody follows you because you're talking about something new. They follow you because they want to read your point of view.
blocks.zh: 没有人关注你是因为你在谈论新东西。他们关注你是因为他们想读你的观点。

blocks.en: You as a single person have more power today than a 20 person company of the past. That's insane. The internet gave you the ability to learn anything. Social media gave you the leverage to reach anyone. AI is giving you the ability to create almost anything. Please don't waste it
blocks.zh: 今天的你作为一个人，比过去一个20人的公司拥有更大的力量。这太疯狂了。互联网给了你学习任何东西的能力。社交媒体给了你触达任何人的杠杆。人工智能正在赋予你创造几乎任何东西的能力。请不要浪费它。

blocks.en: You need to write more.
blocks.zh: 你需要多写。

blocks.en: Without AI. Without templates. Without knowing what you're writing about. Just you, an idea, and enough time to do the difficult cognitive work necessary to reach true understanding. If you don't, your ability to think will drastically decline.
blocks.zh: 不用AI。不用模板。不用知道你在写什么。只有你、一个想法，以及足够的时间去做必要的艰难认知工作以达成真正的理解。如果你不这么做，你的思考能力将急剧下降。

blocks.en: The more "informed" you feel, the less capable of thinking you become.
blocks.zh: 你越觉得自己“见多识广”，你的思考能力就越弱。

blocks.en: You can learn anything in 2 weeks.
blocks.zh: 你可以在两周内学会任何东西。

blocks.en: You can't master it, obviously, but if you obsess over it, you can become better at it than most people ever will. You'd be surprised how fast your life can change when you understand this.
blocks.zh: 当然，你无法精通它，但如果你痴迷于此，你可以比大多数人做得更好。当你明白这一点时，你会惊讶于你的生活能多快改变。

blocks.en: It seems like everyone is obsessed with productivity and efficiency yet rarely get anything meaningful done. I'm convinced your best work is done when you're not working. When you have space for creative ideas to emerge that drastically change the trajectory of your life/work.
blocks.zh: 似乎每个人都痴迷于生产力和效率，却很少完成任何有意义的事情。我确信你最好的工作是在你不工作的时候完成的。当你有空间让创造性的想法出现，从而大幅改变你的生活/工作的轨迹时。

blocks.en: Habits so simple you think they’re not worth doing, but have a profound impact on your life:
blocks.zh: 习惯如此简单，以至于你认为不值得做，但却对你的生活产生深远影响：

blocks.en:
- Not touching your phone when you wake up
- Not thinking about work after work is done
- Putting a book down once you find an idea worth thinking about
- Setting aside time to do nothing for 10 minutes a day
- Going on a short walk after each meal
- Eating a meal without a screen in front of you
- Saying "I don't know" instead of pretending you do
- Asking "What if this isn't actually a problem?" before trying to solve it
- Letting yourself be bad at something instead of expecting perfection
- Trying to understand something you disagree with instead of looking for flaws
- Defaulting to "no" until you think through the commitment
blocks.zh:
- 醒来时不碰手机
- 工作完成后不想工作
- 一旦发现一个值得思考的想法就放下书
- 每天留出10分钟什么都不做
- 每餐后短暂散步
- 吃饭时不看屏幕
- 说“我不知道”而不是假装知道
- 在试图解决问题之前问“如果这实际上不是问题呢？”
- 让自己在某事上做得不好，而不是期望完美
- 试图理解你不同意的事情，而不是寻找缺陷
- 默认说“不”，直到你考虑清楚承诺

blocks.en: "I'm not a creative person."
blocks.zh: “我不是一个有创造力的人。”

blocks.en: No, you are, everyone is, but your mind is just clogged by all of the podcasts and social media you ram into it without properly digesting it. You're conditioned to believe you can only take a certain path in life, and you don't daydream or entertain stupid ideas that could set you on an entirely new trajectory. You're so obsessed with being productive and efficient that you feel like you're always falling behind, and that stress prevents you from thinking outside the box.
blocks.zh: 不，你是的，每个人都是，只是你的头脑被你塞进去的播客和社交媒体堵住了，没有好好消化。你被训练成相信人生只能走某条特定的路，你不去白日做梦，也不去琢磨那些可能把你带上全新轨道的傻点子。你太执着于高效和多产，以至于总觉得自己在落后，而这种压力让你无法跳出框框思考。

blocks.en: You need to slow the fuck down, allow yourself to be bored (actually bored, not so overstimulated that you find enjoyable things boring), and pursue a life that you design, not one that was assigned to you.
blocks.zh: 你需要慢下来，允许自己无聊（真正地无聊，而不是过度刺激到觉得有趣的事都无聊），去追求一种由你设计的人生，而不是被分配的人生。

blocks.en: Copy-pasting into one chat box sucks.
blocks.zh: 复制粘贴到一个聊天框里太糟糕了。

blocks.en: So we built a canvas for LLMs, content, and research.
blocks.zh: 所以我们为LLM、内容和研究构建了一个画布。

blocks.en: Create markdown docs, paste social links, upload files, and connect to AI chats.
blocks.zh: 创建Markdown文档，粘贴社交链接，上传文件，并连接AI聊天。

blocks.en: Agents can handle busy work, but creative work needs a visual space to connect ideas.
blocks.zh: 智能体可以处理繁忙的工作，但创造性工作需要视觉空间来连接想法。

blocks.en: The single most important thing you can do in today's world is to stop operating from the old paradigm. If you need to be told what to do next (go to school, get a job, retire at 65) the outcome of your life will always be in someone else's hands. You must learn how to direct your own work. You must learn how to tolerate and mitigate risk and uncertainty. You must figure out what you want and teach yourself everything necessary to get it. It's extremely difficult, but not as difficult as the silent suffering people learn to accept as "normal."
blocks.zh: 当今世界上你能做的最重要的一件事，就是停止按照旧范式运作。如果你需要别人告诉你下一步该做什么（上学、找工作、65岁退休），你人生的结果就永远掌握在别人手里。你必须学会如何指导自己的工作。你必须学会如何容忍和缓解风险与不确定性。你必须弄清楚你想要什么，并自学一切必要的东西去得到它。这极其困难，但不像人们学会接受的“正常”那种无声的痛苦那么难。

blocks.en: It doesn't matter if it takes years.
blocks.zh: 就算花上几年时间也无所谓。

blocks.en: What the fuck else are you going to do?
blocks.zh: 不然你还能他妈干点啥？

blocks.en: You aren't going to learn, create, experiment, grow, and everything that makes life enjoyable because you have something better to be doing?
blocks.zh: 难道因为有更值得做的事，你就不去学习、创造、尝试、成长，以及享受生活中所有让人愉悦的事情了？

blocks.en: Your mind is playing tricks on you.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑在骗你。

blocks.en: The minute I become too frugal or money-conscious is the moment it starts to control me and becomes difficult to make. When I spend almost carelessly, it seems to find its way back. Money-induced stress narrows the mind and new opportunities become invisible.
blocks.zh: 一旦我变得过于节俭或太在意钱，钱就开始控制我，而且赚钱也变得困难。当我几乎是不假思索地花钱时，钱似乎自己会找回来。金钱带来的压力会窄化思维，新的机会就变得视而不见了。

blocks.en: The problem is that you don't know what you want to do, and figuring out what you want to do requires learning, experimentation, and effort - so you do nothing.
blocks.zh: 问题在于，你不知道自己想做什么，而搞清楚你想做什么需要学习、尝试和努力——所以你干脆什么都不做。

blocks.en: Polymaths will dominate the next 5 years, but only if they practice the skill of knowing what to ignore. You can learn and do anything now, meaning that it will become increasingly rare for a person to put time, attention, and care into one thing.
blocks.zh: 通才会在未来五年主导世界，但前提是他们要练就一项技能：知道该忽略什么。现在你可以学习并做成任何事，这意味着一个人把时间、注意力和心思专注于一件事上会变得越来越少见。

blocks.en: The secret is to have something you're excited to do when you wake up. It takes a few months of learning, failure, and experimentation to find what that thing is, but once you do, everything is just... better.
blocks.zh: 秘诀在于，你醒来时有兴奋的事情可做。这需要几个月的学习、失败和实验才能找到那件事，但一旦找到，一切就……更好了。

blocks.en: Focus is becoming the rarest skill on the planet. Talent, intelligence, marketing, prompting, vibe coding, and whatever else doesn't matter as much as being able to channel your attention for an extended period of time into one useful thing that you want to see in the world.
blocks.zh: 专注正成为地球上最稀有的技能。才华、智慧、营销、提示工程、氛围编程以及其他任何东西，都不如能够将你的注意力长时间集中在你想在世界上看到的一件有用的事情上那么重要。

blocks.en: Self-improvement is a gateway drug into entrepreneurship because you start seeing life as a system you can optimize. You start to believe that if you don't like something about your life, you can change it. And since the source of most people's problems is money, you stop waiting for a raise and start building something.
blocks.zh: 自我提升是创业的入门毒品，因为你开始将生活视为一个可以优化的系统。你开始相信，如果你不喜欢生活中的某些方面，你可以改变它。而且，由于大多数人的问题根源是金钱，你不再等待加薪，而是开始构建一些东西。

blocks.en: The ultimate goal is getting paid to be yourself. To solve problems you can't help but solve. To study what you can't pull yourself away from. To eliminate any work that does not challenge you creatively.
blocks.zh: 最终目标是做自己并获得报酬。解决你忍不住要解决的问题。研究你无法自拔的东西。消除任何不能创造性挑战你的工作。

blocks.en: The easiest way to get ahead is to commit to a period of skill development. 6-12 months. Pure focus for 2-4 hours a day. Learning and building. Not just binge watching tutorials, but creating quality projects that you, others, or businesses could actually benefit from. But don't just let those projects sit around. Tell the world about them. See if people care enough to pay you. Fix what doesn't work until they do. That's it. That's what most people need to completely turn their life around.
blocks.zh: 出人头地最容易的方法，就是投入一段时间专注发展一项技能。6到12个月，每天纯粹专注2到4小时，学习和实践。不是光刷教程，而是打造出高质量的项目，让你自己、他人或企业能真正从中受益。但别让这些项目闲置。向世界展示它们。看看人们是否愿意为此付费。修复那些行不通的地方，直到他们愿意买单。就这么简单。这就是大多数人彻底扭转人生所需要做的。

blocks.en: Grab a notebook.
blocks.zh: 拿一个笔记本。

blocks.en: Write out exactly what you want in your future, don't miss a detail. Then, break it down into goals. Decades, years, months, weeks, and days.
blocks.zh: 把你未来想要的东西，原原本本地写下来，一个细节都别落下。然后，把它拆解成目标：以十年、一年、一个月、一周和一天为单位。

blocks.en: Every day, write down the 3 levers you can pull to make actual progress.
blocks.zh: 每天写下你能拉动的3个杠杆，来取得实质性的进展。

blocks.en: Then, forget about the goals and execute.
blocks.zh: 然后，忘掉目标，只管去做。

blocks.en: The best thing you can do in today's world is practice thinking. Very few people, especially smart people, do this. Snap yourself out of your automatic patterns and stretch your mind for once. This will only become more important as AI and social media distort reality.
blocks.zh: 在当今世界，你能做的最好的事就是练习思考。极少有人这么做，尤其是聪明人。挣脱你的自动模式，让自己的大脑舒展一次。随着AI和社交媒体扭曲现实，这件事只会越来越重要。

blocks.en: That said good luck everyone may the odds be ever in your favor
blocks.zh: 话虽如此，祝大家好运，愿机遇永远眷顾你们。

blocks.en: $1 million dollar prizes aside, I think there's been a quiet hunger for articles. The pendulum swung too far in the direction of TikTok and endless scrolling and the internet has a chance to self-correct.
blocks.zh: 撇开百万美元奖金不谈，我觉得人们心底一直对文章有一种暗暗的渴望。钟摆已经朝 TikTok 和无尽刷屏的方向摆得太远了，互联网有机会自我纠偏。

blocks.en: I don't think the human brain was meant to be ripped in a thousand different directions as soon as you get on your phone. Too much chaos that has downstream affects on the quality of everyday life.
blocks.zh: 我不认为人类的大脑天生就该在打开手机的一瞬间被撕扯成一千个方向。混乱太多，会层层波及日常生活的质量。

blocks.en: Long form content allows you to focus on set of ideas. It brings order to the mind. You learn more, you feel better, and usually you're left with something you can actually apply to your life, even if it's just a better way of thinking.
blocks.zh: 长文内容让你能聚焦于一组思想。它让心智归于秩序。你学到更多，感觉更好，而且通常还能留下一些真正能用到生活里的东西，哪怕只是换个更好的思考方式。

blocks.en: Especially with AI, we've gotten to the point where we think we want things as short as possible. We have this deranged desire to "get to the point" when the point is to sit with it. You can collect all of the tips and tricks you want but you're completely missing the context that allows you to turn those tips into results. A bullet list of actionable steps will do absolutely nothing for you.
blocks.zh: 尤其在 AI 时代，我们已经走到了这样一个地步：总以为东西越短越好。我们有一种近乎病态的执念，非要“直击要点”，可真正的要点恰恰在于静下心来与之相处。你可以把想要的技巧和窍门都收集个遍，却完全缺失了让这些技巧转化为成果的语境。一份可执行步骤的要点清单，对你毫无用处。

blocks.en: Pre-2015 books are the best option, but articles are a great step in what I think is the right direction.
blocks.zh: 2015 年之前出版的书是最佳选择，不过文章也是很好的一步，我认为方向是对的。

blocks.en: The primary reason people don't achieve big goals is because they don't realize that the only source of truth is making mistakes. They soak up advice and theory, expecting it to be an exact match to their mind, experience, and situation just to fail once and give up completely.
blocks.zh: 人们无法实现宏大目标的主要原因，是他们没有意识到：唯一可靠的真理来源就是犯错。他们大量吸收建议和理论，期望这些能完全匹配自己的思维、经验和处境，结果一旦失败一次，就彻底放弃。

blocks.en: You don't magically become focused. You practice it. You notice you're distracted and snap out of it, over and over again until it's second nature. Most people have not trained this muscle, and they are not anywhere close to as focused as they think they are.
blocks.zh: 专注力不会凭空而来。你得去练习。你注意到自己分心了，就把注意力拉回来，一遍又一遍，直到它成为你的第二天性。大多数人从未锻炼过这块肌肉，他们远没有自己以为的那么专注。

blocks.en: be harder on yourself
blocks.zh: 对自己更狠一点

blocks.en: Your life is determined by the amount of uncertainty you're willing to embrace.
blocks.zh: 你的人生，取决于你愿意拥抱多少不确定性。

blocks.en: If you don't shamelessly promote your work, every day for the next 2-3 years, you will get stuck doing someone else's work until you realize that nobody is going to pay you if they have no idea who you are.
blocks.zh: 如果你不坚持每天推广自己的作品，接下来两三年里，你就会一直卡在替别人打工的位置上，直到你意识到：如果别人根本不知道你是谁，就没人会付钱给你。

blocks.en: The deeper you fall into a rut the more fuel you have to launch out of it, but also the more excuses you have to stay the same. It is very important that you see through your own bullshit and choose the first option.
blocks.zh: 你陷进车辙越深，弹射出去所需的燃料就越多，但同时留在原地不动的借口也越多。看清自己的那套鬼话、选择第一条路，这非常重要。

blocks.en: The greatest focus hack is to know what you're working on, why you're working on it, when it needs to be done, and how exactly to get it done.
blocks.zh: 最强大的专注秘诀，就是清楚自己在做什么、为什么做、什么时候必须完成，以及具体该怎么做完。

blocks.en: If you work so that you never have to work again, you'll be disappointed when retirement leaves you feeling empty.
blocks.zh: 如果你拼命工作只是为了有朝一日再也不用工作，那么当退休让你感到空虚时，你会失望的。

blocks.en: Find work that you would do after retirement as early as you can and you'll never feel the need to retire.
blocks.zh: 尽早找到那种你退休后也愿意做的工作，你就永远不会觉得有必要退休。

blocks.en: Don't try to learn the "best new skills."
blocks.zh: 别去学什么“最热门的新技能”。

blocks.en: Build your own thing. Try to sell it. Fail over and over again. Learn what it means to adapt and iterate. Remove your dependency from others and hunt for your own survival.
blocks.zh: 做你自己的东西。试着把它卖出去。一次又一次地失败。去体会什么叫适应和迭代。摆脱对他人的依赖，为自己的生存去狩猎。

blocks.en: You will learn the exact skills you need, and you will learn them better than anyone else.
blocks.zh: 你会学到你恰好需要的那些技能，而且你会比别人学得更好。

blocks.en: As someone who was against AI for a long time, AI is a skill just like any other, and the usefulness of AI increases as you get better at it.
blocks.zh: 作为一个长期反对AI的人，我认为AI和其他任何技能一样，你对它越熟练，它就越有用。

blocks.en: The first time you play a guitar, you literally can't do anything. You sound like shit. But you slowly get better. You can play more songs. You enjoy it so much more.
blocks.zh: 你第一次弹吉他时，真的什么都弹不了。你听起来糟透了。但你会慢慢进步。你能弹更多曲子。你也享受得多得多。

blocks.en: We were made to think that AI would just solve all our problems and do everything for us, so people were disappointed when it didn't do those things, but if you actually try to learn it, then you will see how helpful it can be. That sounds like a cop out, but it's silly to think that AI is just going to solve all your problems out of the box. If you don't use it for an extended period of time then (as with every other skill) you will not be able to get the best results with it.
blocks.zh: 我们被灌输了这样一种观念：AI会解决我们所有的问题，替我们包办一切。所以当它没能做到这些时，人们便大失所望。但如果你真的去学习使用它，就会发现它有多有用。这听起来像是在找借口，但认为AI能直接解决你所有问题，这种想法本身就很愚蠢。如果你不长期使用它（就像其他任何技能一样），你就无法用它获得最佳结果。

blocks.en: It won't remove all of your work, or any of it for that matter if you don't want it to (I've been spending more time working, because it's fun), but it will give you a deeper, more enjoyable way of doing what you already do. You abstract out a layer from physical labor to mental labor. You spend more time in the realm of ideas and taste. It starts to feel more like a game or puzzle than it does "work."
blocks.zh: 它不会消除你所有的工作，甚至如果你不想的话，一点都不会减少（我花在工作上的时间反而更多了，因为觉得有趣），但它会给你一种更深入、更愉悦的方式去做你已经在做的事。你把一层体力劳动抽象成了脑力劳动。你更多时间花在理念和品味的领域。它开始感觉更像游戏或解谜，而不是“工作”。

blocks.en: You have to be okay with moving from doing the manual grunt work of writing lines of code or prose to discerning whether or not it sounds like you want it to sound. I don't think anyone, aside from other writers who haven't detached from the labor, would argue that hiring a ghostwriter (i.e. James Patterson) is cheating. The end readers still love it. He is still in control of the plot, vision, and what actually gets published. Nobody would argue that the director of a film doesn't deserve praise because he is not manually filming it or building the set.
blocks.zh: 你必须接受从手动编写代码或文字的苦力活，转变为判断它听起来是否是你想要的效果。我认为，除了那些尚未脱离苦力的作家，没有人会认为雇佣代笔人（比如詹姆斯·帕特森）是作弊。最终读者仍然喜欢。他仍然掌控着情节、愿景和实际出版的内容。没有人会认为电影导演不值得称赞，因为他没有亲自拍摄或搭建布景。

blocks.en: There is going to be, and there already is, so much pushback on AI for valid reasons, but most of those reasons are psychological defense mechanisms tying you to how you've identified yourself with how you work.
blocks.zh: 对AI的反击将会很多，而且已经有很多，其中一些理由合理，但大多数理由都是心理防御机制，把你束缚在通过工作方式定义自我的旧身份上。

blocks.en: AI doesn't have to be a religion. You don't have to use it for everything. But I don't think it's a wise idea to willingly choose a side that is going to lose.
blocks.zh: AI不必成为一种宗教。你不必事事都用它。但我认为，主动选择注定失败的一方，并非明智之举。

blocks.en: If you want to avoid being replaced, stop worrying about which skills will be relevant 20 years from now.
blocks.zh: 如果你想避免被取代，就别再担心20年后哪些技能还有用。

blocks.en: Nobody has a single clue what those are going to be. The world is changing so rapidly that you can’t even imagine what skills will be valuable in the future.
blocks.zh: 没人知道那些技能会是什么。世界变化太快，你甚至无法想象未来哪些技能有价值。

blocks.en: Instead, you need to learn how to learn fast, because if you can become effective at any skill quicker than other people, it doesn’t matter what skill you learn.
blocks.zh: 相反，你需要学会如何快速学习，因为如果你能比其他人更快地掌握任何技能，那么你学什么技能都无所谓。

blocks.en: But that isn’t something you just sit down and study. You must step into the arena. You must learn by doing. You must build your own thing. Your own project. Your own product. Then you must share it with others to determine whether it’s valuable or not.
blocks.zh: 但这并不是你坐下来学习就能做到的。你必须踏入竞技场。你必须边做边学。你必须打造自己的东西。你自己的项目。你自己的产品。然后你必须与他人分享，以确定它是否有价值。

blocks.en: Why? Because that forces you to learn efficiently. Everything you learn is directly applied to a meaningful project that allows you to not be dependent on an employer that requires you to learn a single skill that they will replace as soon as they can.
blocks.zh: 为什么？因为这迫使你高效学习。你学到的一切都直接应用到一个有意义的项目中，让你不必依赖雇主，而雇主只要求你学习单一技能，一旦可以就会把你替换掉。

blocks.en: You don't achieve the life you want then become the "successful" person. You become the person first, which looks cringe until it becomes normal, and success eventually catches up to you. You choose the character you want to play, and only then do the right quests appear.
blocks.zh: 你不是先实现想要的生活，然后成为“成功”的人。你先成为那个人，这看起来可能很尴尬，直到它变得正常，成功最终会追上你。你选择想要扮演的角色，然后正确的任务才会出现。

blocks.en: You easily quit your goals because there's nothing on the line. You don't have a vision for a better life that is so clear that your current life feels like losing if you don't reach it. Secretly most people don't actually want to achieve their goals. They want to impress others and get a dopamine hit from telling them their goals.
blocks.zh: 你轻易放弃目标，因为没什么可失去的。你没有对更好生活的清晰愿景，清晰到如果不实现，当前生活就像失败。私下里，大多数人其实并不想实现目标。他们想给别人留下印象，并从告诉别人目标中获得多巴胺的快感。

blocks.en: The fastest way to change is to obsessively reflect on what you do every day and do not lie to yourself about what kind of life that is creating.
blocks.zh: 改变的最快方式是执着地反思你每天所做的事，并且不要自欺欺人地忽视那正在创造什么样的生活。

blocks.en: Your life flips upside down when you realize that "who you are" is a program written by people who were also programmed, and unless you make the painful choice to rewrite that code, most of your thoughts and actions are not beneficial to your future, because they are not yours.
blocks.zh: 当你意识到“你是谁”是由同样被编程的人编写的一个程序时，你的生活就会天翻地覆。除非你做出痛苦的选择去重写那段代码，否则你的大部分思想和行为对你的未来无益，因为它们不属于你。

blocks.en: You aren't where you want to be because you don't have the mind of the person who would be in that position. You're exactly where you should be for your level of development, and changing that is within your control.
blocks.zh: 你不在你想去的位置，是因为你没有那个位置的人应有的思维。你正处于你发展水平所应处的位置，而改变这一点在你的掌控之中。

blocks.en:
This goes deeper than you think:
youtu.be/K8K09g9XR4s
blocks.zh:
这比你想象的更深刻：
youtu.be/K8K09g9XR4s

blocks.en: We're going through one of those historical shifts where there are 3 types of people:
blocks.zh: 我们正在经历一次历史性转变，其中有三类人：

blocks.en: 1) People who cry and become violent about the fact that they can't "do what they've been doing" for the rest of their lives without getting left behind (avoid these people)
blocks.zh: 1) 那些人整天哭天抢地、甚至诉诸暴力，只因为他们没法在余生里继续"做自己一直在做的事"而不被淘汰（离这些人远点）

blocks.en: 2) People who do nothing until they are forced to because they have to survive, but the penalty for starting late is so severe because everyone else is exponentially further ahead of them
blocks.zh: 2) 那些人什么都不做，直到为了生存被迫行动，但起步太晚的代价极其惨重，因为其他人早已遥遥领先，差距呈指数级拉大

blocks.en: 3) People who stay curious, experiment, build, and figure out how to adopt the new way of doing things in a way thats useful (without attaching to the way things were done in the past)
blocks.zh: 3) 那些人保持好奇、不断试错、动手构建，想办法以有用的方式接纳新的做事方法（而不执着于过去的老路子）

blocks.en: It has always been important that you choose option 3, but now is as good a time as ever.
blocks.zh: 选择第三条路一直都很重要，而现在正是最好的时机。

blocks.en: Do everything in your power to never become helpless. It's a dangerous and lonely hole. Helpful people will stay as far away from you as they can because they know that you will not do anything with their help. Do not complain without being open to a solution. Do not complain if you know that you are going to do absolutely nothing to change. Do not expect anyone to give you anything. Nobody cares how bad your situation is if you clearly show that you do not want to escape it.
blocks.zh: 竭尽全力，别让自己沦为无助之人。那是一个危险而孤独的深坑。愿意帮你的人会尽可能离你远远的，因为他们知道，你的帮助给了也白给。不要一边抱怨一边拒绝解决方案。如果你明知自己什么都不会去改变，那就别抱怨。别指望任何人白给你什么。如果你明摆着不想逃离困境，那就没人会在乎你的处境有多糟。

blocks.en: You aren't where you want to be because you don't want to be there more than you want to be where you are. Your behavior is your confession. You say you want a better life (mostly for social approval), but when something more instant and pleasurable comes around, your actions show that you want that more.
blocks.zh: 你没到达想去的地方，是因为你想去那里的渴望，还比不上你想留在原地的渴望。你的行为就是你的自白。你说你想要更好的生活（多半是为了社交上的认可），可一旦有更即时、更令人愉悦的东西出现，你的行动就暴露了：你更想要那个。

blocks.en: Your best ideas will never come from trying to have them.
blocks.zh: 你最好的点子，永远不会来自"硬想"。

blocks.en: You must let the creative process play out automatically. You must read more, do more, experience more. Then you must give yourself time to do nothing because that's when your mind will put all the pieces together and shoot out an idea that may change everything.
blocks.zh: 你必须让创造过程自动展开。你必须多读、多做、多体验。然后，你必须给自己留出什么都不做的时间——因为正是在那时，你的大脑会把所有碎片拼到一起，迸出一个可能改变一切的点子。

blocks.en: When everyone has an advantage, it is no longer an advantage.
blocks.zh: 当人人都有优势时，优势就不再是优势。

blocks.en: When everyone can learn and create anything at the click of a button, your advantage comes from slowing down, focusing on your craft, doing the right things manually, and acquiring knowledge that is so specific to you that nobody can generate it with AI.
blocks.zh: 当每个人点一下按钮就能学会并创造任何东西时，你的优势来自放慢脚步、专注手艺、亲手做对的事，以及获取那些高度个人化、没人能用AI生成的知识。

blocks.en: Signs you're on the right track:
blocks.zh: 你走在正确轨道上的迹象：

blocks.en:
Work energizes you
Learning doesn't take effort
Discipline doesn't need to be forced
You think in decades, not days
You're excited to wake up
blocks.zh:
工作让你充满能量
学习不觉得费力
自律无需强逼
你以十年为单位思考，而非以天
你兴奋地醒来

blocks.en: You relate to very few people, but the relationships you do form are irreplaceable.
blocks.zh: 能与你产生共鸣的人寥寥无几，但你真正建立起来的关系无可替代。

blocks.en: When your days become too mundane, you need to change something fast. You need chaos. You need novelty. You need the experiences and ideas that inspire you to go on your next quest. Build something new. Rip apart your daily routine. Do anything but the same thing.
blocks.zh: 当你的日子变得太过平淡，你需要迅速做出改变。你需要混乱。你需要新鲜感。你需要能激励你踏上下一段探索的经历和想法。去构建新东西。打碎你的日常惯例。做什么都行，就是别再重复老一套。

blocks.en: If you aren't building something that leads to the life you want, even if it's "only" 30-60 minutes a day, you will by default stay in the same life you're in, building things that allow others to live the life they want. 30 minutes can, in fact, start the snowball.
blocks.zh: 如果你没有在构建通往理想生活的东西——哪怕"仅仅"每天30到60分钟——那你默认就会停留在现在的生活里，为别人构建让他们过上理想生活的东西。事实上，30分钟就足以让雪球滚起来。

blocks.en: If you're bored, create something.
blocks.zh: 如果你觉得无聊，就去创造点什么。

blocks.en: Anything.
blocks.zh: 任何东西。

blocks.en: Software. Designs. Photos. Videos. Writing. A business. A body. A relationship. A mind.
blocks.zh: 软件。设计。照片。视频。写作。一项事业。一副身体。一段关系。一个心智。

blocks.en: How can you not be excited to wake up when you have the ability to create.
blocks.zh: 当你拥有创造力时，你怎么能不为醒来而兴奋呢？

blocks.en: You can train your mind to achieve anything you want. Most of what you don't have is no more than a lack of skill, knowledge, action, and the logical sequence of steps it takes to achieve that thing. Deep down, everyone knows this, but their mind was trained by someone else to believe their potential is limited.
blocks.zh: 你可以训练你的心智去实现任何你想要的东西。你所没有的大部分东西，不过是缺乏技能、知识、行动，以及实现那个东西所需的逻辑步骤顺序。内心深处，每个人都知道这一点，但他们的心智被其他人训练成相信自己的潜力是有限的。

blocks.en: Chat interfaces suck.
blocks.zh: 聊天界面糟透了。

blocks.en: And you need to copy paste between 10 tabs to do anything worthwhile.
blocks.zh: 而且你需要复制粘贴到10个标签页之间才能做任何有价值的事情。

blocks.en: So we created a canvas for notes, files, YouTube videos, and chats that can branch off of each other.
blocks.zh: 所以我们创建了一个画布，用于笔记、文件、YouTube视频和聊天，这些都可以相互分支。

blocks.en: Eden is only open to the public through black friday weekend.
blocks.zh: Eden仅在黑色星期五周末对公众开放。

blocks.en: Subtle reminder that you're supposed to feel overwhelmed.
blocks.zh: 微妙地提醒你，你本应感到不知所措。

blocks.en: It means you're doing something new. You're taking a new path. You're learning. You're growing. You branched into the unknown, and that's admirable.
blocks.zh: 这意味着你正在做一些新的事情。你正在走一条新的路。你正在学习。你正在成长。你分支进入了未知领域，这值得钦佩。

blocks.en: Self-discipline isn't difficult, you're just distracted.
blocks.zh: 自律并不难，你只是分心了。

blocks.en: The mind craves order. That’s why you feel out of control. Your attention is not focused on a singular vision for the future so potent that distractions can’t penetrate it. Feel deep into your situation. Realize where your life will end up if you keep going down this path. Become absolutely fed up with the lack of progress you are making. Use that negative energy to slingshot toward a meaningful goal you’ve been putting off. I know you can hear that voice that keeps nagging at you saying, you were meant for more than this. Discipline comes from clarity, not force. Discipline is a feature of identity. You aren’t disciplined because you aren’t the type of person who seamlessly does what they need to do. It isn’t difficult for a writer to sit down and write. It isn’t difficult for a bodybuilder to eat healthy. In fact, it’s difficult for them not to eat healthy. They hate it. They do it because that’s who they are. They don’t have options. They deeply understand the impact of being distracted from their goal. Success is automatic. If you want to be disciplined, stop trying to be. Instead, remove every single distraction that prevents you from being disciplined. Give yourself one option. Shut your mind off and execute.
blocks.zh: 心智渴望秩序。这就是为什么你感到失控。你的注意力没有聚焦在一个单一的、如此强大的未来愿景上，以至于分心无法穿透它。深入感受你的处境。意识到如果你继续沿着这条路走下去，你的生活最终会变成什么样。对你自己缺乏进展的状态彻底受够了。利用这种负能量弹射向一个你一直推迟的有意义的目标。我知道你能听到那个不断唠叨你的声音说，你注定不止于此。自律来自清晰，而不是强迫。自律是身份的一个特征。你不自律，因为你不是那种无缝地做他们需要做的事情的人。对作家来说，坐下来写作并不难。对健美运动员来说，健康饮食并不难。事实上，对他们来说，不健康饮食才难。他们讨厌它。他们这样做是因为那就是他们。他们没有选择。他们深刻理解分心于目标的影响。成功是自动的。如果你想自律，不要再试图自律。相反，移除每一个阻止你自律的分心事物。给自己一个选择。关闭你的心智并执行。

blocks.en: You can't improve what doesn't exist.
blocks.zh: 你无法改进不存在的东西。

blocks.en: The ideas in your head. The business you dream of building. The plans you keep putting off. All are worthless until you test them against reality.
blocks.zh: 你头脑中的想法。你梦想建立的事业。你一直推迟的计划。在现实面前测试之前，所有这些都是无价值的。

blocks.en: You're afraid of failure and glorify perfection when the opposite is what determines success.
blocks.zh: 你害怕失败并美化完美，而恰恰相反才是决定成功的因素。

blocks.en: Why the 40 hour workweek is a joke:
blocks.zh: 为什么每周40小时工作制是个笑话：

blocks.en: youtu.be/mA0P-5_QvH8
blocks.zh: youtu.be/mA0P-5_QvH8

blocks.en: You only need 1 hour.
blocks.zh: 你只需要1小时。

blocks.en: 1 hour of building. 1 hour of writing. 1 hour of lifting. 1 hour of studying. 1 hour of anything but distracting yourself from the life you are trying to change.
blocks.zh: 1小时构建。1小时写作。1小时举重。1小时学习。1小时做任何事情，而不是让自己分心于你试图改变的生活。

blocks.en: 1 hour feels like nothing until you look back 365 hours later and everything's changed.
blocks.zh: 一小时感觉不算什么，直到365小时后回望，一切已悄然改变。

blocks.en: If you don't have something important to care about, you will naturally care about things that make you stupid, angry, and depressed.
blocks.zh: 如果你没有重要的事去关心，你自然会去关心那些让你变得愚蠢、愤怒和沮丧的事。

blocks.en: Most people's lives are determined by how they choose to cure their boredom.
blocks.zh: 大多数人的生活，取决于他们选择如何打发无聊。

blocks.en: If you understood that you become what you read, watch, listen to, or the people you surround yourself with, you wouldn't be doing 90% of what you do.
blocks.zh: 如果你明白你会成为你所阅读、观看、倾听的内容以及你周围人的样子，你就不会去做你现在90%的事情。

blocks.en: It's pretty simple.
blocks.zh: 道理很简单。

blocks.en: Wake up early. Complete the single highest priority task. Avoid the destination society set for you at birth. Make giant mistakes. Mistakes are the launchpads toward your ideal life. Always be building a project. Youth is the greatest currency, it would be wise to invest it. If you wasted your youth, crying about it isn't going to speed up the process. You're supposed to feel overwhelmed, it means you're learning. Set aside 30 minutes daily for deliberate boredom (to unfuck your dopamine sensitivity). Walk more. Read more. Write more. Writing is how you practice thinking. Thinking is how you make better decisions. The outcome of your life is determined by the sum of your decisions. Force yourself to do something you've never done before, at least once a week. Learn something new. Talk to someone new. Book a one way plane ticket. Move into that place you can't afford. Because you need pressure. Real pressure. Launch yourself into the situation of your future self and see if you have what it takes.
blocks.zh: 早起。完成那件最重要的任务。避开社会为你出生时设定的目的地。犯大错。错误是通往理想生活的跳板。始终在构建一个项目。青春是最宝贵的货币，明智的做法是投资它。如果你浪费了青春，为此哭泣并不会加速进程。你本该感到不知所措，这意味着你在学习。每天留出30分钟刻意无聊（以修复你的多巴胺敏感度）。多走路。多阅读。多写作。写作是练习思考的方式。思考是做出更好决策的方式。你人生的结果由你决策的总和决定。强迫自己每周至少做一次从未做过的事。学点新东西。和新的人交谈。订一张单程机票。搬进你负担不起的地方。因为你需要压力。真正的压力。把自己投入到未来自我的情境中，看看你是否有能力应对。

blocks.en: The glaring problem with schools is that a topic could take 1 week to learn, but it’s stretched across 3-4 months because that’s how long the course must be. Even worse, the learning doesn’t involve doing, so most people don’t learn a thing until they graduate.
blocks.zh: 学校最明显的问题是，一个主题可能一周就能学会，却被拉长到三四个月，因为课程必须持续那么久。更糟的是，学习不涉及实践，所以大多数人直到毕业也没学到什么。

blocks.en: You don't need to focus harder. Focus is the byproduct of a lack of distractions. You simply need to be in the right environment (mentally and physically) and have a clear set of tasks that you have the knowledge and skill to execute. Ignore everything but that.
blocks.zh: 你不需要更努力地专注。专注是减少干扰后的副产品。你只需要处于正确的环境（心理和物理上），并有一套清晰的任务，且你具备执行这些任务的知识和技能。忽略其他一切。

blocks.en: The best way to stand out as a creator, in my eyes, is to take a weird topic you're passionate about and make it palatable to a larger audience. Don't follow the trends, but take the principles of human nature that make the trends work and apply them to your personal interests.
blocks.zh: 在我看来，作为创作者脱颖而出的最佳方式，是拿一个你热衷的古怪话题，让它更容易被更广泛的受众接受。不要追随潮流，而是提取使潮流奏效的人性原则，并将其应用于你的个人兴趣。

blocks.en: I don’t know of a single successful person who doesn’t have the skill of figuring it out. They don’t need to ask how to do something, because they deeply understand that they will have to fail, change direction, fail again, and repeat that process even if someone gave them the exact roadmap.
blocks.zh: 我认识的成功人士中，没有一个不具备解决问题的能力。他们不需要问如何做某事，因为他们深知，即使有人给了他们确切的路线图，他们也必须经历失败、改变方向、再次失败，并重复这个过程。

blocks.en: The worst life is to wake up and have nothing you want to do. The best life is not being able to stop yourself from launching out of bed, working on a project that's important to you, and having so much clarity that stress and worry can't even find their way into your brain.
blocks.zh: 最糟糕的生活是醒来后没有任何想做的事。最好的生活是忍不住从床上跳起来，投身于对你重要的项目，思路如此清晰，以至于压力和忧虑无法进入你的大脑。

blocks.en: Learn how to do it yourself before you let AI do it for you. If you don't, you will not understand why it was done that way, why it got results, or why it didn't. You will become more and more dependent on a tool rather than your own creative ability.
blocks.zh: 在让AI替你做之前，先学会自己怎么做。否则，你不会理解为什么这样做、为什么能出结果、或者为什么不行。你会越来越依赖工具，而不是自己的创造力。

blocks.en: If you struggle to think clearly, or struggle to generate big creative ideas, give yourself permission to fuck off for 3 days. No work. No laptop. Just sit around. Discover what it’s like to feel bored again.
blocks.zh: 如果你难以清晰思考，或难以产生大的创意，允许自己放空三天。不工作。不用笔记本电脑。就坐着。重新发现无聊的感觉。

blocks.en: Have a pen and paper ready.
blocks.zh: 准备好笔和纸。

blocks.en: You don’t need to dream big. You need to imagine a life so depressing that the only option in your mind is to achieve big.
blocks.zh: 你不需要胸怀大志。你需要想象一种如此压抑的生活，以至于你心中唯一的选择就是成就大业。

blocks.en: Rare traits I’ve noticed in people who go on to do great things:
blocks.zh: 我注意到那些后来成就伟大事业的人身上的罕见特质：

blocks.en: 1. They were expected by their parents to enter a specific career, and it felt extremely limiting
blocks.zh: 1. 他们的父母期望他们从事特定职业，而这让他们感到极度受限

blocks.en: 2. They could clearly see that others achieved great things even when the odds were stacked against them, so they rightfully assumed they could too
blocks.zh: 2. 他们能清楚地看到别人在逆境中取得了伟大成就，因此他们理所当然地认为自己也能做到

blocks.en: 3. They naturally questioned what was possible, and when teachers, family, or friends couldn’t give them good answers, they took it upon themselves to find them
blocks.zh: 3. 他们天生质疑什么是可能的，当老师、家人或朋友无法给出好的答案时，他们自己去寻找

blocks.en: I love entrepreneurship because it allows you to apply anything you learn.
blocks.zh: 我热爱创业，因为它让你可以应用你学到的任何东西。

blocks.en: At school, you’re told what to learn. At a job, you’re told what to work on, and you only learn until you are good enough to do the job (unless you self-educate out of genuine interest, but being honest, an abysmally low amount of people do that, because those who do realize that in order to learn they must grow, and you can’t grow in someone else’s box).
blocks.zh: 在学校里，别人告诉你该学什么。在职场中，别人告诉你该做什么，而你只需学到足以胜任这份工作为止（除非你出于真正的兴趣去自我教育，但说实话，这么做的人少得可怜，因为那些人明白：想要学习，就必须成长，而在他人的框架里，你无法成长）。

blocks.en: When you do your own thing, the only way to survive is to do something you’ve never done before, which requires you to learn what can’t be taught in school.
blocks.zh: 当你做自己的事时，生存下去的唯一方式就是去做从未做过的事，而这要求你去学那些学校里根本教不了的东西。

blocks.en: How to know if you need to make a big change:
blocks.zh: 如何判断自己是否需要做出重大改变：

blocks.en: You stay up late, every night, because you feel like you haven't gotten enough out of the day.
blocks.zh: 你每晚都熬夜，因为你总觉得这一天没有充分利用。

blocks.en: When you combine the internet (access to opportunity), social media (access to people), and AI (access to intelligence) you give high agency people the ability to achieve more, faster, and low agency people a reason to complain, more.
blocks.zh: 把互联网（获取机会）、社交媒体（获取人脉）和 AI（获取智能）三者结合起来，你就给了高能动性的人更多、更快成事的能力，也给了低能动性的人更多抱怨的理由。

blocks.en: Your potential would substantially increase if you understood that the limits of your perspective are not the limits of what's possible.
blocks.zh: 如果你能明白，你的视角的局限并不等于可能性的局限，你的潜力将大幅提升。

blocks.en: The obvious trap here is mental masturbation. This probably won't work if you aren't already intensely committed to building out your vision for the future.
blocks.zh: 这里显而易见的陷阱，就是精神自慰。如果你尚未全身心投入于构建你对未来的愿景，这大概率不会奏效。

blocks.en: That being said, more work isn't always the answer. You need to unfuck your psychology.
blocks.zh: 话虽如此，多干活并不总是答案。你需要先理清自己的心理。

blocks.en: A pattern I’ve noticed in successful people - that didn’t sacrifice their life for success - is that they physically worked very little, yet people see them as hard workers. Mentally, they were always thinking, plotting, and scheming. They worked in their mind. And once they were clear on their idea, they executed with speed that others couldn’t compete with.
blocks.zh: 我在那些成功者身上注意到一个规律——他们没有为了成功而牺牲生活——他们身体上干的活其实很少，可人们却视他们为勤奋的人。他们的大脑始终在思考、谋划、布局。他们是在头脑里工作。而一旦想法清晰，他们便以无人能及的速度执行。

blocks.en: The best way to learn something is to write about it, in public, but only if you care about learning. When you write, you are forced to organize thoughts into words. When you teach someone else, you feel obligated to understand the topic.
blocks.zh: 学习一件事最好的方式，就是公开地写下来，但前提是你真的在意学习。写作时，你会被迫把思绪整理成文字。当你教导别人时，你会觉得自己有义务弄懂这个主题。

blocks.en: You need to go through an extended period of investing their time into self education and skill acquisition before you can expect any kind of unaverage success. The sooner you stop putting off the 1-3 years of trial and error the better.
blocks.zh: 你需要经历一段相当长的时期，把时间投入到自我教育和技能积累上，之后才可能期待任何非同寻常的成功。你越早停止拖延那 1 到 3 年的试错期，就越好。

blocks.en: One of the greatest feelings is seeing your faith in yourself pay off. To keep experimenting even when nothing has yet gotten results. To see the first bit of effort turn into success. Once you get that taste you can never go back to your old life.
blocks.zh: 最美好的感受之一，就是看到对自己的信念得到回报。在尚未有任何结果时依然坚持试验。看到最初的一点努力变成成功。一旦你尝到这种滋味，就再也回不去过去的生活了。

blocks.en: It’s crazy how you can just learn anything you want and become so good people can’t ignore you if you stop getting distracted.
blocks.zh: 只要你停止分心，就能学到任何你想学的东西，并变得足够优秀，让人无法忽视你——这事想想就很疯狂。

blocks.en: If you want to do something that has never been done before, don't choose a career. Choose a great work. A mission. Something that you can dedicate decades of your life to. People won't believe in you, and it may feel lonely at times, but for some, it is the only life worth living.
blocks.zh: 如果你想做一件前无古人的事，别选一份职业。选一项伟大的工作，一个使命，一件你能为之奉献数十年生命的事。人们不会相信你，有时你可能会感到孤独，但对某些人来说，这是唯一值得过的人生。

blocks.en: Sometimes, you need to become so disgusted with yourself, your life, or your situation that you can’t help but change. The work you didn’t care about doing in the first place. The relationships that have grown to be repetitive and stale. The body that doesn’t feel electric anymore. There’s a big difference between being hard on yourself and being so easy on yourself that it becomes the hardest thing in the world. Nobody is going to do it for you. In fact, most people don’t want you to change. Don’t focus on the positive. Focus on the negative, then ruthlessly redirect that energy toward a meaningful future.
blocks.zh: 有时候，你需要对自己、对自己的生活或处境厌恶到极点，以至于不得不改变。那些你起初根本懒得去做的事。那些变得重复而乏味的关系。那具不再感到充满活力的身体。苛责自己，和对自己太过宽容以致宽容成了世上最难的事，这两者之间有天壤之别。没人会替你做这件事。事实上，大多数人不希望你改变。别盯着积极面。盯着消极面，然后毫不留情地把这股能量转向一个有意义的未来。

blocks.en: You need 4 habits.
blocks.zh: 你需要 4 个习惯。

blocks.en:
One that builds your mind
One that builds your body
One that builds your money
One that builds your relationships
blocks.zh:
一个塑造你的心智
一个塑造你的身体
一个构建你的财富
一个经营你的人际关系

blocks.en:
Here's how to maximize all domains of your life:
youtu.be/SL5lwg1wYaE
blocks.zh:
以下是如何让你生活中各个领域都达到最优：
youtu.be/SL5lwg1wYaE

blocks.en: If you were secretly recorded during your next "deep work" session and had to watch it after, you'd probably find that 90% of the work you're doing is unnecessary, and most of the needle-moving tasks could be done in 2-3 hours, maximum.
blocks.zh: 如果你下一次"深度工作"时被偷偷录下来，之后不得不回看，你大概会发现：你所做的工作有 90% 是不必要的，而大多数真正推动进展的任务，最多 2 到 3 个小时就能完成。

blocks.en: Your brain thinks normal life is boring because it's gotten used to constant euphoria. You see more on your phone in 30 minutes than people used to in their entire lives. You eat foods that are so sweet that, once you stop, they become disgusting. If you dropped any and all sources of instant pleasure for the next 30 days, you'd feel like a child again. Life would feel electric.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑觉得日常生活无聊透顶，因为它已经习惯了持续的亢奋。你刷半小时手机看到的东西，比过去的人一辈子看到的还多。你吃的食物甜到发腻，一旦停下来就会觉得恶心。如果你在接下来的30天里戒掉所有即时快感来源，你会感觉自己又像个孩子。生活会再次充满电流。

blocks.en: You don't have ideas because you don't read.
blocks.zh: 你没有想法，因为你不读书。

blocks.en: You can't articulate ideas because you don't write.
blocks.zh: 你表达不出想法，因为你不写作。

blocks.en: You can't leverage ideas because you don't build.
blocks.zh: 你无法利用想法，因为你不构建。

blocks.en: You feel bored, anxious, or overwhelmed because your mind wants ideas to flow but you won't let them.
blocks.zh: 你感到无聊、焦虑或不堪重负，因为你的大脑渴望想法流动，而你却不允许它们流动。

blocks.en: It's liberating once you realize that the mind can be trained to do anything you want. That most of what you lack can be changed with knowledge, skill, and a logical sequence of steps that victims will attempt to convince you don't exist.
blocks.zh: 一旦你意识到大脑可以被训练去做任何你想做的事，你会感到解放。你缺乏的大部分东西都可以通过知识、技能和一系列逻辑步骤来改变——而受害者会试图让你相信这些步骤并不存在。

blocks.en: You're not struggling with productivity. You're struggling with not having a project worth being productive for. If you were working on the right thing, you wouldn't be able to stop thinking, working, obsessing.
blocks.zh: 你挣扎的不是效率问题。你挣扎的是没有一个值得你高效投入的项目。如果你在做正确的事，你会停不下来思考、工作、痴迷。

blocks.en: You're allowed to be motivated by money.
blocks.zh: 你可以被金钱驱动。

blocks.en: Scratch that, you are motivated by money. But you hide it because your parents, teachers, and peers convinced you it was a bad thing to pursue.
blocks.zh: 收回这句话，你就是被金钱驱动。但你隐藏了这一点，因为你的父母、老师和同龄人让你相信追求金钱是件坏事。

blocks.en: You work, right now, for money, to survive.
blocks.zh: 你现在工作，就是为了钱，为了生存。

blocks.en: Don't apologize for wanting to live well.
blocks.zh: 不要为想要过上好日子而道歉。

blocks.en: A bit off brand, but I've been experimenting with peptides for a year or two now.
blocks.zh: 有点偏离主题，但我已经试验肽类一两年了。

blocks.en: Peptides are to health what Bitcoin is to finance and what AI is to business.
blocks.zh: 肽对健康的意义，就像比特币对金融的意义，就像AI对商业的意义。

blocks.en: I tried them for the anti-aging, longevity, and healing benefits, but soon found that I was the most energetic and focused I'd ever been.
blocks.zh: 我尝试它们是为了抗衰老、长寿和修复效益，但很快发现我从未如此精力充沛和专注。

blocks.en: I wrote an article about it:
blocks.zh: 我写了一篇关于它的文章：

blocks.en: Your past is just an image in your mind. But you decide to live as if that image were your reality. Even worse, you Photoshop that image. You make it worse than it was and it slowly dims the future image you could create.
blocks.zh: 你的过去只是你脑海中的一幅图像。但你决定像那幅图像就是你的现实一样生活。更糟的是，你用Photoshop修改那幅图像。你把它变得比实际更糟，它慢慢暗淡了你本可以创造的未来图像。

blocks.en: If you're trying to build your own thing, you need to focus on the fact that nobody knows you exist and work until that's not the case. Your logo, LLC formation, and website are not going to make people know you exist.
blocks.zh: 如果你试图建立自己的事业，你需要专注于一个事实：没人知道你的存在，并努力直到情况改变。你的标志、有限责任公司注册和网站都不会让人们知道你的存在。

blocks.en: How to master any skill fast:
blocks.zh: 如何快速掌握任何技能：

blocks.en:
- Stop studying
- Outline a project
- Start building it
- Hit a roadblock
- Research how to overcome it
- Repeat until completed
blocks.zh:
- 停止学习
- 规划一个项目
- 开始动手做
- 遇到卡点
- 研究如何突破
- 重复，直到完成

blocks.en: Most people get trapped in tutorial hell and have nothing to show for years of "learning."
blocks.zh: 大多数人困在教程地狱里，学了几年却拿不出任何成果。

blocks.en: Do whatever you want.
blocks.zh: 想做什么就做什么。

blocks.en: When you do, you will make mistakes. At that point, if you are smart, you no longer want it, and begin to slowly course correct toward what you really want. If you always do what others want for you, you will never discover what you want.
blocks.zh: 这么做的时候，你会犯错。到那时，如果你足够聪明，你就会不再想要它，并开始慢慢调整方向，朝你真正想要的东西靠近。如果你总是做别人想让你做的事，你就永远发现不了自己想要什么。

blocks.en: You solve a problem by obsessing over it (without letting it destroy your mind).
blocks.zh: 解决一个问题，靠的是对它念念不忘（但别让它摧毁你的心智）。

blocks.en: Any problem, huge or small, can eventually be solved if you sit with it long enough.
blocks.zh: 任何问题，无论大小，只要你与之相处得足够久，最终都能解决。

blocks.en: When a problem is your lens for reality, you subconsciously pick up information and piece together the solution.
blocks.zh: 当一个问题是你看现实的镜头时，你会下意识地收集信息，拼凑出解决方案。

blocks.en: The solution to imposter syndrome is to produce so much that your body of work speaks for itself.
blocks.zh: 解决冒名顶替综合征的办法，是产出足够多，让你的作品本身替你说话。

blocks.en: A meaningful goal + clarity on how to achieve it + a real deadline closing in = the greatest nootropic stack known to man
blocks.zh: 一个有意义的目标 + 清楚知道如何实现它 + 一个真正逼近的截止日期 = 人类已知最强的促智组合

blocks.en: You can become unrecognizable in 5 years
blocks.zh: 5年内，你可以变得判若两人

blocks.en: You're distracted because you don't have responsibilities, priorities, or goals so important that you have no choice but to focus on them. You're afraid to commit so you drown in options.
blocks.zh: 你分心，是因为你没有责任、优先级或目标重要到你别无选择、只能专注于它们。你害怕承诺，所以淹没在选项里。

blocks.en: You don't set a goal to achieve something, you set a goal to become someone. Most people fail because they want the reward without the change that comes with it. If you have a burning desire to change, you'll achieve any goal you want.
blocks.zh: 你设立目标不是为了达成某件事，而是为了成为某个人。大多数人失败，是因为他们想要回报，却不愿接受随之而来的改变。如果你有强烈的改变渴望，你就能实现任何你想要的目标。

blocks.en: The most powerful habit you can adopt:
blocks.zh: 你能养成的最强大的习惯：

blocks.en: Using the first hour of your day to build, write, or produce something of value.
blocks.zh: 用一天中的第一个小时来构建、写作或产出有价值的东西。

blocks.en: If you don't have anyone to talk about your interests and passions with, start writing on the internet and you'll find them.
blocks.zh: 如果你找不到人可以聊你的兴趣和热情，就开始在网上写作，你会找到他们。

blocks.en: Everyone needs to learn about survival.
blocks.zh: 每个人都需要学习生存。

blocks.en: Humans are unique because (unlike animals) we survive on the psychological level.  We feel threatened when our beliefs, values, ideas, or worldview are challenged. We literally feel the fear and pain even when nothing is there.
blocks.zh: 人类的独特之处在于（与动物不同），我们在心理层面求生。当我们的信念、价值观、想法或世界观受到挑战时，我们会感到威胁。即使什么都没发生，我们也确实会感到恐惧和痛苦。

blocks.en: You aren't where you want to be because you don't have the mind of the person who would be in that position. You don't have the knowledge, skill, or experience, obviously. Changing that is in your control.
blocks.zh: 你没能达到理想的位置，是因为你还不具备那个位置的人应有的思维。显然，你缺少知识、技能和经验。但改变这一切，完全在你掌控之中。

blocks.en: If you're lost, start solving problems.
blocks.zh: 如果你感到迷茫，那就开始解决问题。

blocks.en: The problems that are staring you straight in the face. Your fitness, health, finances, mindset, work, or anything preventing you from having control over your life.
blocks.zh: 解决那些直接摆在你面前的问题。你的体能、健康、财务、心态、工作，或者任何阻碍你掌控生活的事情。

blocks.en: Experiment until you become obsessed and watch your life change.
blocks.zh: 不断尝试，直到你沉迷其中，然后看着你的生活发生改变。

blocks.en: You don't need experience to start because you only gain experience by starting.
blocks.zh: 你不需要经验才能开始，因为经验只能通过开始来获得。

blocks.en: Soft requirements / skills / experience:
blocks.zh: 软性要求 / 技能 / 经验：

blocks.en:
- Pref based in Toronto
- Typescript + bun monorepo
- Experience w microservices
- Experience w react-native
blocks.zh:
- 优先考虑多伦多本地
- TypeScript + Bun 单体仓库
- 有微服务经验
- 有 React Native 经验

blocks.en:
Link to short application:
docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAI…
blocks.zh:
简短申请链接：
docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAI…

blocks.en: We're looking for a mobile developer for the next iteration of Kortex (called Eden, more on that later).
blocks.zh: 我们正在为 Kortex 的下一个迭代版本（名为 Eden，详情后续公布）寻找一名移动端开发者。

blocks.en: Please pass the link below around if you know someone who'd be a good fit.
blocks.zh: 如果你认识合适的人选，请帮忙转发下面的链接。

blocks.en: Competitive pay, potential equity, preferably startup-pilled:
blocks.zh: 薪资有竞争力，可能提供股权，最好有创业精神：

blocks.en: When it's time to work, work.
blocks.zh: 该工作时，就工作。

blocks.en: When it's time to rest, rest.
blocks.zh: 该休息时，就休息。

blocks.en: Most people are always thinking about rest while working and work while resting.
blocks.zh: 大多数人总是工作时想着休息，休息时又想着工作。

blocks.en: An empty life is one lived in your head.
blocks.zh: 空虚的人生，是活在头脑中的人生。

blocks.en: Formal education serves society's goals, self-education serves your goals. One is assigned to you, the other is chosen by you. One demands attendance, the other requires curiosity. The difference between the two can drastically change the outcome of your mind and life.
blocks.zh: 正规教育服务于社会的目标，自我教育服务于你自己的目标。一个是被分配的，一个是你选择的。一个要求出勤，一个需要好奇心。两者之间的差异，能极大地改变你思维与人生的结果。

blocks.en: Most people suck at speaking, being social, and relationships because they see people as the static image they've constructed in their head rather than human beings who are just as stupid as you.
blocks.zh: 大多数人不擅长说话、社交和人际关系，因为他们把人看作是自己头脑中构建的静态形象，而不是像你一样愚蠢的人类。
