blocks.en: Personally, I have never felt so close to being radicalized or such a desire in the pit of my stomach to make sure she feels safe. She will be getting both, and I'll need a few gym sessions to think clearly.
blocks.zh: 就我个人而言，我从未如此接近激进化的边缘，也从未在心底里如此渴望确保她感到安全。这两样她都会得到，而我需要去几次健身房才能理清思绪。

blocks.en: I'd like to think that social media surfaces the worst of people right now, but even just one video out of thousands celebrating Charlie's death makes me fucking sick. There should be zero.
blocks.zh: 我愿意相信社交媒体现在只暴露了人们最坏的一面，但即使成千上万个视频中只有一个在庆祝查理的死亡，也让我恶心透顶。这样的视频应该一个都没有。

blocks.en: My innocent little wife now wants a gun + classes for self protection and is deeply questioning the mental health of much of the population. She has never been the type to get wrapped up in this stuff.
blocks.zh: 我天真单纯的小妻子现在想要一把枪和自卫课程，并且深深质疑很多人的心理健康。她从来不是那种会卷入这种事情的人。

blocks.en: Make of this what you will. Something changed yesterday.
blocks.zh: 你爱怎么理解就怎么理解吧。昨天，有些事情变了。

blocks.en: Do what you love, but study psychology, human behavior, and persuasion so people actually care about what you do enough to pay you for it.
blocks.zh: 做你热爱的事，但要学习心理学、人类行为和说服力，这样人们才会真正在乎你做的事，并愿意为之付费。

blocks.en: Procrastination is nature's way of telling you that you aren't working on the right thing.
blocks.zh: 拖延是大自然在告诉你，你并没有在做正确的事情。

blocks.en: Short form to attract minds.
blocks.zh: 用短内容吸引思想。

blocks.en: Long form to change minds.
blocks.zh: 长文改变思维。

blocks.en: Build your own thing for the first hour every day. See where it takes you. Commit to it. Produce something of value that you weren't forced to produce to pay the bills or because your parents or teachers told you to. Your future self is begging you and I know you hear that voice.
blocks.zh: 每天的第一个小时，做点属于自己的东西。看看它会把你带向何方。全身心投入进去。创造出真正有价值的东西——不是为生计所迫，不是因为父母或老师的吩咐。未来的你在恳求你，我知道你听见了那个声音。

blocks.en: Learn a lot of stuff. Build a lot of stuff. Identify problems. Solve them. Discover new paths. Take them. Reflect on the journey. Do it better the next time. Don't get distracted. Don't turn on autopilot. Take risks. Fail until you can afford to succeed.
blocks.zh: 大量学习。大量创造。发现问题。解决问题。探索新路。勇敢去走。反思旅程。下次做得更好。别分心。别自动驾驶。去冒险。失败，直到你有能力成功。

blocks.en: That's it.
blocks.zh: 就这样。

blocks.en: The answer to 99% of your questions is "try it"
blocks.zh: 你的问题，99% 的答案都是「去试试」。

blocks.en: If you feel lost, write down:
blocks.zh: 如果你感到迷茫，写下：

blocks.en:
1) Who you want to become
2) Who you don't want to become
3) The 3-5 things you can do today
blocks.zh:
1）你想成为谁
2）你不想成为谁
3）今天你能做的 3 到 5 件事

blocks.en: You're lost because you don't have a direction to work toward, an enemy to work away from, and tasks that move the needle toward your goals.
blocks.zh: 你迷茫，是因为你没有努力的方向、没有要逃离的敌人、没有能推动你靠近目标的任务。

blocks.en: You don't find what you're passionate about.
blocks.zh: 热情，不是找到的。

blocks.en: You create it. You build it. You invest energy into a goal. You become great at something. You stick with it whether you feel like it or not.
blocks.zh: 是你创造出来的。是你建立起来的。你把精力投入一个目标。你在某件事上变得出色。无论想不想，你都坚持到底。

blocks.en: You aren't going to be passionate about something you have zero experience in.
blocks.zh: 你不可能对一件毫无经验的事情充满热情。

blocks.en: Most people aren't afraid to fail. They're afraid to succeed because that would require them to change. It would require them to become the person who was capable of success. It would require them to let go of the pleasures they are silently addicted to.
blocks.zh: 大多数人不是害怕失败。他们害怕成功，因为那需要他们改变。需要他们成为那个有能力成功的人。需要他们放下自己默默上瘾的种种快感。

blocks.en: Pay close attention to the times when you can't stop having ideas, thinking about a project, or obsessively taking notes. You're being pulled into a new chapter of life and the worst thing you can do is let that spark die out.
blocks.zh: 请密切关注那些时刻：你停不下来地涌出想法、反复琢磨一个项目、痴迷地记着笔记。你正被拽向人生的新篇章，而最糟糕的做法，就是让那点火花熄灭。

blocks.en: You used to want it. You used to be hungry. You used to love the challenge. But then you got soft. Life became dull. You became numb. At some point you're going to have to get so sick of it that your spark comes back.
blocks.zh: 你曾经想要它。你曾经渴望它。你曾经热爱那份挑战。但后来你变软了。生活变得乏味。你变得麻木。总有一天，你会厌倦到极点，直到火花重新燃起。

blocks.en: Everyone is playing one of three money games:
blocks.zh: 每个人都在玩三种金钱游戏之一：

blocks.en: - Survival – Make enough to not die. Money as master.
blocks.zh: - 生存——赚到不至于饿死的钱。金钱是主人。

blocks.en: - Success – Make enough to matter. Money as scoreboard.
blocks.zh: - 成功——赚到足以证明自己重要的钱。金钱是记分牌。

blocks.en: - Sacred – Make enough to authentically create. Money as energy.
blocks.zh: - 神圣——赚到足以真实创造的钱。金钱是能量。

blocks.en: Money is evil at level 1. Money is good at level 3.
blocks.zh: 在第一层，金钱是邪恶的。在第三层，金钱是美好的。

blocks.en: Just solve problems. Your problems first. Then others' problems. That's how you learn, become valuable, become high-agency, earn an income, practice creativity, and improve the quality of your mind, body, spirit, finances, relationships. Get distracted and life starts to crumble.
blocks.zh: 就是解决问题。先解决自己的问题。再解决别人的问题。你就是这样学习、变得有价值、变得有能动性、赚取收入、锻炼创造力，并提升心智、身体、精神、财务和人际关系质量的。一旦分心，生活就开始崩塌。

blocks.en: The desire to succeed is more important than knowing how to succeed because the person with the strongest desire will figure it out no matter the cost.
blocks.zh: 成功的渴望，比知道如何成功更重要。因为渴望最强烈的人，无论付出什么代价，都会找到办法。

blocks.en: The longer you spend studying business, health, relationships, etc the more you see that everything is the wrong thing to do yet everything is the right thing to do until you reach the point where you ignore it all and figure it out for yourself.
blocks.zh: 你研究商业、健康、人际关系等越久，就越会发现：所有事都是错的，但同时所有事都是对的，直到你达到一个境界——无视一切教条，自己摸索出答案。

blocks.en: My editor has hit that point where he finally gets it. Started writing a fiction book and can’t stop thinking about it. Got on a real training program and dialed in his diet. Complete mentality and energy shift. Video games became boring overnight. Fell back in love with life.
blocks.zh: 我的编辑终于开窍了。他开始写一本小说，满脑子都是它；制定了真正的训练计划，调整了饮食。心态和精力彻底转变，电子游戏一夜之间变得索然无味，重新爱上了生活。

blocks.en: Most people have no clue how bad they feel because that’s “normal” to them. Train, walk, and eat well for 2 weeks (vertical diet for simplicity) and your mind will be blown by how much different you feel.
blocks.zh: 大多数人根本不知道自己感觉有多糟，因为那对他们来说是“正常”的。训练、散步、好好吃饭两周（简单起见，可以试试垂直饮食法），你会惊讶地发现自己感觉大不相同。

blocks.en: The best thing about a writing habit is that it makes you realize how stupid you really are. Most people think they have clear ideas, but since they’ve never written them out in physical space, they’ve never thoroughly examined their thinking.
blocks.zh: 写作习惯最大的好处，是让你意识到自己有多蠢。大多数人以为自己想法清晰，但因为从未把它们写下来，也就从未彻底审视过自己的思维。

blocks.en: Master your mind.
blocks.zh: 掌控你的心智。

blocks.en: Read more. Consume less. Produce more. React less. Focus intensely on one thing. Zoom out and let go of everything. Train. Recover.
blocks.zh: 多读，少消费，多产出，少反应。专注一件事，同时也要能抽离出来，放下一切。训练，恢复。

blocks.en: Your mind is the operating system for reality. If you don't program it, others will, and that never ends well.
blocks.zh: 你的心智是现实的操作系统。如果你不编程，别人就会替你编，而那从来不会有好结果。

blocks.en: Pro bodybuilders don't force themselves to train and eat healthy, they can't imagine a life where they don't.
blocks.zh: 职业健美运动员不会强迫自己训练和健康饮食，他们根本无法想象不这样生活。

blocks.en: That doesn't mean it isn't hard or uncomfortable, but their relationship with pain is completely different from the average person.
blocks.zh: 这不意味着过程不艰难、不舒服，但他们对待痛苦的态度与普通人截然不同。

blocks.en: Discipline is an identity problem.
blocks.zh: 自律，本质上是一个身份认同问题。

blocks.en: If you have to force yourself to do hard things, you're not going to make it. I can't think of one successful person who hated their entire way to the top. Their desire to succeed was so much stronger than their desire for comfort that they couldn't help but do the hard thing.
blocks.zh: 如果你必须强迫自己去做艰难的事，你走不远。我认识的成功人士中，没有一个是一路痛恨着登上顶峰的。他们对成功的渴望远超过对舒适的渴望，以至于不由自主地去完成艰难的事。

blocks.en: The only thing standing between where you are and where you want to be is a series of decisions that most people refuse to make.
blocks.zh: 横亘在你现状与理想之间的，只有一系列大多数人拒绝做出的决定。

blocks.en: If you feel lost, the solution is counterintuitive.
blocks.zh: 如果你感到迷茫，解决方法可能反直觉。

blocks.en: Throw yourself into the unknown and become even more lost. Move locations. Read new books. Upskill for a new job.
blocks.zh: 投身未知，让自己更迷茫。换个地方住，读新书，学新技能换份工作。

blocks.en: Force yourself into a place where you CAN gain clarity and interest.
blocks.zh: 强迫自己进入一个能获得清晰感和兴趣的环境。

blocks.en: Then, discover your way out.
blocks.zh: 然后，找到出路。

blocks.en: Nobody is coming to save you.
blocks.zh: 没有人会来救你。

blocks.en: Your parents, friends, or government may try, but then you don't learn a thing. You aren't actually saved. And you'll need to be saved over and over again until you decide to take control of your life.
blocks.zh: 父母、朋友或政府或许会尝试，但那样你什么也学不到。你并没有真正得救，而且你会一次又一次需要被拯救，直到你决定自己掌控人生。

blocks.en: Learning is one of the few superpowers that everyone has, but most people view it as a way to prepare themselves to earn an income, then they become too busy, or attach themselves to rigid beliefs, and stop. It's simple, but learning one new thing every day can change your life.
blocks.zh: 学习是少数人人都拥有的超能力之一，但大多数人只把它看作赚钱前的准备工作，然后他们就忙起来了，或者固守某些死板的观念，就此止步。道理很简单：每天学一点新东西，就能改变你的人生。

blocks.en: I get unnecessarily mad when people don't stick to their goals.
blocks.zh: 看到别人坚持不下去自己的目标，我会没来由地恼火。

blocks.en: You say you want to start a business, lose weight, meet new people, whatever. You say you want to change your life because you're tired of where you are.
blocks.zh: 你说你想创业、想减肥、想认识新朋友，随便什么吧。你说你想改变自己的人生，因为你对现状厌倦了。

blocks.en: Someone tells you exactly what to do, gives you the entire roadmap.
blocks.zh: 有人把该怎么做一五一十地告诉了你，把整张路线图都给了你。

blocks.en: Then you don't do it. And you can't give any good reason why.
blocks.zh: 然后你并不去做。而且你给不出任何像样的理由。

blocks.en: "Oh I have to work and got sidetracked."
blocks.zh: “唉，我得上班，就分心了。”

blocks.en: "I didn't go to the gym because I had something else do to."
blocks.zh: “我今天没去健身房，因为有事要忙。”

blocks.en: What the fuck are you talking about?
blocks.zh: 你他妈在说什么？

blocks.en: You say you "have" to work and "have" to do whatever else you're doing in the life you just said you don't want to live, but you don't HAVE to do the only things that lead to the life you want?
blocks.zh: 你说你“得”上班，“得”去做你刚说自己不想要的那种生活里的那些事，可你偏偏就不“得”去做那些唯一能通向你想要的生活的事？

blocks.en: Everyone is obsessed with getting "actionable advice" when that clearly doesn't matter at all. Your psychology is in the toilet. Your priorities are nonexistent. You need to take a day off and really think about what you are doing.
blocks.zh: 人人都执迷于获取“可操作的忠告”，可这显然根本不重要。你的心态已经烂透了。你的优先级压根不存在。你需要请一天假，好好想想自己到底在干什么。

blocks.en: "Oh Dan be more empathetic!"
blocks.zh: “哦，Dan（丹），多点同理心吧！”

blocks.en: That IS empathy. Empathy is wanting the best for someone even if it hurts their little feelings. Most people will simply pander to you so that they feel good about not making you feel bad. That's nowhere close to empathy.
blocks.zh: 这恰恰就是同理心。同理心是希望对方变得更好，哪怕这会伤到他那点小心情。大多数人只会顺着你，好让自己在没让你难受这件事上心安理得。那跟同理心差得远了。

blocks.en: Do better.
blocks.zh: 争点气吧。

blocks.en: Just copy what works and make it slightly better.
blocks.zh: 照着行得通的做法抄，再把它改得稍微好一点。

blocks.en: If you're starting out, it is so incredibly unlikely that you have the experience to do something that's 100% new. If you look around, you will see copies upon copies with one tiny thing that's different. Just do that.
blocks.zh: 如果你刚起步，那你几乎不可能有经验去做一件百分之百全新的事。你环顾四周就会发现，全是复制品叠着复制品，只差一个微小的不同之处。照做就是了。

blocks.en: Imitate, then innovate.
blocks.zh: 先模仿，再创新。

blocks.en: The reason most beginners fail is because they have this weird to desire to be original when they haven't earned the right to be original. Drop your ego and do what works. Save yourself the pain.
blocks.zh: 大多数新手失败，是因为他们有种奇怪的执念，非要原创，可他们还没挣到原创的资格。放下自尊，去做行得通的事。省下那份苦吧。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to learn, start writing.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道该学什么，那就从写作开始。

blocks.en: Not because writing is a great skill, but because writing teaches you how to think, how to learn, and how to inspire people to care about what you do. Those skills are much less likely to be replaced.
blocks.zh: 不是因为写作是多了不起的技能，而是因为写作能教你如何思考、如何学习，以及如何激励别人在乎你所做的事。这些技能被取代的可能性要小得多。

blocks.en: You'll learn a lot more by saying "fuck it," shutting your mind off, and doing the thing rather than reading 10 new books that fill your mind with noise and make it easy to do nothing.
blocks.zh: 说一句“去他的”，关掉脑子，直接动手去做，你能学到的东西远比读十本新书多得多——那些书只会往你脑子里塞满噪音，让你更容易什么都不做。

blocks.en: If you're the type of person who has a lot of ideas, your mind is your worst enemy, because you also have a lot of excuses. The good news is: making excuses is a habit, and if you can replace that habit with execution, you become unstoppable.
blocks.zh: 如果你是那种点子很多的人，你的大脑就是你最大的敌人，因为你的借口也很多。好消息是：找借口是一种习惯，而如果你能用行动取代这个习惯，你就会变得势不可挡。

blocks.en: Artisan > factory
blocks.zh: 匠人 > 工厂

blocks.en: That being said, I don't know how it looks for beginners starting out, but I've heard good things.
blocks.zh: 话虽如此，我不清楚初学者刚起步时情况如何，但我听说反馈不错。

blocks.en: I transferred and cleaned my list beforehand, but gave it a few months before gauging open rates. They've stayed consistent
blocks.zh: 我提前转移并清理了列表，但等了几个月才评估打开率。打开率一直保持稳定。

blocks.en: I slept on Substack for a while and am pretty baffled that (1) I've been getting more monthly views there than on YouTube and (2) open rates are higher than they've ever been
blocks.zh: 我一度对Substack不以为然，但现在相当困惑：(1) 我每月在那里的浏览量居然超过了YouTube，(2) 打开率也达到了历史新高。

blocks.en: Bullish on written long form
blocks.zh: 看好长篇文字创作。

blocks.en: Most people don't have money problems, they have emotional management and focus problems.
blocks.zh: 大多数人没有金钱问题，他们有情绪管理和专注力的问题。

blocks.en: You need a product or service, people to buy it, and the ability to learn and iterate. That's it. You know that. You just can't sit down and do it, and you can't see through the illusions your mind constantly fabricates to try and keep you the same.
blocks.zh: 你需要一个产品或服务，需要有人购买，还需要学习和迭代的能力。就这样。你明白的。你只是没法坐下来去做，也没法看穿你大脑不断编织的幻象——那些幻象试图让你保持原样。

blocks.en: 18-year-olds are expected to know exactly what they want to do with their life when the only thing they've learned is how to imitate their parents and teachers. The greatest thing young people can do is admit they don't know what they want, begin self-education, and take as many risks as possible while they have their youth.
blocks.zh: 18岁的年轻人被期望清楚地知道自己一生想做什么，可他们唯一学到的东西就是模仿父母和老师。年轻人能做的最了不起的事，就是承认自己不知道想要什么，开始自我教育，并在拥有青春时尽可能多地去冒险。

blocks.en: This is somewhat counterintuitive, because you have to be confident and polarizing. That's what gives people the clarity to act. Nuance absolutely has its place, but it often just leads to people being overwhelmed with options and provides justification to do nothing.
blocks.zh: 这有点反直觉，因为你必须自信且立场鲜明。这才能让人清晰地采取行动。细微差别当然有其价值，但它往往只会让人被选项淹没，并为什么都不做提供理由。

blocks.en: The more I write and create stuff on the internet, the more I'm realizing that my job isn't to help people succeed with my super special advice. It's to help them fail by giving them something to try. That way they can start to understand what *they* want and take their own path.
blocks.zh: 我在网上写作和创作得越多，就越意识到我的工作不是用我那些超级特别的建议帮助人们成功。而是通过给他们一些可以尝试的东西来帮助他们失败。这样他们才能开始理解*自己*想要什么，并走出自己的路。

blocks.en: A sign of a well designed life is that you don't want to take a day off because that would be far less enjoyable than your average day.
blocks.zh: 精心设计的人生有一个标志：你不想休假，因为那会比平常的日子无趣得多。

blocks.en: I am once again telling you if you can spend 8 hours building someone else's dreams you can spend 1 hour building your own.
blocks.zh: 我再次告诉你：如果你能花8小时构建别人的梦想，你就能花1小时构建自己的。

blocks.en: If you can't learn anything in 2 weeks you're trying to learn too much.
blocks.zh: 如果你两周内什么都学不会，那是你想学的东西太多了。

blocks.en:
Here's how to learn fast without any science tactics that just distract you even more from achieving your goal:
youtu.be/oGSHKXEKT2Q
blocks.zh:
这里有个快速学习的方法，不需要任何科学技巧——那些技巧只会让你更分心，离目标更远：
youtu.be/oGSHKXEKT2Q

blocks.en: If you don't choose your own game, society will assign you one, and society's games are incredibly boring. Same quest. Same routine. For 40 years until you win a mediocre prize. You don't want freedom from rules. You want the freedom to create your own.
blocks.zh: 如果你不选择自己的游戏，社会就会给你分配一个，而社会的游戏极其无聊。同样的任务。同样的日常。四十年，直到你赢得一个平庸的奖品。你想要的不是摆脱规则的自由。你想要的是创造自己规则的自由。

blocks.en: I am once again asking you to start and never stop. What the fuck else are you going to do? You AREN'T going to reach your potential? You're just going to sit in front of your little screen all day? You're just going to keep making life hard instead of doing something hard?
blocks.zh: 我再次请求你：开始，并且永不停止。你他妈还能做什么？你*不*去发挥自己的潜力了？你就打算整天坐在那小屏幕前？你就打算继续让生活艰难，而不是去做点难做的事？

blocks.en: You can log 8 hours of World of Warcraft or staring at your phone without blinking an eye but can't focus for 30 minutes on work that will change your life. You don't have a focus problem. You just don't see your life as a game and don't treat your goals as quests.
blocks.zh: 你可以连续打8小时《魔兽世界》或盯着手机眼睛都不眨，却无法专注30分钟去做能改变你人生的工作。你没有专注力问题。你只是没把人生看作一场游戏，没把目标当作任务。

blocks.en: This only becomes overwhelming if you don't know how to move any of those numbers. Most people drown with anxiety looking at analytics because they don't instantly decide to acquire new skills and learn how to move the numbers. They play the game but refuse to gain experience.
blocks.zh: 只有当你不知道如何改变那些数字时，这才会变得令人不堪重负。大多数人看着分析数据就淹没在焦虑中，因为他们没有立刻决定去获取新技能、学习如何改变数字。他们玩这个游戏，却拒绝获得经验。

blocks.en: Get absolutely dialed for a month. Life becomes a game when you pay a 'delusional' amount of attention to the details. Track your food. Track your lifts. Track your steps. Track your revenue. Progressive overload each week. Ignore everything else. You'll enjoy progress again.
blocks.zh: 用一个月彻底调整到位。当你对细节给予‘妄想般’的关注时，生活就变成了一场游戏。追踪你的食物。追踪你的举重。追踪你的步数。追踪你的收入。每周渐进超负荷。忽略其他一切。你会再次享受进步。

blocks.en: Quitting bad habits is easy if you research their negative impacts to the point where you're disgusted with them and hate the thought of doing them.
blocks.zh: 戒掉坏习惯其实很简单——只要你深入研究它们的负面影响，直到你对它们心生厌恶，光是想到要做就反感。

blocks.en: Everything meaningful in life is downstream of self-direction. Pursuing your own goals (not the ones society assigned you), making mistakes, correcting them, discovering new knowledge, and falling in love with that process so you never fall into a depressing stagnation.
blocks.zh: 人生中一切有意义的事，都源于自我主导。追求你自己的目标（而非社会指派给你的那些），犯错，纠错，探索新知，并爱上这个过程，这样你就永远不会陷入令人沮丧的停滞。

blocks.en: You don't know what to do with your life because you thought about your future for 30 seconds and called it a day.
blocks.zh: 你不知道这辈子该做什么，是因为你只花30秒想了想未来，就草草了事了。

blocks.en: You need to think about it every day. For the rest of your life. You need to ruthlessly eliminate what you don't want and refine what you want.
blocks.zh: 你需要每天都去想它。终其一生。你需要狠下心来剔除你不想要的，打磨你想要的。

blocks.en: For the next 6 months, every time you blame someone else or try to change them, try accepting the blame and changing yourself even if you aren't at fault. Your life will turn around faster than you can imagine.
blocks.zh: 接下来的6个月里，每次你想责怪别人或试图改变别人时，试着承担责任、改变自己——哪怕错不在你。你的人生会以超乎想象的速度迎来转机。

blocks.en: Work when it's time to work and rest when it's time to rest.
blocks.zh: 该工作时工作，该休息时休息。

blocks.en: Work is a narrow state of mind while rest is an open state. If your life is dominated by work, you miss out on the ideas and creativity that lead to higher-paying meaningful work. This is why most people are stuck.
blocks.zh: 工作是一种收窄的心智状态，而休息是一种开放的状态。如果你的生活被工作主导，你就会错过那些能带来更高收入、更有意义工作的灵感和创造力。这就是大多数人困在原地的原因。

blocks.en: If it doesn't lead to something you'd want to take over your life, don't do it.
blocks.zh: 如果一件事最终不会带你走向你愿意为之倾注人生的东西，那就别做。

blocks.en: Nobody cares about your niche. They care about your point of view. They don't want regurgitated information they can get from chat gpt or google. They want your opinion. They want your conviction. They want to feel the excitement and despair happening in your unique mind.
blocks.zh: 没人在乎你的细分领域。他们在乎的是你的观点。他们不想要那些从ChatGPT或谷歌上就能找到的、被反复咀嚼过的信息。他们想要你的看法，想要你的信念，想要感受你那颗独特头脑里翻涌的兴奋与绝望。

blocks.en: People drastically underestimate how much one single hour per day on 1-2 needle-moving tasks can compound. It doesn't feel like much each day, and it can be demotivating, but sometimes an hour is all you have, and 365+ hours can build something incredible.
blocks.zh: 人们严重低估了每天一小时、专注在一两件真正推动进展的事情上，能产生多大的复利效应。单看每一天，似乎微不足道，甚至会让人泄气，但有时你拥有的就只有这一小时，而365小时以上足以筑起了不起的东西。

blocks.en: The single greatest productivity tip I could give is to wake up an hour earlier and get straight to work on the single most important thing that will move the needle toward your goals. Preferably before most people are even awake. People are the biggest source of distractions.
blocks.zh: 我能给出的最棒的一条效率建议，就是早起一小时，直接着手去做那件最能推动你目标前进的最重要的事。最好赶在大多数人还没醒来之前。人，是干扰的最大来源。

blocks.en: Competition is largely an illusion. 95% of people don't even try to do great things. 0.1% of the people are loud, so you overestimate how many people there are. The rest get stuck worrying about competition and quitting after 2 weeks.
blocks.zh: 竞争在很大程度上是一种幻觉。95%的人压根儿就没尝试去做了不起的事。0.1%的人嗓门很大，所以你高估了人数。其余的人则困在担忧竞争里，两周后就放弃了。

blocks.en: If you're young, I don't think you understand how much of an advantage you have. When I talk with various leaders, CEOs, etc, they're absolutely clueless when it comes to social media and technology. They pay an absurd amount of money for young people to help them. By simply being on social media for so long, your brain is wired for it. You have what could be a hyper valuable skill set out of the box. You just need to shift from a consumer mindset to a business mindset. You need to realize that people will, in fact, pay you to make stupid videos.
blocks.zh: 如果你还年轻，我觉得你并不明白你手握多大的优势。我和各路领导者、CEO等人交流时，发现他们对社交媒体和科技一无所知。他们花大价钱请年轻人来帮忙。仅仅因为你长期泡在社交媒体上，你的大脑就是为此而生的。你天生就拥有一套可能极具价值的技能。你只需要从消费者心态转向商业心态。你需要意识到，人们真的会付钱让你拍那些“愚蠢”的视频。

blocks.en: Discipline is about getting clear on what you want. Once you know with absolute conviction that you don't want the life that your current habits are leading to, you hate the thought of doing them. Staying the same becomes more painful than pursuing an uncertain goal.
blocks.zh: 自律的本质，是搞清楚你想要什么。一旦你无比确信自己不想要当前习惯所导向的那种人生，你就会厌恶去做那些事。维持现状，会变得比追求一个不确定的目标更痛苦。

blocks.en: Your potential is determined by how much uncertainty you're willing to embrace.
blocks.zh: 你的潜力，取决于你愿意拥抱多少不确定性。

blocks.en: Don't identify with a tool because tools change and get replaced. Identify with what the tools allow you to do: create. That's what you love doing. It doesn't matter if you do it with a paintbrush, camera, Photoshop, or AI. What matters is the vision you bring into reality.
blocks.zh: 不要把自己等同于某个工具，因为工具会变、会被取代。要把自己等同于工具所让你做的事：创造。那才是你热爱的事。无论是用画笔、相机、Photoshop还是AI，都无所谓。重要的是你带入现实的愿景。

blocks.en: Discipline is a feature of identity.
blocks.zh: 自律是身份认同的一个特征。

blocks.en: Meaning, you are already disciplined based on what you view as important. Some people play 12 hours of video games, others have no issue eating healthy and going to the gym.
blocks.zh: 也就是说，你其实早已在自己看重的事情上展现出了自律。有人能打12小时游戏，另一些人对健康饮食和去健身房毫无障碍。

blocks.en: Discipline isn't forced, it's native to who you are.
blocks.zh: 自律不是逼出来的，它本就根植于你是谁。

blocks.en: One of the best things you can do for your future is learn "how to think."
blocks.zh: 你能为自己的未来做的最好的事情之一，就是学会“如何思考”。

blocks.en: Money, relationships, or anything else you can do in life are dependent on how well you think.
blocks.zh: 金钱、人际关系，或你人生中能做的任何事，都取决于你思考的质量。

blocks.en:
Use this mental model and you'll be blown away:
youtu.be/YTWm6sG0n6s
blocks.zh:
用这个思维模型，你会大开眼界：
youtu.be/YTWm6sG0n6s

blocks.en: You as a single person have more power today than a 20 person company of the past. The internet gave you the ability to learn anything. Social media gave you the leverage to reach anyone. AI is giving you the ability to create almost anything. Please don't waste it.
blocks.zh: 如今，你单枪匹马的力量，已经超过了过去一家二十人的公司。互联网让你有能力学会任何东西。社交媒体给了你触达任何人的杠杆。AI 正赋予你创造几乎任何事物的能力。请别浪费这一切。

blocks.en: Feeling lost is a sign that you are no longer your past self, but not fully the person you want to become. That's uncomfortable. The worst thing you can do here is what most people do, which is to numb the pain with comfort and close yourself off to your future self.
blocks.zh: 感到迷茫，说明你已不再是过去的自己，但还没完全成为你想成为的人。这让人不舒服。此时你能做的最糟的事，就是大多数人都会做的事：用舒适麻痹痛苦，把自己对未来的自己封闭起来。

blocks.en: The reason you're not happy is because you think happiness = euphoria so if you aren't maxing out on dopamine all the time you think you're doing something wrong.
blocks.zh: 你不快乐，是因为你把快乐等同于兴奋，所以只要没有一直把多巴胺拉满，你就觉得自己哪里做错了。

blocks.en: Happiness, most of the time, is being calm and in a good mood.
blocks.zh: 快乐，大多数时候，是平静，是心情不错。

blocks.en: Focus on 2 things:
blocks.zh: 专注两件事：

blocks.en: - Mastering your mental / emotional state in situations you can't control
blocks.zh: - 在无法掌控的处境中，掌控好自己的心理与情绪状态

blocks.en: - Realizing you can control more than you think, and that you can improve your skill to the point of getting what you want
blocks.zh: - 意识到你能掌控的比你想象的多，并且你能把技能提升到足以得到你想要的东西

blocks.en: Give it 10 years and watch everything change
blocks.zh: 给自己十年时间，然后看着一切改变

blocks.en: One of the most important things you can understand is that school trains you to learn a specific way, and that way is extremely slow. Learning allows you to be useful and get what you want. It should be a top priority to learn how to learn, practice it, and master it.
blocks.zh: 你能理解的最重要的事情之一，是学校训练你用某种特定的方式学习，而那种方式极其缓慢。学习让你变得有用、让你得到想要的东西。学会如何学习、加以练习、直至精通，应该成为你的头等大事。

blocks.en: As much as people want to argue that physical appearance doesn’t matter, it does. A lot. It’s 24/7 non-verbal communication of your values.
blocks.zh: 无论人们多么想争辩外表不重要，它其实很重要，而且非常重要。它是你价值观全天候的非语言表达。

blocks.en: Most people aren’t unattractive, they just don’t put a shred of effort into taking care of themselves.
blocks.zh: 大多数人并不丑，他们只是对自己的照料连一丁点努力都不肯付出。

blocks.en: You can learn anything in 2 weeks.
blocks.zh: 你可以在两周内学会任何东西。

blocks.en: If you can't, you're trying to learn too much at once. Break the goal down and focus solely on doing what's necessary to reach it. If your learning doesn't involve doing, most of what you learn is disappearing the second you learn it.
blocks.zh: 如果做不到，那是因为你想一次学太多。把目标拆解，只专注于达成目标所必需的事。如果你的学习不包含动手去做，那你学到的大部分内容，在学到的瞬间就消失了。

blocks.en: If you're trying to get exposure on your work, it sounds weird, but starting a podcast is one of the best things you can do.
blocks.zh: 如果你想为自己的作品获得曝光，这听起来有点怪，但做一档播客是你能做的最好的事情之一。

blocks.en: Not because you want to make it the number 1 podcast in the world, but because:
blocks.zh: 不是因为你想要把它做成世界第一的播客，而是因为：

blocks.en: 1) High status people / people you respect would rather be on a podcast than on a call with you. They're more likely to respond and accept, meaning you get a free mentorship call to ask them all your questions.
blocks.zh: 1）高地位的人／你尊敬的人，更愿意上你的播客，而不是跟你通电话。他们更可能回复并接受，这意味着你免费获得一次导师级的通话，可以问他们所有问题。

blocks.en: 2) You leverage their large audience, and they also benefit from it. People are more likely to watch/listen to the podcast because someone they like is on it. This is arguably the best beginner growth "hack."
blocks.zh: 2）你借助了他们庞大的受众，他们也从中受益。人们更可能观看／收听这档播客，因为他们喜欢的人在节目里。这可以说是最适合新手的最佳增长“黑客技巧”。

blocks.en: 3) You form deeper relationships with good people. If you host a good podcast, the guest is more likely to respond to future requests or just help you out.
blocks.zh: 3）你与优秀的人建立了更深的关系。如果你主持一档好播客，嘉宾更可能回应你未来的请求，或者干脆帮你一把。

blocks.en: If you're a creator, freelancer, or just someone who is trying to do their own thing, you need people to see your content and work.
blocks.zh: 如果你是创作者、自由职业者，或者只是想做自己事情的人，你需要让人看到你的内容和作品。

blocks.en: Most people rarely gain traction because the algorithm is like the lottery. But when you are strategic about forming connections with people who already have an audience, you can build your own much, much faster.
blocks.zh: 大多数人很少获得起势，因为算法就像抽奖。但当你策略性地与已经拥有受众的人建立联系时，你就能快得多地建立起自己的受众。

blocks.en: Even if you only host 2-4 podcasts in your entire career, those alone could change everything for you depending on the guest you get on.
blocks.zh: 哪怕你整个职业生涯只主持 2 到 4 期播客，单凭这些，就可能因为你请到的嘉宾而改变你的一切。

blocks.en: Everyone wants a great story to tell (but not the catastrophic failure that makes it worth telling).
blocks.zh: 每个人都想有一个精彩的故事可讲（但又不想经历那场让故事值得一讲的灾难性失败）。

blocks.en: There is a very rare type of idea. When it pops into your mind, you feel like you can't help yourself. You're forced by some higher instinct to act on it. You cancel all plans. The vision is clear. You must protect it at all costs. These are the ideas that change your life.
blocks.zh: 有一种非常罕见的思想。当它闪过你的脑海，你会觉得自己情不自禁。某种更高的本能逼着你去行动。你取消所有计划。愿景清晰。你不惜一切代价保护它。这些，就是改变你人生的思想。

blocks.en: Your work is unlikely to be noticed until your skill matches your taste. You know what “good” looks like, but you need to practice until what you produce is at that level. That’s when things take off.
blocks.zh: 在你的技艺追上你的品味之前，你的作品很难被人注意到。你知道“好”是什么样子，但你需要练习，直到你产出的东西达到那个水平。那时，一切才会腾飞。

blocks.en: I hate the whole "entrepreneurship isn't for everyone" narrative because "it's a hard thing to do." No shit it's hard. That's the point. Yes, most people aren't cut out for it right at this very second. But people can grow. They can learn something new. They can, in fact, challenge themselves. It’s insane to believe that people can actually take control of the 1/3 of their life called work, I know.
blocks.zh: 我讨厌“创业不适合所有人”这种说法，理由居然是“这事太难了”。废话，当然难。难就对了。是的，大多数人眼下确实不是这块料。但人是可以成长的。他们可以学新东西。事实上，他们可以挑战自己。我知道，相信人们能真正掌控自己人生中三分之一的时间——也就是工作——这听起来很疯狂。

blocks.en: Everyone could benefit from at bare minimum trying to do something difficult that has such a massive upside in the form of wisdom, skill, and increasing your value even if it doesn't work out. Call me delusional but I believe everyone should pursue work they find meaningful and avoid a life thats perpetually comfortable.
blocks.zh: 每个人至少都应该尝试去做一些困难的事，哪怕不成，也能收获智慧、技能，并提升自身价值，何乐而不为。说我妄想也好，但我相信每个人都应该追求自己觉得有意义的工作，避免过一种永远舒适的生活。

blocks.en: “But you can also get a super high paying job that you enjoy!”
blocks.zh: “但你也可以找一份高薪又享受的工作啊！”

blocks.en: Yes, but that is still fucking hard. Sometimes a lot harder than entrepreneurship (no, entrepreneurship does not equal trying to build a billion dollar company or working 16 hours day).
blocks.zh: 没错，但那照样他妈的难。有时候比创业难多了（不，创业不等于要打造一家十亿美元的公司，也不等于每天工作16小时）。

blocks.en: Being an “entrepreneur” originally meant “to undertake.” To do something. To take a risk. To be high agency. Self governance. To direct your own life rather than outsource it to someone else.
blocks.zh: “创业者”最初的意思是“承担”。去做一件事。去冒险。拥有高度的能动性。自我治理。引导自己的人生，而不是外包给别人。

blocks.en: So yes, entrepreneurship is for everyone, like the free individuals of the past working on their craft and pursuing their interests.
blocks.zh: 所以，创业适合所有人，就像过去那些自由人一样，专注于自己的手艺，追求自己的兴趣。

blocks.en: If you haven’t tried it (actually tried it) then you have no idea whether or not it’s for you, and not trying it because someone said it’s “not for everyone” is both dumb and robbing you of potential.
blocks.zh: 如果你还没试过（真正试过），那你根本不知道它适不适合你。因为别人说“不适合所有人”就不去尝试，这既愚蠢，又剥夺了你的潜力。

blocks.en: Be incredibly careful with what you allow to access your mind
blocks.zh: 对你允许进入头脑的东西要极其小心

blocks.en: If you want to achieve anything great, it needs to become your one true priority. The only thing on your mind. Nobody accidently got rich. Nobody accidently built a great physique. They were obsessed with it for multiple years until they no longer had to think about it.
blocks.zh: 如果你想成就任何伟大的事业，它必须成为你唯一真正的优先事项。你满脑子想的都应该是它。没有人是意外致富的。没有人是意外练出好身材的。他们痴迷于此多年，直到不再需要刻意去想。

blocks.en: For those who need to hear it: getting rich is a perfectly viable goal. People who have a poor relationship with money will try to convince you that it isn't a meaningful way to live, but that couldn't be further from the truth. You can do great things and make great money.
blocks.zh: 给那些需要听这句话的人：致富是一个完全可行的目标。与金钱关系不佳的人会试图说服你，这不是一种有意义的生活方式，但这大错特错。你可以做伟大的事，赚大钱。

blocks.en: The fact that most people turn 23 and repeat the same 6 months for the rest of their life scared the shit out of me to the point where I would do anything to avoid that. Same city. Same bars. Same problems. They call it "living life" when it is the complete opposite.
blocks.zh: 大多数人到了23岁，就把同样的6个月重复一辈子，这一事实吓坏了我，以至于我愿意做任何事来避免那样。同一个城市。同一批酒吧。同样的问题。他们称之为“生活”，而事实恰恰相反。

blocks.en: Money is a skill that can be learned just like playing a video game, but since it's become so intertwined with status, self-worth, morality, and survival people have such a distorted view of it.
blocks.zh: 赚钱是一门可以学习的技能，就像玩电子游戏一样。但由于它与地位、自我价值、道德和生存紧密交织，人们对此的看法严重扭曲。

blocks.en: Your parents tell you to save it.
blocks.zh: 你父母告诉你要存钱。

blocks.en: Your pastor tells you to avoid it.
blocks.zh: 你的牧师告诉你要避开它。

blocks.en: Your culture tells you it's not important.
blocks.zh: 你的文化告诉你它不重要。

blocks.en: Yet most of your modern problems can only be solved by money.
blocks.zh: 然而，你现代生活中的大多数问题只能靠钱解决。

blocks.en: People have such warped perceptions of money that they become controlled by it. And since they scoff at the thought of improving themselves and making more, there's no way out.
blocks.zh: 人们对金钱的看法如此扭曲，以至于被它控制。既然他们对提升自己、赚更多钱的想法嗤之以鼻，那就没有出路了。

blocks.en: How to figure out what you want:
blocks.zh: 如何弄清楚你想要什么：

blocks.en: 1) Make a guess at what you want
blocks.zh: 1) 猜猜你想要什么

blocks.en: 2) Do everything in your power to achieve it
blocks.zh: 2) 竭尽全力去实现它

blocks.en: 3) Realize that everything you did was just a prototype
blocks.zh: 3) 意识到你所做的一切都只是原型

blocks.en: 4) Start over with more clarity on what you want
blocks.zh: 4) 带着更清晰的目标重新开始

blocks.en: Then repeat steps 2 through 4.
blocks.zh: 然后，重复第2步到第4步。

blocks.en: Probably for the rest of your life.
blocks.zh: 大概率，余生都要如此。

blocks.en: It's painful to watch young people treat youth as a currency rather than investment capital. The time, energy, and focus you have when you're young are extremely valuable and disappear fast. You're forming habits that will come back and hit you like a truck when you turn 30.
blocks.zh: 看着年轻人把青春当作可以挥霍的货币，而不是用来投资的资本，实在令人痛心。年轻时拥有的时间、精力和专注力极其宝贵，却也消失得飞快。你正在养成的种种习惯，到了30岁，会像一辆卡车一样撞向你。

blocks.en: Be careful listening to anyone who doesn’t have the life you want. Those people are rare. 1% of the population. The other 99% will blabber about how you should live your life when they’ve wasted their own. I'm sure they're kind people, but they have no idea what's best for you.
blocks.zh: 要小心，别去听那些没活成你想要的样子的人的话。那样的人很少。只占人群的1%。剩下的99%，自己把人生过废了，却会对你的人生该怎么活滔滔不绝。我确信他们都是好人，但他们根本不知道什么对你最好。

blocks.en: Your mind expands to fill the goals set for achievement.
blocks.zh: 你的心智会不断扩张，去填满你为达成目标所设定的框架。

blocks.en: You're going to miss out on 99% of the experiences life has to offer. That's just how it is.
blocks.zh: 你注定会错过人生99%的体验。事情就是这样。

blocks.en: In other words, you're not missing out on anything by focusing on a few important things.
blocks.zh: 换句话说，专注于少数几件重要的事，你并没有错过任何东西。

blocks.en: There is always more that can be done.
blocks.zh: 永远都有更多事情可以做。

blocks.en: Lost people can't figure out what to do. Drained people try to do it all. Happy people choose a few things they deeply care about and dedicate the entirety of their mental, physical, and financial energy toward that.
blocks.zh: 迷茫的人不知道做什么。精疲力竭的人试图什么都做。而快乐的人会选出几件自己真正在乎的事，把全部的心力、体力和财力都倾注其中。

blocks.en: Life is hard because you don't know what you want. That's 90% of the battle. Once you have extreme clarity on what you want, after 5-10 calculated risks, everything else is quite simple. If you can reach that before you turn 25, you're in the top 1%.
blocks.zh: 生活之所以艰难，是因为你不知道自己想要什么。这一点占了整场战役的90%。一旦你对自己想要什么有了极度的清晰，再经过5到10次深思熟虑的冒险，剩下的就相当简单了。如果你能在25岁前做到这一点，你就属于那顶尖的1%。

blocks.en: You need to believe you are better than most people.
blocks.zh: 你需要相信自己比大多数人强。

blocks.en: Not because you’re superior to them, but because what most people create isn’t that good.
blocks.zh: 不是因为你比他们优越，而是因为大多数人创造出来的东西并没有那么好。

blocks.en: If you don’t believe that you can create something at least slightly better than what is already out there – the product, the app, the writing, the designs, the photos – then you are lying to yourself, and you will never produce great work.
blocks.zh: 如果你不相信自己能做出至少比现有东西稍好一点的作品——无论是产品、应用、文字、设计还是照片——那你就是在骗自己，你也永远做不出伟大的作品。

blocks.en: Why do people who wasted their life always have the most to say about how you should live yours
blocks.zh: 为什么那些虚度了人生的人，总是对你的人生该怎么过最有话说？

blocks.en: You're always tired because you don't have a purpose, or your purpose is to complete some meaningless set of tasks that lead to a paycheck. You can sleep for 8 hours and cut out every food imaginable, but if you don't have a life trajectory you deeply care about, you will never feel the raw source of energy that makes you unstoppable even in horrible conditions.
blocks.zh: 你总是疲惫，是因为你没有目标，或者你的目标就是完成一堆毫无意义的任务，好换来一份薪水。你可以睡满8小时，戒掉一切能想到的食物，但如果你没有一条自己深深在乎的人生轨迹，你就永远感受不到那股原始的能量之源，那股让你即使在糟糕的处境下也势不可挡的能量。

blocks.en: Your life is determined by a series of 10-12 bold decisions to shift the trajectory you were given by your parents and teachers.
blocks.zh: 你的人生，由一系列10到12个大胆的决定所决定，这些决定会扭转父母和老师给你设定的轨迹。

blocks.en: If you don’t, you stall out. You wake up 10 years later wondering why your life got worse even though you’ve done everything you were told to do.
blocks.zh: 如果你不这么做，你就会停滞不前。10年后你一觉醒来，会纳闷为什么自己的人生变得更糟，明明你已经把别人教你做的事都做了一遍。

blocks.en: The best decisions you will make are the ones that everyone else will say are stupid, risky, or crazy. And they’re right. To normal people, they are, but that’s exactly why you’re doing it. You deeply understand that it’s the only way to never end up like them.
blocks.zh: 你能做出的最好的决定，恰恰是别人会说愚蠢、冒险或疯狂的那些。他们说得没错。对普通人来说确实如此，但这正是你这么做的原因。你深知，唯有如此，才不会最终变成他们那样。

blocks.en: There is no better place to be than under an immense amount of pressure from a challenge that you chose to take on.
blocks.zh: 没有什么比主动迎战一场你自愿选择的挑战、置身于巨大的压力之下更好的状态了。

blocks.en: Not for everyone, but the reason my business grew is because I made "stupid" decisions that forced me to make it work. I moved into a place 2x what I could afford so I had to make more. I got rid of everything and moved to a new state for the same reason. I've become very good at creating tactical stress: not destroying my life, but putting myself in a do or die situation knowing that there is some way to come out the other side.
blocks.zh: 这不适合所有人，但我的事业之所以能成长，正是因为我做了那些“愚蠢”的决定，逼着自己必须把它做成。我搬进了一个租金是我承受能力两倍的房子，所以我必须赚更多。出于同样的理由，我舍弃了一切，搬到了另一个州。我已经非常擅长制造战术性压力：不是摧毁自己的生活，而是把自己置于一个不成功便成仁的处境，同时心里清楚，总有办法杀出重围。

blocks.en: Most people have quietly given up.
blocks.zh: 大多数人已经悄悄地放弃了。

blocks.en: Especially young people. They don't feel in control. They don't know what to do or how to do it.
blocks.zh: 尤其是年轻人。他们觉得自己掌控不了什么，不知道做什么，也不知道怎么做。
