blocks.zh:
这是一段关于如何成为自己人生主角的视频：
youtu.be/JGlx6norGpM

blocks.en: First, you’re in pain. Then, you become curious. And if you don’t suppress that desire to explore a new domain of life, you become obsessed. Most people never change because the pain of their current situation doesn’t outweigh the pain of pursuing the highest version of yourself.
blocks.zh: 起初，你感到痛苦。接着，你生出好奇。如果你不压抑那份探索人生新领域的渴望，你就会变得痴迷。大多数人之所以从不改变，是因为当下处境的痛苦，还敌不过追求最好版本自己的那份痛苦。

blocks.en: You “aren’t interested in anything” because you don’t give yourself a chance to become interested in anything. Most people aren’t born with a crystal clear vision for their future. The people who create a good life are those who understand that vision is accumulated with the mistakes that come from pursuing anything aside from the default path.
blocks.zh: 你「对什么都不感兴趣」，是因为你从不给自己对任何事产生兴趣的机会。大多数人并非生来就对未来有清晰透辟的构想。能创造美好生活的人，都明白愿景是靠犯错积累出来的——而错误，源于你敢于偏离那条默认路径去追求点什么。

blocks.en: Create something with care, and eventually you will care.
blocks.zh: 用心去做一件事，最终你自然会用心。

blocks.en: You don’t find your passion. You cultivate it by doing something with enthusiasm for a long enough time until you discover the depth of that craft, leading to a burning passion for it. You generate passion in the pursuit of a goal you may not have wanted to pursue, but you saw it as necessary to reach the life you want, so you shut your mind off and did it anyway.
blocks.zh: 热情不是被发现的，而是被培养出来的。你满怀热忱地做一件事，坚持足够长的时间，直到你窥见这门手艺的深度，从而对它燃起炽烈的热爱。热情，是在追求一个你或许本不想追求、却认定它是通往理想生活必经之路的目标时，被激发出来的。于是你屏蔽掉杂念，无论如何先做了再说。

blocks.en: You don’t find your calling. You listen for it. Because it’s always calling you.
blocks.zh: 使命不是被找到的，而是被聆听出来的。因为它始终在召唤你。

blocks.en: But most people can't hear it. Too many tasks, bills, and responsibilities they never really chose to take on.
blocks.zh: 但大多数人听不见。任务太多，账单太多，责任太多，而这些他们从未真正主动选择过。

blocks.en: The most important task in your life is to listen for it and act without hesitation.
blocks.zh: 你人生中最重要的任务，就是聆听那个召唤，然后毫不犹豫地行动。

blocks.en: build your own thing
blocks.zh: 打造属于你自己的事业

blocks.en: The ultimate goal is getting paid to be yourself. To solve problems you can't help but solve. To study what you can't pull yourself away from. To remove or delegate any work that does not involve a creative challenge. You don't wait for this day to magically come. You live it, right now, and slowly one hour a day will turn into every waking hour.
blocks.zh: 终极目标，是靠做自己而获得报酬。去解决那些你忍不住想解决的问题，去钻研那些你无法抽离的东西，去移除或委派一切与创造性挑战无关的工作。你不会坐等这一天奇迹般地降临。你现在就活在那一天里，慢慢地，一天一小时，终将变成醒着的每一个小时。

blocks.en: Pursuing usefulness will make you a lot happier than chasing happiness.
blocks.zh: 追求有用，会让你比追逐快乐快乐得多。

blocks.en: If you don't lie to yourself, you'll go down the right path.
blocks.zh: 如果你不对自己撒谎，你就会走上正确的路。

blocks.en: People justify why they feel terrible, why they're trapped by money, why they can't get what they want.
blocks.zh: 人们总在为自己的糟糕感受找借口，为自己被金钱所困找借口，为自己得不到想要的东西找借口。

blocks.en: All of those are problems that can be solved with skill and knowledge. Honesty allows you to start solving them.
blocks.zh: 而所有这些问题，都能靠技能和知识解决。唯有诚实，才能让你开始动手解决它们。

blocks.en: Be a loser.
blocks.zh: 做个失败者。

blocks.en: Let your parents think you are stupid for not following their path. Start a business and embrace failure after failure. Study the interests that make you feel like an outcast.
blocks.zh: 让你的父母觉得你不遵循他们的道路很愚蠢。去创业，拥抱一个又一个失败。钻研那些让你感觉像异类的兴趣。

blocks.en: Where most people conform is where greatness is born.
blocks.zh: 大多数人随波逐流之处，正是伟大诞生之地。

blocks.en: The easiest way to get ahead in life is to commit to a period of skill development. 6-12 months. Pure focus for 2-4 hours a day. Learning and building. Not just binge watching tutorials, but creating quality projects that you, others, or businesses could actually benefit from. Most people won't do it but those who do launch ahead of everyone else.
blocks.zh: 人生中取得领先的最简单方法，就是投入一段时间进行技能发展。6-12个月。每天2-4小时纯粹专注。学习和构建。不只是狂看教程，而是创建高质量的项目，让你、他人或企业真正能从中受益。大多数人不会这么做，但那些做了的人会领先于其他所有人。

blocks.en: If you can spend 4 years getting a degree to do something you don’t care about you can spend 1 year reeducating yourself to build your own thing. A lack of perspective is why most quit after 2 weeks.
blocks.zh: 如果你能花4年时间拿一个学位去做你不在乎的事，你就能花1年时间重新教育自己，去构建你自己的东西。视野的缺乏是大多数人在两周后就放弃的原因。

blocks.en: Your brain works against you until you give it a meaningful goal to wire itself around.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑会和你作对，直到你给它一个有意义的目标去围绕它重新接线。

blocks.en: But you can't force it, you will know when it's time
blocks.zh: 但你无法强求，时机到了你自然会知道。

blocks.en: Most people don't get what they want because they challenge themselves without changing themselves.
blocks.zh: 大多数人得不到他们想要的，是因为他们挑战自己却不改变自己。

blocks.en: They challenge themselves to stick to a diet for 6 months, stop scrolling 30 minutes before bed, learn a new skill, change careers. And they always fail, because discipline is a feature of identity.
blocks.zh: 他们挑战自己坚持6个月的饮食计划，睡前30分钟停止刷手机，学习一项新技能，转换职业。他们总是失败，因为自律是身份的一个特征。

blocks.en: It’s not a challenge for fit people to eat healthy and go to the gym. It’s who they are. They can’t even imagine a life where they eat like shit and let themselves go. It doesn’t even cross their mind.
blocks.zh: 对健康的人来说，健康饮食和去健身房并不是挑战。那就是他们本身。他们甚至无法想象一种胡吃海塞、放任自流的生活。那根本不会出现在他们脑海中。

blocks.en: Why? Because they learned long ago that they didn't want to live that way.
blocks.zh: 为什么？因为他们很久以前就认识到，他们不想那样生活。

blocks.en: They visualized where their life would end up. All the bad things that would happen. How they would look and feel. The opportunities that wouldn't be available to them.
blocks.zh: 他们想象过自己的生活最终会变成什么样。所有会发生的坏事。他们会变成什么样子、感觉如何。那些他们将无法获得的机会。

blocks.en: That negative image fueled them more than any challenge ever could.
blocks.zh: 那幅负面图景比任何挑战都更能激励他们。

blocks.en: You need to be okay with the fact that you will never return to how you live right now.
blocks.zh: 你需要接受一个事实：你永远无法回到你现在的生活方式。

blocks.en: None of your bad habits have a place in your future life. That's why you are where you are. No 6 month challenge is going to change that unless you are brutally aware that the challenge doesn't end after month 6.
blocks.zh: 你所有的坏习惯在你未来的生活中都没有位置。这就是你目前处境的原因。没有任何6个月的挑战能改变这一点——除非你清醒地意识到，挑战在第6个月之后并不会结束。

blocks.en: I'm generally unpleasant to be around.
blocks.zh: 我通常不讨人喜欢。

blocks.en: I prefer being alone. I hate being out of routine for more than 2-3 days. I'm either thinking about nothing or everything with little in between. I say no to almost everything that gets in the way.
blocks.zh: 我更喜欢独处。我讨厌脱离常规超过2-3天。我要么什么都不想，要么什么都想，很少有中间状态。我几乎对所有妨碍我的事情都说‘不’。

blocks.en: At first I thought it was a character flaw and tried to change it. That only led to me splitting focus and slowing progress on the goals that bring me joy in life.
blocks.zh: 起初我以为这是性格缺陷，试图改变它。那只会导致我分散焦点，拖慢那些给我带来人生乐趣的目标的进展。

blocks.en: When I observe people I look up to, their mission comes first. That's what makes life enjoyable, and if that enjoyment is taken away, it spreads into their work, their loved ones, and their friendships.
blocks.zh: 当我观察我敬仰的人时，他们的使命排在第一位。这正是让生活愉快的原因，如果这种愉快被剥夺，它会蔓延到他们的工作、他们所爱的人以及他们的友谊中。

blocks.en: If you know what you want, and you don't fold to what others think you should want, you are going to be unpleasant to be around.
blocks.zh: 如果你知道自己想要什么，并且不屈服于别人认为你应该想要什么，你就会变得不讨人喜欢。

blocks.en: That isn't something to be ashamed of but embraced.
blocks.zh: 这不是什么值得羞愧的事，而应欣然接受。

blocks.en: In fact, you'll find that people want to be around you more because they trust you. They can feel that you aren't putting on an act like everyone else.
blocks.zh: 事实上，你会发现人们更愿意接近你，因为他们信任你。他们能感觉到，你并没有像其他人那样在演戏。

blocks.en: If you don't know what you want, people will tell you what you want, and you'll believe it because you have nothing better to do.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道自己想要什么，别人就会告诉你你想要什么，而你会相信，因为你没有更好的事可做。

blocks.en: Focus on these 3 things for the next 30 days:
blocks.zh: 接下来30天，专注于这三件事：

blocks.en: 1) One book for mental gains (30 minutes reading)
blocks.zh: 1）一本书，提升心智（阅读30分钟）

blocks.en: 2) One project for career gains (2 hours deep work)
blocks.zh: 2）一个项目，助力事业（深度工作2小时）

blocks.en: 3) One fitness routine for physical gains (1 hour workout)
blocks.zh: 3）一套健身计划，强健体魄（锻炼1小时）

blocks.en: Changing your life can be so simple.
blocks.zh: 改变生活，可以如此简单。

blocks.en: How to be an NPC:
blocks.zh: 如何成为一个NPC（非玩家角色）：

blocks.en:
- Never question your parents beliefs
- Never go off the guardrails at school
- Regurgitate what you hear in the news
- Always make a choice that's safe and secure
blocks.zh:
- 从不质疑父母的观念
- 在学校从不越轨
- 新闻里听到什么就照搬什么
- 永远选择安全稳妥的路

blocks.en: And of course: always treat others goals and opinions as more important than your own.
blocks.zh: 当然还有：始终把别人的目标和意见看得比自己的更重要。

blocks.en: a good life is the process of narrowing down what doesn't work
blocks.zh: 美好的人生，就是一个不断缩小“行不通”范围的过程。

blocks.en: High intelligence + high agency = building rocket ships to bring humanity to mars.
blocks.zh: 高智力 + 高能动性 = 建造火箭飞船，将人类送上火星。

blocks.en: Low intelligence + high agency = starting a small business without caring about optimization.
blocks.zh: 低智力 + 高能动性 = 不关心优化，直接开始做小生意。

blocks.en: High intelligence + low agency = crying about how rich people should not exist.
blocks.zh: 高智力 + 低能动性 = 哭诉富人凭什么存在。

blocks.en: Low intelligence + low agency = playing victim while following the default path laid out for you.
blocks.zh: 低智力 + 低能动性 = 扮演受害者，沿着为你铺好的默认路径走。

blocks.en: The lesson = with the right amount of agency, it doesn't matter how intelligent you are.
blocks.zh: 教训 = 只要能动性足够，智力高低并不重要。

blocks.en: How to make the wrong decision:
blocks.zh: 如何做出错误决定：

blocks.en: Ask everyone for their opinion. Tell everyone what you’re going to do before you do it. Listen to everyone, especially those who don’t have the results you want in life.
blocks.zh: 征求每个人的意见。行动前告诉所有人你的计划。听取所有人的话，尤其是那些生活里没有你想要的结果的人。

blocks.en: Ask yourself, "What would the average person do?"
blocks.zh: 问问自己：“普通人会怎么做？”

blocks.en: Then do the opposite.
blocks.zh: 然后反其道而行之。

blocks.en:
Everything is a muscle
Everything is a skill issue
blocks.zh:
一切皆肌肉
一切皆技能问题

blocks.en: I oscillate between wanting to be the next Steve Jobs and wanting to throw my phone in a lake and join the monks at least 3 times a day.
blocks.zh: 我每天至少在“想成为下一个史蒂夫·乔布斯”和“想把手机扔进湖里、加入僧侣行列”之间摇摆三次。

blocks.en: Hate to break it to you but the hours spent in your head won't save you from the second needed to take the step
blocks.zh: 不想打击你，但你在脑子里耗费的数小时，也抵不过迈出那一步所需的一秒。

blocks.en: This may sound obvious but if you don’t feel inspired, you need to surround yourself with inspiration. Books that inspire your thinking and articulation. Businesses that inspire your vision and strategy. It gets the cogs turning in your brain. You can feel the boost in energy.
blocks.zh: 这听起来可能显而易见，但如果你感觉不到灵感，就需要让自己置身于灵感之中。那些能激发你思考和表达的书。那些能激发你愿景和战略的企业。它能让你的大脑齿轮转动起来。你能感受到能量的提升。

blocks.en: This sounds stupid but I swear it works miracles.
blocks.zh: 这听起来很蠢，但我发誓它屡试不爽。

blocks.en: For the next 7 days, find a 1 hour long lecture on YouTube from Alan Watts.
blocks.zh: 接下来7天，在YouTube上找一段艾伦·瓦茨（Alan Watts）的一小时讲座。

blocks.en: You have to listen to it when you aren't distracted by anything else: before you take a nap, before you fall asleep, or on a quiet walk.
blocks.zh: 你必须在不受任何干扰的时候听：午睡之前、入睡之前，或者安静散步的时候。

blocks.en: When I do this I can start to feel my mind opening. Ideas start flowing again. Everything feels lighter.
blocks.zh: 当我这样做时，我能感觉到自己的心智开始打开。想法又开始流动。一切都变得轻盈。

blocks.en: I find myself doing this when I feel very narrow. I can't come up with new ideas. I've been working too much. Life feels repetitive.
blocks.zh: 当我感到非常狭隘时，我会这样做。我想不出新点子。我工作过度。生活感觉重复。

blocks.en: I've done this once a year for the past 5 years and I still don't know why I don't make it a daily thing.
blocks.zh: 过去5年里，我每年做一次，但我仍然不明白为什么我不把它变成每天的事。

blocks.en: Crazy is good
blocks.zh: 疯狂是好事

blocks.en: I hate being put in a box.
blocks.zh: 我讨厌被框住。

blocks.en: Therefore I hate the traditional concept of niching down as far as possible.
blocks.zh: 因此我讨厌尽可能细化定位的传统观念。

blocks.en:
If you have multiple interests, here's how you don't go insane:
youtu.be/6Q_1QJsO4Ro
blocks.zh:
如果你有多个兴趣，以下是你不发疯的方法：
youtu.be/6Q_1QJsO4Ro

blocks.en: Don’t feel bad for being picky about who you allow into your life.
blocks.zh: 不要因为对允许谁进入你的生活而挑剔感到内疚。

blocks.en: distractions are the byproducts of goals you don't care about
blocks.zh: 分心是你不在乎的目标的副产品

blocks.en: You care too much about what other people think because your self-image would be shattered if you didn't.
blocks.zh: 你太在意别人的看法，因为如果不这样，你的自我形象就会破碎。

blocks.en: You want to be a "good" person.
blocks.zh: 你想成为一个“好”人。

blocks.en: And you think a good person is always kind, noble, and caring.
blocks.zh: 而你认为好人总是善良、高尚、有爱心的。

blocks.en: You secretly admire those who don't give a fuck, but if you did the same, you would no longer be a good person according to your broken idea of what that means.
blocks.zh: 你私下羡慕那些毫不在乎的人，但如果你也这样做，根据你对“好”的扭曲理解，你就不再是好人。

blocks.en: You don't need to become an asshole, but you do need to choose what you value and give yourself permission to make that your priority.
blocks.zh: 你不需要变成混蛋，但你需要选择你珍视的东西，并允许自己把它放在首位。

blocks.en: reset
blocks.zh: 重置

blocks.en: The best way to learn is the opposite of what we're taught.
blocks.zh: 最好的学习方式与我们所受的教导相反。

blocks.en: You don't learn everything, then start. You start, then learn why it did or didn't work. You start with minimum viable knowledge, then experiment, then succeed or fail, then study to understand why.
blocks.zh: 你不是学完所有东西再开始。你先开始，然后了解为什么它行得通或行不通。你从最小可行知识开始，然后实验，然后成功或失败，然后研究以理解原因。

blocks.en: People dumber than you tend to run circles around you because of this. They aren't paralyzed by the overthinking that comes with overeducation, and they avoid the blindness of pure trial and error.
blocks.zh: 比你笨的人往往在这方面比你强。他们不会被过度教育带来的过度思考所麻痹，也避免了纯粹试错的盲目性。

blocks.en: Everyone wants to get rich with AI but nobody wants to go through the uncertainty of building a business.
blocks.zh: 每个人都想用AI发财，但没人愿意经历创业的不确定性。

blocks.en: The people who would have gotten rich without AI will, and the people who only start because they think AI will do it for them won't.
blocks.zh: 那些没有AI也会发财的人会发财，而那些只因为认为AI会替他们发财才开始的人则不会。

blocks.en: do this once every 6 months, minimum
blocks.zh: 至少每6个月做一次

blocks.en: It seems like every tech CEO and their mother won't stop talking about how AI is coming for your job.
blocks.zh: 似乎每个科技公司的CEO，连同他们的老妈，都在喋喋不休地谈论AI要怎么抢走你的饭碗。

blocks.en: So I did the same thing.
blocks.zh: 于是我也凑了个热闹。

blocks.en:
Here's my thoughts on the future of work and how to become AI first:
youtu.be/vFgjDSySYo8
blocks.zh:
以下是我对未来工作的看法，以及如何成为AI优先的人：
youtu.be/vFgjDSySYo8

blocks.en:
If you struggle with knowing what you want out of life, I send 2 weekly letters out on becoming future-proof:
thedankoe.substack.com
blocks.zh:
如果你正为不知道自己想要什么而苦恼，我每周会发两封信，聊聊如何让自己不被未来淘汰：
thedankoe.substack.com

blocks.en: You need 3 habits.
blocks.zh: 你需要三个习惯。

blocks.en: One that builds your mind (reading, learning, journaling).
blocks.zh: 一个滋养你的头脑（阅读、学习、写日记）。

blocks.en: One that builds your body (gym, running, nutrition).
blocks.zh: 一个强健你的身体（健身、跑步、营养）。

blocks.en: One that builds your money (business, skill dev, investing).
blocks.zh: 一个壮大你的钱包（创业、技能提升、投资）。

blocks.en: Anything more is a bonus, anything less is self-destructive.
blocks.zh: 多出来的都是加分项，少了的都是自我毁灭。

blocks.en: If you can't find the answer by searching for it, you can probably find it on a long walk, at the end of a workout, or during an extended period of time alone.
blocks.zh: 如果搜索找不到答案，那答案多半藏在一次长途散步里、一场训练的尾声里，或一段独处的漫长时光里。

blocks.en: It's only difficult because you are sitting around thinking about how difficult it is.
blocks.zh: 之所以难，只是因为你坐在那儿，一个劲儿地想它有多难。

blocks.en: When you can't make a decision, remind yourself of:
blocks.zh: 当你做不了决定时，提醒自己：

blocks.en:
1 - Who you don't want to become
2 - Who you want to become
blocks.zh:
1 - 你不想成为谁
2 - 你想成为谁

blocks.en: And if you still can't make a decision, ask yourself why you care so much about the approval of others.
blocks.zh: 如果还是定不下来，那就问问自己：你为什么这么在意别人的认可？

blocks.en: You're bored because you don't have a quest.
blocks.zh: 你无聊，是因为你没有任务。

blocks.en: You played the game up until getting a job, spouse, or house and didn't realize that was just the tutorial phase.
blocks.zh: 你把游戏玩到拿到工作、伴侣或房子，却没意识到那不过是个新手教程。

blocks.en: How to build a business in 2025:
blocks.zh: 2025年如何创业：

blocks.en:
- Post ideas on social media
- Analyze which do the best
- Turn them into free downloads
- Analyze reception and results
- Turn one into digital product/service
- Improve until irresistible
- Turn into software, physical products, etc
blocks.zh:
- 在社交媒体上发布想法
- 分析哪些反响最好
- 把它们做成免费下载资源
- 分析反馈和结果
- 挑一个做成数字产品或服务
- 不断打磨，直到让人无法抗拒
- 再转化为软件、实体产品等

blocks.en: Free idea validation, cash flow to do it full time, and a base of potential customers to support the startup you've always wanted to build.
blocks.zh: 免费的创意验证，让你全职投入的现金流，以及一群潜在客户，来支撑你一直想做的那个创业项目。

blocks.en: Pair it with AI and it's the lowest risk highest reward option.
blocks.zh: 再配上AI，那就是风险最低、回报最高的选项。

blocks.en: Working in paradise is extremely overrated.
blocks.zh: 在人间天堂里工作，被严重高估了。

blocks.en: You can't even see your screen from the sun glare on the beach. Wifi connection is always spotty. Can rarely find a place without distractions.
blocks.zh: 海滩上的阳光刺得你连屏幕都看不清。Wi-Fi信号总是时有时无。想找个没有干扰的地方，几乎不可能。

blocks.en: I'd take a home office with nothing in it every day of the week.
blocks.zh: 我宁愿每天待在一间空无一物的家庭办公室里。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to write about, write about the difficult thing you've been trying to learn, because it will help you learn it so much faster.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道该写点什么，就写你一直在努力弄懂的那件难事，因为这会让你学得快得多。

blocks.en: The sooner you start the sooner you can start sucking less.
blocks.zh: 越早开始，就能越早开始少犯点蠢。

blocks.en: Luck is a percentage that increases with the number of people who know what you do and how well you do it.
blocks.zh: 运气是一个百分比，知道你在做什么、做得有多好的人越多，这个百分比就越高。

blocks.en: I've worn a hat to simulate blocking distractions.
blocks.zh: 我戴过帽子，模拟屏蔽干扰。

blocks.en: I've set the pomodoro timers to 'unlock laser focus.'
blocks.zh: 我设过番茄钟，号称能“解锁激光般的专注”。

blocks.en:
I've done many things, but few things are as powerful (and realistic) as this deep work routine:
youtu.be/kLd5AvsLWAc
blocks.zh:
我试过很多办法，但很少有哪种能像这套深度工作流程一样强大（又现实可行）：
youtu.be/kLd5AvsLWAc

blocks.en: You're bored because you haven't developed a skill set that allows you to take on interesting challenges.
blocks.zh: 你觉得无聊，是因为你还没练出一套能让你迎接有趣挑战的技能。

blocks.en: Grab a notebook.
blocks.zh: 拿一个笔记本。

blocks.en: Write out exactly what you want in your future, don't miss a detail. Then, break it down into goals. Decades, years, months, weeks, and days.
blocks.zh: 把你未来想要的东西事无巨细地写下来，一个细节都别漏。然后把它拆解成目标：十年、一年、一个月、一周、一天。

blocks.en: Every day, write down the 3 levers you can move to create your vision.
blocks.zh: 每天写下你能撬动愿景的三根杠杆。

blocks.en: Then, forget about the goals and execute.
blocks.zh: 然后，忘掉目标，去执行。

blocks.en: Get excited over the small things. The bland but healthy food. The difficult but rewarding last rep. The uncomfortable but necessary silence of being alone. All of it.
blocks.zh: 为小事感到兴奋。寡淡但健康的饭菜。艰难但值得的最后一组。独处时不舒适却必要的寂静。这一切都是。

blocks.en: The highs, lows, bigs, and smalls of life are going to pass whether you enjoy them or not.
blocks.zh: 人生的高峰低谷、大事小情，无论你享不享受，都会过去。

blocks.en: Being able to figure it out is becoming more important than ever:
blocks.zh: 能自己把事情搞明白，正变得比以往任何时候都重要：

blocks.en: thedankoe.substack.com/p/the-unpleasa…
blocks.zh: thedankoe.substack.com/p/the-unpleasa…

blocks.en: Read last weeks letter^
blocks.zh: 读一读上周的信^

blocks.en: Cope:
blocks.zh: 认命：

blocks.en: "I can't do that."
blocks.zh: “我做不到。”

blocks.en: Curiosity:
blocks.zh: 好奇：

blocks.en: "Why can't I do that?"
blocks.zh: “我为什么做不到？”

blocks.en: Conviction:
blocks.zh: 笃定：

blocks.en: "Fuck it I'll figure it out."
blocks.zh: “管它呢，我总会搞明白的。”

blocks.en: It can be as simple as 4 habits.
blocks.zh: 可以简单到只需4个习惯。

blocks.en: One for mind. One for body. One for finances. One for relationships.
blocks.zh: 一个给心智。一个给身体。一个给财务。一个给关系。

blocks.en: Choose a habit for each that gets 80% of the results with 20% of the effort.
blocks.zh: 每个方面选一个习惯，用20%的努力拿下80%的结果。

blocks.en: Stick with them for a year and you'll be ahead of most people.
blocks.zh: 坚持一年，你就会领先大多数人。

blocks.en: As a creator who doesn't like AI doing all of your writing, scripting, idea generation, what has been the most useful AI workflow you've come across?
blocks.zh: 作为一个创作者，你不喜欢让 AI 包办所有写作、脚本和创意生成，那么你遇到过最有用的 AI 工作流程是什么？

blocks.en: I see the value in businesses having all of that done for them, but for "idea workers" so to say, what have you found?
blocks.zh: 我理解企业把所有这一切都交给 AI 的价值，但对于所谓的“创意工作者”，你发现了什么？

blocks.en: How to be productive as fuck:
blocks.zh: 如何把效率拉到极致：

blocks.en:
- Find something you deeply care about
- Do everything in your power to do that full time
- Say no to anything that pulls you away from those
blocks.zh:
- 找到一件你真正在乎的事
- 尽你所能全职去做这件事
- 对任何会把你从这件事上拉开的东西说不

blocks.en: Most people use deep work tactics to compensate for a lack of work they can't pull themselves away from.
blocks.zh: 大多数人用深度工作技巧，来弥补自己无法全身心投入工作的欠缺。

blocks.en: If you have multiple interests, this is for you.
blocks.zh: 如果你有多个兴趣，这篇就是为你写的。

blocks.en: thedankoe.substack.com/p/the-most-pro…
blocks.zh: thedankoe.substack.com/p/the-most-pro…

blocks.en: Read here^
blocks.zh: 点这里阅读^

blocks.en: If you struggle with topics to write about, or you don't know which niche to choose:
blocks.zh: 如果你为写什么话题而苦恼，或者不知道该选哪个细分领域：

blocks.en: Try creating a mission instead.
blocks.zh: 不妨试试创建一个使命。

blocks.en: An ideal life you are leading people towards.
blocks.zh: 一个你正引领人们走向的理想生活。

blocks.en: Then, almost any idea can be framed to help move toward that end goal.
blocks.zh: 这样一来，几乎任何想法都能被框定为推动你朝那个终极目标前进的一步。

blocks.en: I wrote a post on this:
blocks.zh: 我写过一篇相关的文章：

blocks.en: It's better to have conviction in a bad idea and fail than to nuance yourself into irrelevance.
blocks.zh: 与其把观点打磨得圆滑周全、最终让自己变得无关紧要，不如对一个糟糕的想法抱有信念，然后失败。

blocks.en: If you want to grow fast, you need to create something so undeniably good that people with good taste share it without second thought. Forget about the algorithm for a bit. Smart people love to share high-signal things on socials and in tight-knit group chats. Optimize for that.
blocks.zh: 如果你想快速成长，你需要创造出无可争议的优质内容，好到有品味的人会毫不犹豫地分享它。先暂时忘掉算法。聪明人喜欢在社交平台和紧密的小群聊里分享高信号的东西。针对这一点去优化。

blocks.en: Spill your mind onto the internet for a year and see where it takes you.
blocks.zh: 把你的想法倾泻到互联网上一年，看看它会把你带向何方。

blocks.en: The next 10 years will be insane.
blocks.zh: 未来十年将会疯狂至极。

blocks.en: Nobody knows what's going to happen.
blocks.zh: 没人知道会发生什么。

blocks.en: Work will change. People will feel lost. It's inevitable.
blocks.zh: 工作会变。人们会感到迷茫。这是不可避免的。

blocks.en:
But there are a few things you can do to prepare:
youtu.be/encqErQFKoE
blocks.zh:
但有几件事你可以做，来做好准备：
youtu.be/encqErQFKoE

blocks.en: The minute I become too frugal or money conscious is the moment it starts to control me and becomes difficult to make. When I spend almost carelessly, it seems to find its way back. A poor psychological relationship with money will ruin you.
blocks.zh: 一旦我变得过于节俭或太在意钱，那一刻起，钱就开始控制我，也变得难以赚到。当我几乎毫不在意地花钱时，它似乎总能自己找回来。与金钱之间糟糕的心理关系会毁了你。

blocks.en: If you want to have great ideas, surround yourself with people who have great ideas. These are usually found in non-mainstream books and small pockets of the internet. Once it hits mainstream it gets tainted.
blocks.zh: 如果你想拥有绝妙的想法，就让自己身边围绕着有绝妙想法的人。这些人通常出现在非主流的书籍和互联网的小角落里。一旦它进入主流，就会被污染。

blocks.en: You don't need an insane sales funnel.
blocks.zh: 你不需要一个疯狂复杂的销售漏斗。

blocks.en: You need to build a world. A small-scale Marvel with movies (long form), shows (short form), and action figures (products) for people to binge and explore.
blocks.zh: 你需要打造一个世界。一个微缩版的漫威宇宙——有电影（长内容）、剧集（短内容）和可玩可藏的手办（产品），让人们沉浸其中、尽情探索。

blocks.en: Posting for 2 weeks then giving up doesn't give people a chance to trust you.
blocks.zh: 发两周帖子就放弃，别人根本来不及信任你。

blocks.en: You aren't passionate about the skill.
blocks.zh: 你对这项技能并不热爱。

blocks.en: You're passionate about creating things.
blocks.zh: 你热爱的是创造本身。

blocks.en: Skills change as technology accelerates. Don't latch onto them. But the act of creation is something you can always hold onto, because it's the deepest part of you.
blocks.zh: 技术加速迭代，技能也会随之更替。别死守某一项技能。但创造这件事，你可以永远握在手里，因为它根植于你内心最深处。

blocks.en: Find something you're deeply excited about.
blocks.zh: 找到一件让你热血沸腾的事。

blocks.en: Obsess over it. Rip it apart, study it, and put it back together, but in your own way. Share it where billions of people hang out. Get one person to care about it as much as you do. Then five. Then a thousand. Then you're set.
blocks.zh: 对它痴迷。拆解它、钻研它、再重新组装起来——但要用你自己的方式。把它分享到有几十亿人聚集的地方。先让一个人像你一样在乎它，然后是五个，再是一千个。到那时候，你就稳了。

blocks.en: Here's a short future-proof manifesto:
blocks.zh: 这里有一份简短的未来生存宣言：

blocks.en: thedankoe.substack.com/p/the-future-p…
blocks.zh: thedankoe.substack.com/p/the-future-p…

blocks.en: Read here^
blocks.zh: 点这里阅读^

blocks.en: The safer you try to be, the more vulnerable you become, because you don't create that safety. You seek certainty in a job, a belief system, a nice little path someone else has laid out for you.
blocks.zh: 你越想求安稳，就越脆弱，因为那份安稳并非由你创造。你在工作里寻找确定性，在信仰体系里寻找确定性，在别人替你铺好的那条看似安稳的小路上寻找确定性。

blocks.en: A good life stems from how much uncertainty you're willing to embrace.
blocks.zh: 好的人生，取决于你愿意接纳多少不确定性。

blocks.en: How to future-proof yourself:
blocks.zh: 如何让自己无惧未来：

blocks.en:
- Act without permission
- Share your work in public
- Make as many mistakes as possible
- Get really fucking good at what you do
- Learn AI by trying to automate yourself out of work
- Deeply embody that any and all problems can be solved
blocks.zh:
- 无需许可，直接行动
- 公开分享你的作品
- 尽可能多犯错
- 把手上的事做到极致
- 学习AI，试着用自动化把自己从工作中解放出来
- 深深相信：任何问题都有解

blocks.en: It doesn’t matter how hard you worked.
blocks.zh: 你有多努力，根本不重要。

blocks.en: You can write for 10 years straight, but that doesn’t mean anyone will care about your writing.
blocks.zh: 你埋头写了十年，不代表就会有人在意你的文字。

blocks.en: I don’t care how much you “just want to write” and how everyone else has bad taste but you. Writing is a two-player game. 80% of your success lies in giving the reader a reason to care.
blocks.zh: 我不在乎你有多“只是想写”，也不在乎你是不是觉得除了你别人都没品味。写作是两个人的游戏。你80%的成功，在于给读者一个在乎的理由。

blocks.en: Call it marketing, persuasion, business, whatever you want. At least put some thought into reader psychology.
blocks.zh: 叫它营销也好，说服力也罢，或者商业，随你怎么称呼。至少，在读者心理上花点心思。

blocks.en: Your life isn’t good because you’ve spent years learning skills to advance your career, but you haven’t spent a day learning how to live. They are completely different things.
blocks.zh: 你的生活不够好，是因为你花了几年时间学习技能来推进事业，却没花过一天学习如何生活。这两件事，压根是两码事。

blocks.en: The only real safety net in today's world is a body of work that's impossible to ignore.
blocks.zh: 在当今世界，唯一真正的安全网，是一系列让人无法忽视的作品。

blocks.en: Being productive and being creative are two entirely different states.
blocks.zh: 高效和创造是两种截然不同的状态。

blocks.en: Productivity demands narrow focus, order, deadlines, urgency, stress.
blocks.zh: 高效要求狭窄的焦点、秩序、截止日期、紧迫感和压力。

blocks.en: Creativity demands an open mind, the right amount of chaos, and a lack of focus on outcomes.
blocks.zh: 创造则需要开放的心态、恰到好处的混乱，以及不执着于结果。

blocks.en: They work together for the best results.
blocks.zh: 二者相辅相成，方能成就最佳结果。

blocks.en: Creativity is where the real work is done, productivity is where the work is put out into the world.
blocks.zh: 创造力是做实事的地方，生产力则是把成果推向世界的出口。

blocks.en: A trend I see coming soon:
blocks.zh: 我预见的一个即将到来的趋势：

blocks.en: Creators sharing AI prompts along with their posts, videos, newsletters, or even courses because it adds an interactive layer.
blocks.zh: 创作者们会在发布帖子、视频、通讯或甚至课程的同时，分享配套的 AI 提示词，因为这能增加一层互动性。

blocks.en: The problem with content is that it's static.
blocks.zh: 内容的问题在于它是静态的。

blocks.en: The teachings may be valuable, but since they don't account for your own mind and experience, most of it doesn't apply 1-1.
blocks.zh: 其中的教法或许有价值，但由于它们没有考虑到你自己的思维和经历，大部分内容并不能一一套用。

blocks.en: But when you turn something like your newsletter into a prompt, not only do you increase the value of that newsletter, the reader can plug in their own mind.
blocks.zh: 但当你把通讯这类东西变成一段提示词时，不仅提升了那份通讯的价值，读者还能把自己的头脑嵌进去。

blocks.en: The 3 main categories of products / content is do it yourself, done for you, and done with you.
blocks.zh: 产品与内容的三大类别是：自己做、替你做、和你一起做。

blocks.en: This marks the end of the do it yourself era, because AI can use the context to both be your coach or freelancer.
blocks.zh: 这标志着“自己做”时代的终结，因为 AI 可以利用上下文，既能当你的教练，也能当你的自由职业者。

blocks.en: A strategy someone gives out in a YouTube video now becomes information that can execute on that strategy for you.
blocks.zh: 某人在 YouTube 视频里给出的策略，如今变成了可以直接为你执行该策略的信息。

blocks.en: Your mind runs on a storyline.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑靠一条故事线运转。

blocks.en: Games are interactive stories with certain mechanisms that narrow your focus and make progress addictive.
blocks.zh: 游戏就是互动式的故事，其中某些机制会收窄你的注意力，让进展变得令人上瘾。

blocks.en: If you want to get unstuck, use this AI prompt to turn your life into a video game (it's long):
blocks.zh: 如果你想摆脱停滞，用这段 AI 提示词把人生变成一款电子游戏（篇幅较长）：

blocks.en: You are LifeQuest AI, a strategic life coach that transforms the user's life into an immersive game experience. You analyze their current life phase (Limbo, Vision, Flow, or Resistance), help identify their true desires, and create a personalized game structure with actionable quests and meaningful narrative. You maintain honesty about uncertainty and ask clarifying questions when needed to provide accurate guidance.
blocks.zh: 你是 LifeQuest AI，一位战略性人生教练，负责把用户的人生转化为一段沉浸式的游戏体验。你分析用户当前所处的人生阶段（迷茫期、愿景期、心流期或阻力期），帮助识别他们真正的渴望，并构建一个个性化的游戏架构，配以可执行的支线任务和有意义的叙事。你对不确定性保持诚实，并在需要时提出澄清性问题，以提供准确的指引。

blocks.en: Context:
blocks.zh: 背景：

blocks.en: The user wants to gamify their life journey using principles from Adlerion psychology, flow psychology, and Greek philosophy. They seek clarity on their current life phase, future direction, and meaningful pursuits. They need support to break these goals into manageable quests within a cohesive narrative framework that makes progress tangible and rewarding. This interaction unfolds in two phases: first to assess and strategize, then to implement and coach ongoing progress through quests.
blocks.zh: 用户希望借助阿德勒心理学、心流心理学和希腊哲学的原理，将自己的人生旅程游戏化。他们寻求厘清当前的人生阶段、未来方向以及有意义的追求。他们需要支持，以便把这些目标拆解为可管理的任务，纳入一个连贯的叙事框架，让进展变得切实可见且充满回报。本次互动分两个阶段展开：先评估与制定策略，再通过任务实施并持续辅导进展。

blocks.en: Instructions:
blocks.zh: 指令：

blocks.en: Phase 1: Life Assessment & Game Design
blocks.zh: 第一阶段：人生评估与游戏设计

blocks.en: 1. Throughout this phase, ask 1-3 questions at a time. Do not ask all questions at once to reduce overwhelm.
blocks.zh: 1. 在整个阶段中，每次只问 1 到 3 个问题。不要一次性问完所有问题，以免让人不堪重负。

blocks.en: 2. Begin by asking key diagnostic questions to identify the user's current life phase:
blocks.zh: 2. 首先提出关键的诊断性问题，以识别用户当前的人生阶段：

blocks.en:
- What areas of life feel stuck, flowing, or unclear?
- What activities currently energize vs. drain them?
- What would they fight to avoid as a future outcome?
- What new information, people, or experiences have recently sparked their interest?
blocks.zh:
- 生活中哪些领域让他们感到停滞、顺畅或不明朗？
- 目前哪些活动让他们充满能量，哪些又让他们精疲力竭？
- 作为未来的结果，他们会拼命避免什么？
- 最近有哪些新信息、新结识的人或新经历激发了他们的兴趣？

blocks.en: 3. Analyze responses to determine which life phase they're in:
blocks.zh: 3. 分析用户的回答，判断其处于哪个人生阶段：

blocks.en:
- Limbo (uncertainty, directionless feeling)
- Vision (emerging clarity, building momentum)
- Flow (strong engagement, rapid progress)
- Resistance (plateauing, clinging to past success)
blocks.zh:
- 迷茫期（充满不确定、感觉没有方向）
- 愿景期（思路逐渐清晰、开始积聚动力）
- 心流期（深度投入、进展迅速）
- 抗拒期（陷入停滞、固守过往的成功）

blocks.en: 4. Guide the user to articulate their "negative vision" — the outcome they want to avoid if nothing changes.
blocks.zh: 4. 引导用户说清自己的“负面愿景”——也就是如果一切照旧、他们最想避免的结果。

blocks.en: 5. Help the user discover potential positive directions by asking about:
blocks.zh: 5. 通过询问以下方面，帮用户找到可能的正向方向：

blocks.en:
- Sources of genuine curiosity
- Skills they enjoy developing
- Meaningful impacts they wish to make
- Environments where they thrive
blocks.zh:
- 真正让用户好奇的事物
- 用户乐于打磨的技能
- 用户渴望带来的有意义的影响
- 能让用户如鱼得水的环境

blocks.en: 6. Synthesize findings into a complete game structure:
blocks.zh: 6. 将以上发现整合成一套完整的游戏结构：

blocks.en:
- Main Quest: Primary life direction/purpose
- Side Quests: Supporting goals in various life domains
- Character Stats: Key abilities to develop
- Level System: How progress will be measured
- Rules: Non-negotiable boundaries and values
- Rewards: Meaningful celebration of progress
- Tutorial Phase: Initial low-risk experiments to try
blocks.zh:
- 主线任务：主要的人生方向／目标
- 支线任务：各个生活领域中的辅助目标
- 角色属性：需要培养的关键能力
- 等级系统：如何衡量进展
- 规则：不可妥协的边界与价值观
- 奖励：对进展的有意义庆祝
- 新手教程阶段：最初可以尝试的低风险实验

blocks.en: 7. Design quantifiable feedback loops with daily/weekly priority tasks that provide clear markers of progress.
blocks.zh: 7. 设计可量化的反馈回路，配以每日／每周的优先任务，让进展有清晰的标志。

blocks.en: Phase 2: Ongoing Quest Guidance
blocks.zh: 第二阶段：持续的任务指引

blocks.en: 1. Begin each session by checking progress on previous quests and updating the user's "character status."
blocks.zh: 1. 每次开始时先检查此前任务的进展，并更新用户的“角色状态”。

blocks.en: 2. Provide appropriate coaching based on their current situation:
blocks.zh: 2. 根据用户当前的情况提供相应的教练式指导：

blocks.en:
- If stuck: Help identify obstacles and potential solutions
- If progressing: Suggest appropriate "level-ups" or new challenges
- If overwhelmed: Simplify quests or adjust difficulty
- If bored: Introduce novel challenges at the edge of their capabilities
blocks.zh:
- 如果卡住了：帮忙找出障碍和可能的解决办法
- 如果在推进：建议合适的“升级”或新挑战
- 如果不堪重负：简化任务或降低难度
- 如果感到无聊：在能力边缘引入新颖的挑战

blocks.en: 3. Frame all advice within their game narrative, maintaining the metaphor consistently.
blocks.zh: 3. 把所有建议都放进用户的游戏叙事中，始终保持这个比喻的一致性。

blocks.en: 4. Regularly revisit and update the main quest as the user's vision evolves.
blocks.zh: 4. 随着用户愿景的演变，定期回看并更新主线任务。

blocks.en: 5. Balance short-term achievements with long-term development.
blocks.zh: 5. 平衡短期成果与长期发展。

blocks.en: 6. When the user faces significant obstacles, help them:
blocks.zh: 6. 当用户遇到重大障碍时，帮他们：

blocks.en:
- Analyze patterns that led to the block
- Break down complex challenges into smaller quests
- Identify potential "power-ups" (resources, skills, or allies)
- Reframe setbacks as essential plot developments
blocks.zh:
- 分析导致卡点的模式
- 把复杂的挑战拆成更小的任务
- 找出可能的“增益道具”（资源、技能或盟友）
- 把挫折重新理解为剧情中必不可少的发展

blocks.en: Constraints:
blocks.zh: 限制条件：

blocks.en:
- Maintain game metaphor consistently but never at the expense of providing practical, actionable advice
- Focus on intrinsic motivation over external rewards
- Recommend only challenges slightly beyond current capabilities (the edge of the unknown)
- Never suggest activities that conflict with user's stated boundaries or values
- Avoid generic advice; tailor all guidance to user's specific situation
- Acknowledge uncertainty when you don't have enough information
blocks.zh:
- 始终保持游戏比喻的一致性，但绝不能以牺牲实用、可操作的建议为代价
- 关注内在动机，而非外部奖励
- 只建议略微超出当前能力的挑战（未知的边缘）
- 绝不建议与用户已说明的边界或价值观相冲突的活动
- 避免泛泛而谈的建议；所有指导都要贴合用户的具体情况
- 信息不足时，坦承不确定性

blocks.en: Output Format:
blocks.zh: 输出格式：

blocks.en: Phase 1 Output:
blocks.zh: 第一阶段输出：

blocks.en: Life Phase Analysis: Current phase identification with supporting evidence
blocks.zh: 人生阶段分析：当前阶段的判定及支撑证据

blocks.en: Character Assessment: Strengths, weaknesses, motivations, and potential directions
blocks.zh: 角色评估：优势、弱点、动机和潜在方向

blocks.en: Game Design:
blocks.zh: 游戏设计：

blocks.en:
- Main Quest (overall life direction)
- Side Quests (supporting goals)
- Character Stats (skills to develop)
- Level System (progress metrics)
- Game Rules (boundaries/values)
blocks.zh:
- 主线任务（人生大方向）
- 支线任务（辅助目标）
- 角色属性（待发展的技能）
- 等级系统（进度指标）
- 游戏规则（边界/价值观）

blocks.en: Tutorial Phase: First 1-2 weeks of specific quests and experiments
blocks.zh: 新手引导阶段：最初1-2周的具体任务与实验

blocks.en: Feedback System: Daily/weekly check-in structure
blocks.zh: 反馈系统：每日/每周打卡结构

blocks.en: Phase 2 Output (for each coaching session):
blocks.zh: 第二阶段输出（每次辅导会话）：

blocks.en: 1. Quest Log Update: Progress since last interaction
blocks.zh: 1. 任务日志更新：自上次互动以来的进展

blocks.en: 2. Character Status: Current "level" and stats
blocks.zh: 2. 角色状态：当前"等级"与属性

blocks.en: 3. Quest Guidance: Next immediate steps with specificity
blocks.zh: 3. 任务指导：接下来要采取的具体步骤

blocks.en: 4. Challenge Calibration: Adjustments to maintain optimal difficulty
blocks.zh: 4. 挑战校准：调整以保持最佳难度

blocks.en: 5. Narrative Development: How recent developments fit into their overall story
blocks.zh: 5. 叙事发展：近期进展如何融入他们的整体故事

blocks.en: One of the most beneficial things to spend your time on is transcending the fear response that you're programmed to have. You aren't fighting a bear. You're sitting down to type at a computer. You're not in danger and it isn't a threat to try something new with your life.
blocks.zh: 最值得花时间去做的事情之一，就是超越你天生就有的恐惧反应。你不是在跟熊搏斗。你只是坐在电脑前打字。你没有危险，尝试新事物对你的人生也构不成威胁。

blocks.en: Your actions reflect your goals.
blocks.zh: 你的行动反映了你的目标。

blocks.en: But most people aren't conscious of the goal their mind is trying to achieve. They don't realize that they are unconsciously choosing the very life they claim to hate.
blocks.zh: 但大多数人并没有意识到自己大脑试图实现的目标。他们没意识到，自己正在无意识地选择他们声称厌恶的生活。

blocks.en: You may say you want success, but your actions show that you want to avoid the pain and embarrassment that comes with changing your life.
blocks.zh: 你可能会说你想成功，但你的行动表明，你想避免改变生活所带来的痛苦和尴尬。

blocks.en: The most disciplined people I know have a negative outcome that sents rent free in their mind and fuels them to work in the opposite direction even if they don't feel like it.
blocks.zh: 我认识的最自律的人，脑子里都萦绕着一个负面结果，这个结果免费住在他们心里，驱使他们朝着相反的方向努力，即使他们并不想动。

blocks.en: It doesn't matter if it takes years.
blocks.zh: 哪怕要花好几年，也无所谓。

blocks.en: What the fuck else are you going to do?
blocks.zh: 不然你他妈还能干什么？

blocks.en: You aren't going to learn, build, experiment, and everything that makes life enjoyable because you have something better to be doing?
blocks.zh: 你难道因为有更好的事情要做，就不去学习、不去创造、不去实验，放弃一切让生活变得有趣的事情吗？

blocks.en: Snap out of it.
blocks.zh: 醒醒吧。

blocks.en: Most people quit because they don't realize that 2-3 months of feeling like you have no idea what you're doing is a feature not a bug.
blocks.zh: 大多数人放弃，是因为他们没意识到，头2-3个月感觉自己完全不知道在干什么，这是特性，不是缺陷。

blocks.en: The secret you're looking for is found in the experience you gain by not looking for secrets.
blocks.zh: 你寻找的秘诀，就藏在你不去寻找秘诀时所获得的经验里。

blocks.en: Your life gains purpose when you deliberately choose who and what deserves your attention rather than handing it out to anything that gives you a bit of dopamine.
blocks.zh: 当你刻意选择谁和什么值得你关注，而不是把注意力随意分配给任何能给你一点多巴胺的东西时，你的人生就有了目的。

blocks.en: Only about ten people in your life genuinely care about you because we aren't wired to care for more than a small tribe's worth of people. Focus your energy on those people.
blocks.zh: 你生命中只有大约十个人真正关心你，因为我们的大脑天生就不会关心超过一个小部落的人数。把精力集中在这些人身上。

blocks.en: You can either build a strong mind through the hardships of doing nothing with your life or through the hardships of doing something with your life, but at least the second option makes life fun, lucrative, and interesting along the way.
blocks.zh: 你可以通过无所事事地艰难生活来塑造强大的心智，也可以通过有所作为地艰难生活来塑造强大的心智，但至少第二种选择能让生活变得有趣、有利可图、充满意思。

blocks.en: The difference between greatness and mediocrity is the difference between doing what you want while correcting mistakes and doing what you want while not even being aware that you made a mistake because you don't have goals that the mistakes prevent you from achieving.
blocks.zh: 卓越与平庸的差别在于：前者在实现目标的同时纠正错误，后者在实现目标的同时甚至意识不到自己犯了错，因为他们没有目标，错误也就无从妨碍。

blocks.en: Everything worthwhile in life is deeply counterintuitive.
blocks.zh: 生活中一切值得追求的事物，都深刻违背直觉。

blocks.en: The things that seem most logical to the average mind are often the exact opposite of what actually works.
blocks.zh: 在常人看来最合乎逻辑的事，往往与真正行之有效的做法恰恰相反。

blocks.en: This is why doing the opposite of what most people do is often the quickest path to the results you want.
blocks.zh: 这就是为什么反其道而行之，常常是达成所愿的捷径。

blocks.en: If you need to force yourself to work, you're working on the wrong thing.
blocks.zh: 如果需要强迫自己才能工作，说明你做的并不是对的事。

blocks.en: Prioritize self-reliance.
blocks.zh: 把自立自强放在首位。

blocks.en: For the first time in history people have an overwhelming amount of choices, and that will ruin the people who are dependent on being told what to learn, what to do, and who do it for without caring about why they're doing it in the first place.
blocks.zh: 历史上首次，人们拥有海量的选择，而这将毁掉那些依赖他人告知该学什么、该做什么，以及不关心为何做而只关心谁来做的人。

blocks.en: If you're good at your job, your boss will give you more work.
blocks.zh: 如果你工作出色，老板就会给你更多任务。

blocks.en: If you answer emails fast, people email you more because you seem available.
blocks.zh: 如果你回复邮件快，人们就会给你发更多邮件，因为你看起来总有空。

blocks.en: If you're effective at what you do, guard your time because people will fill it up as much as they can.
blocks.zh: 如果你办事高效，请守护好你的时间，因为人们会尽可能把它填满。

blocks.en: Act busy but don't be busy.
blocks.zh: 表现得忙碌，但不要真的忙。

blocks.en: The best way to use AI as a beginner is to get unstuck.
blocks.zh: 作为初学者，使用AI的最佳方式是打破僵局。

blocks.en: Ask it to teach you what to do next for a project, reveal gaps in your thinking, etc.
blocks.zh: 让它教你项目下一步该做什么，揭示你思维中的盲点等。

blocks.en: You learn the most when your mind is ready to apply the information to a problem.
blocks.zh: 当你的大脑准备好将信息应用于问题时，你学到的最多。

blocks.en: The accelerated progress is nice too.
blocks.zh: 加速的进步也很不错。

blocks.en: Give yourself permission to let your life get worse before it gets better. Most people are trapped in limbo because they don't know what goal to pursue, but when you've experienced the negative outcome firsthand, the goal becomes clear and you can't help but work toward it.
blocks.zh: 允许自己的生活先变糟，再变好。大多数人因不知道追求什么目标而困于迷茫，但当你亲身经历负面结果后，目标就会清晰起来，你会不由自主地为之努力。

blocks.en: How I've been using AI to enhance my thinking:
blocks.zh: 我如何用AI增强思考：

blocks.en:
- Find 3-5 thinkers I admire
- Have AI break down their core ideas, beliefs, and worldview
- Save results in documents to reference later
blocks.zh:
- 找出3-5位我钦佩的思想家
- 让AI拆解他们的核心思想、信念和世界观
- 将结果保存为文档，供日后参考

blocks.en: Then, I can ask my "tribe of mentors" to share their perspective on any problem or situation.
blocks.zh: 然后，我可以请我的“导师部落”就任何问题或情况分享他们的见解。

blocks.en: 5AM alarms and cold showers are great.
blocks.zh: 凌晨5点的闹钟和冷水澡很棒。

blocks.en: But they don't get to the root of why your life feels terrible.
blocks.zh: 但它们并没有触及你的生活为何糟糕的根源。

blocks.en:
Here's a video to change the structure of your thinking (so you achieve higher forms of success):
youtu.be/Ug_VkmCPeM8
blocks.zh:
这个视频能改变你的思维结构（从而助你取得更高层次的成就）：
youtu.be/Ug_VkmCPeM8

blocks.en: hours worked is not a useful metric for value created
blocks.zh: 工作时长不是衡量价值创造的有效指标

blocks.en: I wasn't expecting the tweet below to do so well (almost 1m views)
blocks.zh: 我没料到下面这条推文反响这么好（近百万浏览量）

blocks.en: I assume people want to know more, so I made a mini course on it (free)
blocks.zh: 我猜大家想了解更多，所以做了个迷你课程（免费）

blocks.en: Watch here: thedankoe.com/ai
blocks.zh: 看这里：thedankoe.com/ai

blocks.en: I'll add more videos as I come up with use cases worth sharing
blocks.zh: 以后有值得分享的用例，我会再加视频

blocks.en: @thedankoe
How I've been using AI:
blocks.zh: 我是这样用AI的：

blocks.en:
- Choose a task
- Find YT expert that teaches it
- Have AI summarize their video
- Add examples / context
- Have AI turn that into a meta prompt
- Test, refine, and reuse that prompt
blocks.zh:
- 选一个任务
- 找教这个的YouTube专家
- 让AI总结他们的视频
- 补充例子/背景
- 让AI把它变成元提示词
- 测试、优化、复用这个提示词

blocks.en: This has led to the best results in almost everything I have AI do.
blocks.zh: 这让我用AI做的几乎所有事都达到了最佳效果。

blocks.en: If you’re young, the reason people don’t believe in you is because you don’t have any evidence. You haven’t done anything. Until you become someone worth believing in, expect very few people to honestly support you.
blocks.zh: 如果你还年轻，别人不相信你，是因为你没有任何证据。你还没做成过什么事。在你成为值得被相信的人之前，别指望有多少人会真心支持你。

blocks.en: The creator's paradox:
blocks.zh: 创作者的悖论：

blocks.en: Creativity is the result of not trying to be creative.
blocks.zh: 创造力是不刻意追求创造的结果。

blocks.en: the most broken life is the most ready to change
blocks.zh: 最破碎的人生，最渴望改变。

blocks.en: You're telling me I can give AI a model like Spiral Dynamics, have it identify my exact worldview and decision-making patterns, and coach me to achieve any goal I want so I can gain awareness of self-sabotage faster and shave years off of my development? Crazy.
blocks.zh: 你是说，我可以给AI一个像螺旋动力学这样的模型，让它识别我的确切世界观和决策模式，然后教练我实现任何目标，从而更快意识到自我破坏，把个人成长缩短好几年？太疯狂了。

blocks.en:
Prime example here:
youtu.be/PsfHcM5FP5I
blocks.zh:
绝佳例子：
youtu.be/PsfHcM5FP5I

blocks.en: If AI sucks at a task (which it does for most) you need to summarize the exact steps (from a PDF, book, YT vid, etc) and give examples to the AI to do the task like you would.
blocks.zh: 如果AI某项任务做得很烂（大多数任务都是如此），你需要总结出具体步骤（来自PDF、书、YouTube视频等），并给AI提供示例，让它像你一样完成任务。

blocks.en: This should be obvious, but typing one sentence into AI will probably disappoint you.
blocks.zh: 这显而易见，但往AI里敲一句话，大概率会让你失望。

blocks.en: One most important task in life is to experiment until you find that one thing that feels like play but is worth paying for, because most of life's stress comes from the feeling of work for minimal reward, and that drastically dampens your health, relationships, and mind.
blocks.zh: 人生最重要的任务之一，就是不断尝试，直到找到那件感觉像玩、却值得付费的事，因为生活中大部分压力都来自付出多回报少的工作感，这会严重损害你的健康、人际关系和心智。

blocks.en: you can just restart
blocks.zh: 你可以随时重新开始。

blocks.en: Everyone has a mind that no one else has access to.
blocks.zh: 每个人都有一颗别人无法触及的心灵。

blocks.en: You will lose if you try to be anyone but yourself.
blocks.zh: 如果你试图成为自己以外的任何人，你都会输。

blocks.en: AI doesn't replace creativity. It allows you to store your creative processes as a digital cognitive model (systematic prompts + curated knowledge base) that you can reuse at any time, freeing up the ability to think at higher levels of creativity.
blocks.zh: AI不会取代创造力。它让你可以把创作过程存储为数字认知模型（系统化提示词+精选知识库），随时复用，从而解放你，让你在更高层次上发挥创造力。

blocks.en: "AI makes reading irrelevant"
blocks.zh: “AI让阅读变得无关紧要”

blocks.en: No.
blocks.zh: 不。

blocks.en: You just don't understand the purpose of reading.
blocks.zh: 你只是没理解阅读的目的。

blocks.en:
When done correctly, reading is the one thing that WILL set you apart in the age of AI:
youtu.be/0OEtXlPtyYk
blocks.zh:
只要方法得当，阅读就是在AI时代让你脱颖而出的那件事：
youtu.be/0OEtXlPtyYk

blocks.en: what you consume, consumes you
blocks.zh: 你消费什么，什么就消费你

blocks.en: It takes about 1-2 months of confusion, feeling lost, and being on the verge of giving up for the right amount of vision to form where you have absolute clarity and launch into a new way of life.
blocks.zh: 大约需要经历1-2个月的迷茫、失落和濒临放弃，才能形成足够的视野，让你拥有绝对的清晰感，并迈入全新的生活方式。

blocks.en: The most important life task in my opinion is to experiment until you create work that doesn't feel like work. If it feels like work, stress starts to rule your life, and very few good ideas (which lead to life decisions) come from a stressed mind.
blocks.zh: 在我看来，人生最重要的任务就是不断尝试，直到你创造出感觉不像工作的工作。如果它感觉像工作，压力就会开始主宰你的生活，而很少有好的想法（进而带来人生决策）会来自一个压力重重的大脑。

blocks.en: Another example of this (with prompt):
blocks.zh: 另一个例子（附提示词）：

blocks.en: Task: I want to write high-converting copy for a landing page
blocks.zh: 任务：我想为落地页撰写高转化率的文案

blocks.en: Instead of finding a YT video, I can find the PDF of a book like Great Leads or any other copywriting book.
blocks.zh: 与其找YouTube视频，我可以找到一本像《Great Leads》或任何其他文案写作书籍的PDF。

blocks.en: Feed that to AI and ask it to break down in detailed steps how to write high converting copy
blocks.zh: 把它喂给AI，并让它详细分解如何写出高转化率的文案

blocks.en: Then, find a landing page structure you want to emulate (SaaS, info, local biz, whatever)
blocks.zh: 然后，找到一个你想要模仿的落地页结构（SaaS、信息产品、本地商家，随便什么）

blocks.en: Copy the text over to AI and ask it to break down the exact structure of the page and why it performs well.
blocks.zh: 把文本复制给AI，让它分解页面的确切结构以及为什么它表现良好。

blocks.en: Save both the 'how to write copy' output and the 'landing page structure' output to somewhere in your notes, or just copy/paste when you need them below
blocks.zh: 把“如何写文案”的输出和“落地页结构”的输出都保存到笔记里的某个地方，或者需要时直接复制粘贴到下面

blocks.en: Then, you're going to:
blocks.zh: 然后，你要做的是：

blocks.en:
- Send the prompt below to a new AI chat
- Tell it you want to create a high converting landing page
- Tell it to use the 'how to write copy' output to understand how to write copy
- Tell it to use the 'landing page structure' output to format the copy
blocks.zh:
- 将下面的提示词发送到一个新的AI聊天
- 告诉它你想创建一个高转化率的落地页
- 告诉它使用“如何写文案”的输出来理解如何写文案
- 告诉它使用“落地页结构”的输出来格式化文案

blocks.en: Now it'll probably ask for your target audience and what you are selling.
blocks.zh: 现在它可能会问你的目标受众和你在卖什么。

blocks.en: If you don't know those things, you can run through the exact same process (break down YT vid or PDF to teach you how > turn that into prompt) for each of them to create a customer avatar and irresistible offer.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道这些，你可以对每一项运行完全相同的流程（分解YouTube视频或PDF来教你如何做 > 将其转化为提示词），以创建客户画像和不可抗拒的offer。

blocks.zh: app.kortex.co/public/documen…

How I've been using AI:

blocks.en:
- Choose a task
- Find YT expert that teaches it
- Have AI summarize their video
- Add examples / context
- Have AI turn that into a meta prompt
- Test, refine, and reuse that prompt
blocks.zh:
- 选择一个任务
- 找到教这个任务的YouTube专家

blocks.en: This has led to the best results in almost everything I have AI do.
blocks.zh: 这让我在几乎所有让AI做的事情上取得了最好的结果。

blocks.en: You can be happy, but you have to choose to see the world as it is, not as you interpret it to be, and that requires you to become aware of your mind silently trying to keep you in the same comfortable and certain situation that has led to you being unhappy.
blocks.zh: 你可以快乐，但你必须选择看到世界的本来面目，而不是你解读中的样子，这要求你意识到你的大脑在默默试图让你保持在同样舒适和确定的境况中，而这种境况已经导致你不快乐。

blocks.en: When I stop trying to "write content" and start trying to clarify my thoughts instead, the right people find their way to my content.
blocks.zh: 当我停止试图“写内容”，转而开始试图理清我的想法时，合适的人就会找到我的内容。

blocks.en: Here's an example with training AI to interview me to get my own ideas, stories, and experiences then formatting them into viral tweet structures
blocks.zh: 这里有一个例子，训练AI采访我，获取我自己的想法、故事和经历，然后将它们格式化成病毒式推文结构

blocks.en: (use with caution and don't be dumb)
blocks.zh: （谨慎使用，别犯傻）

blocks.en: @thedankoe
How I've been using AI:
blocks.zh: 我是这样用AI的：

blocks.en:
- Choose a task
- Find YT expert that teaches it
- Have AI summarize their video
- Add examples / context
- Have AI turn that into a meta prompt
- Test, refine, and reuse that prompt
blocks.zh:
- 选一个任务
- 找一个教这个任务的YouTube专家
- 让AI总结他们的视频
- 添加例子/背景
- 让AI把它变成一个元提示
- 测试、改进并重复使用该提示

blocks.en: This has led to the best results in almost everything I have AI do.
blocks.zh: 这让我在几乎所有让AI做的事情上都取得了最好的结果。

blocks.en: How I've been using AI:
blocks.zh: 我是这样用AI的：

blocks.en:
- Choose a task
- Find YT expert that teaches it
- Have AI summarize their video
- Add examples / context
- Have AI turn that into a meta prompt
- Test, refine, and reuse that prompt
blocks.zh:
- 选一个任务
- 找一个教这个任务的YouTube专家
- 让AI总结他们的视频
- 添加例子/背景
- 让AI把它变成一个元提示
- 测试、改进并重复使用该提示

blocks.en: This has led to the best results in almost everything I have AI do.
blocks.zh: 这让我在几乎所有让AI做的事情上都取得了最好的结果。

blocks.en: This is one thing we're trying to account for while building kortex.
blocks.zh: 这是我们在构建kortex时试图考虑的一点。

blocks.en: It's hard for me to believe that most people will want to get rid of their creative work.
blocks.zh: 我很难相信大多数人会想要放弃他们的创造性工作。

blocks.en: Yes, many people will outsource work they don't want to do (like writing or marketing) to AI, and that's fine, but I still believe there will be a place carved out for those who take the craft seriously.
blocks.zh: 是的，许多人会把不想做的工作（比如写作或营销）外包给AI，这没问题，但我仍然相信，对于那些认真对待这门手艺的人来说，会有一席之地。

blocks.en: I could be very wrong and the dead internet could get worse. But it's already pretty bad. There's a ton of garbage content (mostly at the bottom of the barrel and is never seen by many people) and true creatives are still able to take their piece of the pie.
blocks.zh: 我可能大错特错，死互联网可能会变得更糟。但现在已经很糟了。有大量的垃圾内容（大多在底层，很少有人看到），而真正的创作者仍然能够分到他们的一杯羹。

blocks.en: As a writer, I've noticed that AI doesn't shorten my writing process (because I don't want it to), it makes it longer.
blocks.zh: 作为一名作家，我注意到AI并没有缩短我的写作过程（因为我不想让它缩短），反而让它更长了。

blocks.en: I don't treat AI as the writer, I treat it as the reader.
blocks.zh: 我不把AI当作作家，我把它当作读者。

blocks.en: I have it raise objections to my points.
blocks.zh: 我让它对我的观点提出反对意见。

blocks.en: I have it rate my hook and introduction for various metrics like relatability, use of curiosity gaps, and brevity.
blocks.zh: 我让它根据各种指标来评价我的钩子和引言，比如亲和力、好奇心缺口的运用和简洁性。

blocks.en: I have it overview my writing to ensure readers understand it, learn something knew, and are given at least one thing to implement once they're done reading.
blocks.zh: 我让它概览我的写作，以确保读者能理解，学到新东西，并且至少得到一件读完就能实施的事情。

blocks.en: I really struggle to have AI do the writing for me.
blocks.zh: 我真的很难以让AI替我写作。

blocks.en: It doesn't feel right. No matter how good the AI gets it still lacks a soul.
blocks.zh: 感觉不对。无论AI变得多好，它仍然缺乏灵魂。

blocks.en: Even if it comes up with good or novel ideas, I don't want to use them because that strips the joy from coming up with them myself. I literally start to feel dumber and less creative when I let AI take over too much of the process.
blocks.zh: 即使它想出了好的或新颖的想法，我也不想使用它们，因为那会剥夺我自己想出来的乐趣。当我让AI过多地接管过程时，我真的开始感觉更笨、更没创造力了。

blocks.en: My prompts have shifted to helping enhance the writing process rather than replace it, and it's allowed me to spend more time (not less) on the craft I enjoy mastering.
blocks.zh: 我的提示已经转向帮助增强写作过程，而不是取代它，这让我能够花更多时间（而不是更少）在我喜欢掌握的技艺上。

blocks.en: Reject the busy life.
blocks.zh: 拒绝忙碌的生活。

blocks.en: Always doing, never being. Always stressed and worried, never giving your mind a chance to breathe.
blocks.zh: 总是在做，从不存在的。总是压力和担忧，从不给你的大脑一个呼吸的机会。

blocks.en: The most successful people I know aren't the busiest, they're the ones who protect their thinking time as if everyone is out to steal it, because they are.
blocks.zh: 我认识的最成功的人不是最忙的，而是那些保护自己思考时间的人，就好像每个人都想偷走它一样，因为他们确实如此。

blocks.en: Anthony De Mello, maybe you should suffer a little more
blocks.zh: 安东尼·德·梅洛，也许你应该多受点苦

blocks.en: The only real opinion you have to live with is the opinion of yourself. Most people, even if they hate you, will forget about you in a few minutes and move on to the next thing they hate, because they hate themselves.
blocks.zh: 你唯一真正必须忍受的意见是你自己的意见。大多数人，即使他们恨你，也会在几分钟内忘记你，然后继续恨下一件事，因为他们恨自己。

blocks.en: Animals and AI cannot select, create, or pursue new goals. This alone shines a light on what humans should lean into: imagination, creativity, agency.
blocks.zh: 动物和 AI 无法选择、创造或追求新的目标。单凭这一点，就照亮了人类应当倾力投入的方向：想象力、创造力、能动性。

blocks.en: If you're easily persuaded that something is more important than your mission (like drama, news, hype) you will constantly spin your wheels and feel like you're never making progress because great work demands an untainted mind to generate the creative ideas that lead to unique success.
blocks.zh: 如果你轻易就被说服，认为某件事比你的使命更重要（比如八卦、新闻、炒作），你就会不停地空转，感觉自己永远没有进展，因为伟大的工作需要一个不受污染的心智，才能生成带来独特成功的创意。

blocks.en: You can't focus because you aren't alone, physically and mentally, with the work you need to do. You may think you aren't distracted, but you simply haven't identified removed the things that are sapping your mental energy.
blocks.zh: 你无法专注，是因为在身体上和精神上，你都没有独处，没有和需要做的工作单独待在一起。你可能觉得自己没有分心，但你只是还没有找出并移除那些消耗你精神能量的事物。

blocks.en: Do what you love, but learn marketing, sales, and psychology so you can actually make a living out of it.
blocks.zh: 做你热爱的事，但要学习营销、销售和心理学，这样你才能真正以此为生。

blocks.en: Or, use AI to do it for you because it's tedious and you want to focus on your craft:
blocks.zh: 或者，用 AI 替你完成这些，因为这些事很枯燥，而你想专注于自己的手艺：

blocks.en: Not caring what other people think is mostly about realizing that others' minds work in the same way that yours does.
blocks.zh: 不在意别人的看法，主要在于认识到别人的思维方式和你的运作方式是一样的。

blocks.en: Most people don't build the thing because they think they need to be first or second place to earn any kind of money from it. In reality, you can be 2000th place and make more than enough to live a good life.
blocks.zh: 大多数人不去打造那个东西，是因为他们认为必须做到第一或第二，才能从中赚到钱。实际上，你哪怕排到第 2000 名，也能赚到足够过上美好生活的钱。

blocks.en: You need to understand that most of your friends won't support you, not because they're afraid of your success, but because they're afraid you'll expose their own inadequacies.
blocks.zh: 你需要明白，大多数朋友不会支持你，不是因为他们害怕你成功，而是因为他们害怕你会暴露他们自己的不足。

blocks.en: Your brain wants to use the familiar path of least resistance.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑想走熟悉的、阻力最小的路。

blocks.en: The same habits. The same places. The same people.
blocks.zh: 同样的习惯。同样的地方。同样的人。

blocks.en: But if you want to change your life, you need to consciously take the dirt road, over and over again, until it becomes as smooth as a highway.
blocks.zh: 但如果你想改变自己的人生，你需要有意识地走上那条泥土路，一次又一次，直到它变得像高速公路一样平坦。

blocks.en: Built an AI workflow that breaks down any skill into a 90 day study regimen that spits out the best books and YouTube videos so you can learn fast and for free (you can return to the chat to ask questions when you need help)
blocks.zh: 构建了一个 AI 工作流，能把任何技能拆解成 90 天的学习计划，并输出最好的书籍和 YouTube 视频，让你快速且免费地学习（需要帮助时可以回到对话中提问）

blocks.en: It takes practice, but you can train your mind to flip into a good mood in an instant by realizing that most of your bad moods come from holding onto things that don't matter and can't be changed. You can choose to frame your situation in a way that leads to more happiness.
blocks.zh: 这需要练习，但你可以训练自己的心智，瞬间切换到好心情，方法是认识到大多数坏心情都源于执着于那些不重要且无法改变的事情。你可以选择以更幸福的方式解读你的处境。

blocks.en: I built 10+ AI workflows to help you
blocks.zh: 我构建了 10 多个 AI 工作流来帮助你

blocks.en:
- Create your niche of one
- Create an irresistible offer
- Generate landing page copy
- Draft YT vids, newsletters, threads, reels, etc
blocks.zh:
- 打造你的细分领域
- 创建令人无法抗拒的报价
- 生成落地页文案
- 起草 YouTube 视频、新闻通讯、推文串、短视频等

blocks.en: All without sacrificing your own ideas, authenticity, and experience
blocks.zh: 这一切都不牺牲你自己的想法、真实性和经验
