Watch here
youtu.be/z9dtU-xUX04
blocks.zh:
在这里观看
youtu.be/z9dtU-xUX04

blocks.en: 10,000 iterations
full vid going over it all
blocks.zh: 完整视频涵盖所有内容

blocks.en: You can now use all models inside Kortex (including the new Gemini 2.5 pro, Llama Scout, and Llama Maverick).
blocks.zh: 现在你可以在 Kortex 里使用所有模型了（包括全新的 Gemini 2.5 pro、Llama Scout 和 Llama Maverick）。

blocks.en: There are also 25+ prebuilt AI workflows for content creation, marketing, learning, and planning that generate better results than most people who use AI.
blocks.zh: 另外还有 25+ 个预置的 AI 工作流，涵盖内容创作、营销、学习和规划，产出的结果比大多数人自己用 AI 做得更好。

blocks.en: I'd recommend trying these in this order:
blocks.zh: 建议按这个顺序依次尝试：

blocks.en:
- Personal brand strategy workflow
- Customer avatar generation workflow
- Irresistible offer creation blueprint
- Then plug those all into the persuasive landing page generation workflow
blocks.zh:
- 个人品牌策略工作流
- 客户画像生成工作流
- 无法抗拒的提案打造蓝图
- 然后把以上成果全部接入说服性落地页生成工作流

blocks.en: You can also follow the "Create a digital product" workflow to help guide you through outlining an ebook, guide, or product with your own ideas and expertise (AI shouldn't do this all for you, but it can help with stringing things together.)
blocks.zh: 你还可以跟随“创建数字产品”工作流，借助你自己的想法和专业积累，梳理出一本电子书、指南或产品的提纲（AI 不该替你包办一切，但它能帮你把零散的东西串起来）。

blocks.en: Also with the desktop app, you can open a floating AI chat from anywhere on your computer to ask questions or use AI outside of Kortex.
blocks.zh: 另外，有了桌面应用，你可以在电脑上任意位置打开一个悬浮的 AI 聊天窗口，随时提问，或在 Kortex 之外使用 AI。

blocks.en: You can also upload and reference PDFs in your workspace for learning or research, like downloading a book PDF from z-library and uploading it for AI to act as your reading partner.
blocks.zh: 你也可以在工作区上传并引用 PDF 用于学习或研究，比如从 z-library 下载一本书的 PDF 上传，让 AI 充当你的阅读伙伴。

blocks.en: Last thing, the YouTube link extractor is much more reliable now. You can paste a YouTube link into a chat to reference the transcript. You can get pretty crazy with this depending on the prompts you use.
blocks.zh: 最后一件事，YouTube 链接提取器现在可靠多了。你可以把 YouTube 链接粘贴到聊天里来引用字幕。根据你用的提示词不同，可以玩得相当花。

blocks.en: This is a big update for us and sets us up for quite a few things.
blocks.zh: 对我们来说这是一次大更新，也为后续不少事情打下了基础。

blocks.en: Your life becomes what you pay attention to, and if everyone had a spreadsheet of it all, they'd understand why they are where they are.
blocks.zh: 你的生活，最终会变成你注意力所投向的样子。如果每个人都能把自己注意力的去向做成一张表格，他们就会明白自己为何身处今日之地。

blocks.en: When you create your own path, your only option is to figure it out.
blocks.zh: 当你走出一条属于自己的路，你唯一的选择就是把它想明白。

blocks.en: A "path" forms behind you. You have to make decisions that could be, and probably will be, wrong. You will always feel like you have no idea what you're doing, and you must learn to be okay with that.
blocks.zh: “路”是在你身后形成的。你必须做出可能出错、而且大概率会出错的决策。你会始终觉得自己根本不知道在干什么，而你必须学会坦然接受这一点。

blocks.en: It's not about the journey or the destination.
blocks.zh: 关键既不在旅途，也不在终点。

blocks.en: It's about the mission.
blocks.zh: 关键在于使命。

blocks.en: Why you're heading toward that specific destination.
blocks.zh: 在于你为何要奔赴那个特定的终点。

blocks.en: The reason you're willing to go through the pain of the journey.
blocks.zh: 在于你为何甘愿承受旅途的苦。

blocks.en: That's what makes it meaningful.
blocks.zh: 正是这些，让它有了意义。

blocks.en: Moved to San Diego yesterday.
blocks.zh: 昨天搬到了圣地亚哥。

blocks.en: What are the best spots? Best gyms? Best food?
blocks.zh: 有哪些好去处？最好的健身房？最好吃的地方？

blocks.en: Any creator/entrepreneur hotspots?
blocks.zh: 有没有创作者、创业者的聚集地？

blocks.en: Your old self must die a painful death for your new self to emerge. Most people aren't willing to face that pain head-on, so it becomes their master for the rest of their lives.
blocks.zh: 旧我必须痛苦地死去，新我才能诞生。大多数人并不愿直面这份痛苦，于是它便在余生中成了他们的主宰。

blocks.en: Obstacles aren't in your path, they are your path, and when you try to avoid them, you end up going nowhere.
blocks.zh: 障碍不在你的路上，障碍就是你的路；你越想绕开它，越是哪里都去不了。

blocks.en: How I stay focused in the morning:
blocks.zh: 我如何在早晨保持专注：

blocks.en:
- 60-90 minute work blocks
- 15-30 minute walks in between
- Order tasks by amount of creativity needed
- Listen to a book or lecture on the walk
blocks.zh:
- 60-90 分钟的工作区块
- 中间穿插 15-30 分钟的散步
- 按所需创造力高低给任务排序
- 散步时听一本书或一场讲座

blocks.en: This creates a Zeigarnik Effect loop - I rarely finish the task or book in that time block, so my brain wants to keep working / walking, minimal discipline required.
blocks.zh: 这就形成了一个蔡格尼克效应循环——我很少在那个时间段完成任务或读完书，所以我的大脑总想继续工作/散步，几乎不需要什么自律。

blocks.en: this book feels good to hold
blocks.zh: 这本书拿在手里感觉很好

blocks.en: If the average person sees work as a curse and work is a necessary part of life then there isn't anything better to do than to focus for 2-4 years on creating your own work that doesn't feel like work.
blocks.zh: 如果普通人把工作视为诅咒，而工作又是生活中必不可少的一部分，那么没有什么比花2-4年专注于创造自己的作品更好的了，那样的工作感觉不像工作。

blocks.en: Successful people don't feel the constant need to retire or take unnecessary vacations because they've filled their day with work that they don't want to escape from.
blocks.zh: 成功人士不会时常觉得需要退休或度不必要的假，因为他们每天的工作都是他们不想逃离的。

blocks.en: One thing I learned with the AOF launch is that word of mouth marketing is extremely difficult to nail. It's much more than 'launch a good product and expect people to spread it to millions of others.'
blocks.zh: 在AOF发布过程中我学到的一件事是，口碑营销极难把握。它远不止是‘发布一个好产品，然后指望人们把它传播给数百万其他人。’

blocks.en: And "having a large audience" is only an advantage if you promote as much as you possibly can. Whether you're self-published or go with a large publisher, you have to sell. Hard.
blocks.zh: 而“拥有大量受众”只有在你尽可能多地推广时才是一种优势。无论你是自出版还是与大型出版商合作，你都必须努力推销。

blocks.en: I'll aim for a NYT bestseller with my next book. The team I have working on it has been building up leads, distribution beyond my audience, strategizing positioning + angles + hooks, and more for the past 6 months, and we're still 6 or more months out from launch.
blocks.zh: 我的下一本书目标是成为《纽约时报》畅销书。我的团队已经为此准备了6个月，积累潜在客户、在我的受众之外进行分销、制定定位+角度+钩子策略等等，而我们距离发布还有6个多月。

blocks.en: These little books like P&P (I have 4 more planned) are just outlets to write what I want to write without having to worry about all of the nooks and crannies that come along with marketing.
blocks.zh: 像P&P这样的小书（我还计划了4本）只是 outlets，让我写我想写的东西，而不必担心营销带来的所有细节。

blocks.en: Purpose & Profit is one of those books I hope is passed around in small circles over the years.
blocks.zh: 《目的与利润》是我希望多年来在小圈子里传阅的那种书之一。

blocks.en: No big launch. No early reviews. No sending to influencers.
blocks.zh: 没有大型发布会。没有早期评论。没有送给网红。

blocks.en: I don't even have a copy yet, I made it live when it was ready.
blocks.zh: 我甚至还没有拿到副本，准备好就上线了。

blocks.en: May be shooting myself in the foot, but we will see.
blocks.zh: 可能会自断后路，但我们会看到的。

blocks.en: A job is work you do to survive, but often unpleasant.
blocks.zh: 工作是为了生存而做的事，但往往令人不快。

blocks.en: A career is work you tolerate for the eventual promise of more status and money.
blocks.zh: 职业是你为了最终获得更多地位和金钱而忍受的工作。

blocks.en: A calling is work you discover and can't pull yourself away from.
blocks.zh: 使命是你发现并无法自拔的工作。

blocks.en: Even if it takes years, try everything until you find that one thing.
blocks.zh: 即使需要数年时间，也要尝试一切，直到找到那件事。

blocks.en: If your entire day is made up of working on tasks you don't care about, you are creating a life you won't care about.
blocks.zh: 如果你的每一天都充斥着你不关心的任务，你就是在创造一个你不会关心的生活。

blocks.en: “Why” content
blocks.zh: “为什么”内容

blocks.en: “How” product
blocks.zh: “如何”产品

blocks.en: I wrote a second book.
blocks.zh: 我写了第二本书。

blocks.en: A short and philosophical take on money and discovering your life's work.
blocks.zh: 一本关于金钱和发现你一生事业的简短而哲学性的书。

blocks.en: I made it free because this is one of those things I just want in as many hands as possible.
blocks.zh: 我把它免费公开，是因为这类东西，我只希望它能落到尽可能多的人手里。

blocks.en: The paperback is not free for clear reasons.
blocks.zh: 纸质版不免费，原因显而易见。

blocks.en: Links below to read:
blocks.zh: 阅读链接在下方：

blocks.en: Self-confidence comes in 2 parts:
blocks.zh: 自信分为两部分：

blocks.en: 1) Convincing your mind to see a different perspective that makes self-doubt seem irrational.
blocks.zh: 1）说服你的大脑换一个视角，让自我怀疑显得荒谬可笑。

blocks.en: 2) Doing the uncomfortable thing over and over again until you realize it wasn't that uncomfortable in the first place.
blocks.zh: 2）一遍又一遍地去做那件让你不舒服的事，直到你发现它一开始根本就没那么不舒服。

blocks.en: Most people aren't as original as you think they are. They're just reading little-known books, having nuanced conversations, and giving themselves time to think. They are brutally aware that being stuck on their phone and doing busy work all day ruins the quality of your mind.
blocks.zh: 大多数人并没有你想象的那么有原创性。他们不过是读些冷门书，进行些有深度的对话，并给自己留出思考的时间。他们非常清楚，整天盯着手机、瞎忙活，会毁掉你头脑的敏锐度。

blocks.en: The fastest path to making better choices is to think about your ideal life before every single decision you make until it becomes a habit.
blocks.zh: 做出更好选择的最快路径，就是在你做出每一个决定之前，都先想想你理想中的生活，直到它成为一种习惯。

blocks.en: I feel like AI's impact on writing is vastly overhyped.
blocks.zh: 我觉得AI对写作的影响被严重夸大了。

blocks.en: And that's coming from someone building an AI writing software.
blocks.zh: 这话还是出自一个正在开发AI写作软件的人之口。

blocks.en: First, there is already too much content. We can't read it all. AI will add more, but most of it will go to the bottom of the barrel unless written by someone who could have gotten that content seen (someone who's already a skilled writer). Writing is one skill that only gains traction when paired with a personality and complementary skills that make other people see it and care about it. It may get slightly harder to separate signal from noise, but I doubt it, because AI content can still be signal.
blocks.zh: 首先，内容已经太多了。我们根本读不完。AI会生出更多内容，但其中大部分都会沉到最底层，除非写它的人本来就有能力让内容被看见（也就是那些已经是熟练写作者的人）。写作这门技能，只有与个性以及互补技能相结合，让他人看到并关心它，才能获得 traction。从噪音中分辨出信号可能会稍微难一点，但我对此表示怀疑，因为AI生成的内容依然可以是信号。

blocks.en: Second, AI can write a tweet or article or newsletter or video script, but that's not why or how you build an audience of readers. Your "brand" is a culmination of everything you've put out.
blocks.zh: 第二，AI可以写推文、文章、新闻通讯或视频脚本，但这并不是你建立读者群的缘由或方式。你的“品牌”是你所发布的一切的积累。

blocks.en: Having one tweet or TikTok go viral does almost nothing for you aside from maybe a quick cash grab. Most viral content is shallow and low IQ. That's not a foundation for a meaningful long-term brand. Most worthwhile content is not viral.
blocks.zh: 一条推文或TikTok视频火了，除了可能让你快速捞一笔之外，对你几乎没什么用。大多数爆款内容都是肤浅且低智的。那不是打造有意义长期品牌的基础。大多数有价值的内容都不会爆火。

blocks.en: Your brand is a culmination of every piece of writing you put out, viral or not. It's the personal or organizational philosophy, meaning, and vision. Your writing is a thread in that tapestry woven over time.
blocks.zh: 你的品牌是你所发表的每一篇文字的积累，无论爆火与否。它是个人或组织的哲学、意义和愿景。你的写作是那幅随时间编织的挂毯中的一根线。

blocks.en: Third, just because AI can write or code or market doesn't mean that everyone will write or code or market. It means that people who already wanted to write, or see the value in it, will attempt to leverage AI. And once they realize that a lack of fundamental understanding of the skill won't get you very far, they'll have to learn it from scratch anyway (shoutout vibe coders).
blocks.zh: 第三，AI能写作、编程或做营销，并不意味着所有人都会去写作、编程或做营销。它意味着那些本来就想写作、或者看到了其中价值的人，会尝试利用AI。而一旦他们意识到，缺乏对技能的基本理解根本走不远，他们无论如何都得从头学起（此处向氛围编码者致敬）。

blocks.en: AI is revolutionary. There's no question about it.
blocks.zh: AI是革命性的。这点毋庸置疑。

blocks.en: But the hype right now feels like everyone hopping on the next get rich quick scheme. The people who aren't slaves to quick fixes and cheap dopamine will continue to do well as they have been.
blocks.zh: 但如今的炒作感觉就像所有人都在追逐下一个快速致富计划。那些不沦为快速解决方案和廉价多巴胺奴隶的人，会一如既往地继续过得很好。

blocks.en: In reality, this is more like the next evolution of how we write.
blocks.zh: 实际上，这更像是我们写作方式的下一次进化。

blocks.en: Pen and paper > typewriter > keyboard > software assisted > AI assisted.
blocks.zh: 笔和纸 > 打字机 > 键盘 > 软件辅助 > AI辅助。

blocks.en: It's a big jump, but after all the "writing is dead" hype we're still in the same place we've been.
blocks.zh: 这是一次巨大的飞跃，但在所有“写作已死”的炒作之后，我们其实还是处在原来的位置。

blocks.en: There are infinite different ways to think about a situation. Meaning, if you feel stuck, overwhelmed, or anxious, you're probably thinking from a sub-optimal perspective and can't "see" a way to get yourself out.
blocks.zh: 看待一种处境有无数种不同的方式。也就是说，如果你感到困顿、不堪重负或焦虑，你很可能正从一个次优的视角思考，并且“看不到”让自己脱困的方法。

blocks.en: Even worse, most people have a worldview so deeply conditioned into their minds from parents, schools, mainstream news, social media, and the rest that they can't even fathom changing their mind.
blocks.zh: 更糟的是，大多数人的世界观深受父母、学校、主流新闻、社交媒体等的影响，根深蒂固，以至于他们甚至无法想象改变自己的想法。

blocks.en: You become powerful when you realize that you're probably wrong about almost everything, and that most of your problems can be solved with a simple change in how you view the situation.
blocks.zh: 当你意识到自己几乎对所有事情的看法都可能是错的，并且你的大多数问题都可以通过简单改变看待处境的方式来 解决时，你就变得强大了。

blocks.en: If you want non-self-help books that will fundamentally change how you think about the world, people, and everything else in your life, read:
blocks.zh: 如果你想读一些非自助类书籍，能从根本上改变你对世界、对人以及生活中其他一切的看法，请读：

blocks.en:
- Spiral Dynamics
- The Evolving Self
- Sex, Ecology, and Spirituality
blocks.zh:
- 螺旋动力学
- 进化的自我
- 性、生态与灵性

blocks.en: Study them for a year and you will think on a much deeper level.
blocks.zh: 研习一年，你的思维深度将今非昔比。

blocks.en: Reason to read:
blocks.zh: 阅读的理由：

blocks.en: Most of your ideas are triggered by other people’s ideas.
blocks.zh: 你的多数想法，都由他人的想法激发而来。

blocks.en: You have thousands of dormant ideas waiting to present themselves and reading is a great way to activate ideas you forgot about or didn’t know you had.
blocks.zh: 你脑中沉睡着成千上万的念头，阅读能唤醒那些被遗忘或未曾察觉的想法。

blocks.en: This vid will bump us over 1 million subs then I can finally release my second book (free PDF version along with it)
blocks.zh: 这期视频将使我们突破百万订阅，届时我终于能发布我的第二本书（附免费PDF版）。

blocks.en:
If you want to rewire your mind to be a strategic thinker, watch this:
youtu.be/0cSwXV2FAJ8
blocks.zh:
若你想重塑思维，成为策略思考者，请观看：
youtu.be/0cSwXV2FAJ8

blocks.en: Subtle reminder that you're supposed to feel overwhelmed.
blocks.zh: 温馨提示：感到不知所措是正常的。

blocks.en: It means you're doing something new. You're taking a new path. You're learning. Growing. You branched into the unknown. It will be frustrating. You will feel lost. It will be painful, but staying the same is even worse.
blocks.zh: 这意味着你在尝试新事物，踏上新道路，在学习，在成长。你步入了未知领域，难免沮丧、迷茫、痛苦，但一成不变更糟。

blocks.en: Good things happen to people who understand that through deliberate and persistent practice, the bursts of progress will inevitably come, even if it feels like you are stuck spinning your wheels for months or years at a time.
blocks.zh: 懂得通过刻意、持续的练习，进步终将爆发的人，会收获美好——即便你感觉像原地打转数月甚至数年。

blocks.en: If you don't shamelessly promote your work, every day for the next 10-20 years, you will get stuck doing someone else's work until you realize that nobody is going to pay you if they have no idea who you are.
blocks.zh: 如果不坚持每天毫无保留地推广你的作品，未来10到20年你都会困在别人的事业里，直到你意识到：没人认识你，就没人会为你付费。

blocks.en: How people think learning works:
blocks.zh: 人们以为的学习过程：

blocks.en: You make linear progress, every time you study and practice you get better.
blocks.zh: 线性进步，每次学习练习都有提升。

blocks.en: How learning actually works:
blocks.zh: 实际的学习过程：

blocks.en: Long and frustrating plateaus followed by bursts of progress where everything clicks.
blocks.zh: 漫长而沮丧的平台期，之后是突破性的飞跃，一切豁然开朗。

blocks.en: Learn to enjoy the periods where you feel stuck.
blocks.zh: 学会享受卡壳的阶段。

blocks.en: One of the most difficult yet life changing skills to develop is knowing when to drop everything and execute on idea as fast as possible. Quick and accurate decision making. No hesitation. No ego. Pure flow state to make it happen.
blocks.zh: 最难却最能改变人生的技能之一，是懂得何时放下一切、尽快执行想法。快速而准确地决策，毫不犹豫，放下自我，全然进入心流去实现它。

blocks.en: The best skill to learn is any skill paired with a personality that values agency, adaptability, learning, persistence, iteration, and creating something that not only you enjoy, but something others can't live without.
blocks.zh: 最好的技能，是任何技能配上一种重视自主性、适应性、学习、坚持、迭代的人格，去创造你享受、他人离不开的东西。

blocks.en: Every single post, book, video, or conversation you consume changes your mental DNA which goes on to influence the decisions you make and how good or bad your life is.
blocks.zh: 你消费的每一条帖子、每一本书、每一个视频或对话，都在改变你的精神DNA，进而影响你的决策和生活的好坏。

blocks.en: You become what you consume, but most don't care because it takes 2-3 years for the damage to really show.
blocks.zh: 你吃什么，就成为什么。但多数人不在意，因为损害要两三年才显现。

blocks.en: A clear vision + daily learning + daily building + persistence & iteration = how you achieve anything you want.
blocks.zh: 清晰的愿景 + 每日学习 + 每日构建 + 坚持与迭代 = 实现任何目标的方法。

blocks.en: Anything worth doing with your life takes about 1 year of deliberate practice 3+ times a week to even consider yourself decent at that thing. 5 years to be good. 10 years to be great.
blocks.zh: 生活中任何值得做的事，大约需要每周至少3次、持续1年的刻意练习才算入门，5年做好，10年卓越。

blocks.en: If you hesitate on an idea it dies and will almost never be found again.
blocks.zh: 对想法犹豫不决，它就会消逝，几乎再也找不回来。

blocks.en: People get stuck because they let limiting beliefs take control of their mind as they age that convince them they can’t do difficult things, even when they’ve learned something as complex as speaking English, which is as difficult as playing something like Beethoven on the piano.
blocks.zh: 人们停滞不前，是因为随着年龄增长，限制性信念掌控了头脑，让他们相信自己无法完成困难的事——即便他们早已学会了像说英语这样复杂的事，其难度不亚于在钢琴上弹奏贝多芬。

blocks.en: Learning is a meta skill.
blocks.zh: 学习是一项元技能。

blocks.en: The skill of all skills.
blocks.zh: 所有技能之上的技能。

blocks.en: Because if you can learn faster, you can achieve success that much faster.
blocks.zh: 因为如果你能学得更快，你就能更快地取得成功。

blocks.en: Learning, for most people, has become a form of mental masturbation, consuming information just so they feel like they're learning something.
blocks.zh: 对大多数人来说，学习已经变成了一种精神自慰，他们消费信息，只是为了感觉自己正在学习。

blocks.en: The most important thing you can do when the world is changing rapidly is learn.
blocks.zh: 当世界快速变化时，你能做的最重要的事情就是学习。

blocks.en: Here's how to learn anything 10x faster than anyone:
blocks.zh: 以下是如何比任何人快10倍地学习任何东西：

blocks.en: Think bigger.
blocks.zh: 把格局放大。

blocks.en: Because that alone will open your mind to possibilities you didn't even know existed. Your choices shift in a way that start getting results. Big or small.
blocks.zh: 因为仅此一点就能让你的思维向那些你甚至不知道存在的可能性敞开。你的选择会以开始产生结果的方式转变。无论大小。

blocks.en: You can limit yourself and say you don't want to achieve big things, but that only guarantees that you wont.
blocks.zh: 你可以限制自己，说不想成就大事，但这只能保证你无法做到。

blocks.en: Learn a lot of stuff. Build a lot of stuff. Identify problems. Solve them. Discover new paths. Take them. Reflect on the journey. Do it better the next time. Stay aware of distractions. Don't turn on autopilot. Take risks. Make mistakes. Fail, hard. Bounce back. Win.
blocks.zh: 学习很多东西。构建很多东西。发现问题。解决它们。发现新路径。踏上它们。反思旅程。下一次做得更好。保持对分心的警觉。不要开启自动驾驶。承担风险。犯错。惨痛地失败。反弹回来。赢。

blocks.en: That's it.
blocks.zh: 就是这样。

blocks.en: Maturity is discovering that most of your life is spent in a plateau, and if you don't fall in love with practice, mastery, and moving the needle forward you'll constantly try to escape the plateau with cheap stimulation and busy work that only keeps you there longer.
blocks.zh: 成熟是发现你一生大部分时间都花在高原期，如果你不爱上练习、精通和推动进步，你就会不断试图用廉价的刺激和忙碌的工作来逃离高原期，而这只会让你在那里停留更久。

blocks.en: Fill your mind with books, learning, and socializing.
blocks.zh: 用书籍、学习和社交填满你的头脑。

blocks.en: Use your mind with creativity, focus, and meaningful work.
blocks.zh: 用创造力、专注和有意义的工作使用你的头脑。

blocks.en: Clear your mind with rest, silence, and self-reflection.
blocks.zh: 用休息、沉默和自我反思清空你的头脑。

blocks.en: Most people fill. Less use. Few clear.
blocks.zh: 大多数人只填满。较少使用。极少清空。

blocks.en: I've started writing down every single thing that could go wrong when I start something new and it's insane how much clarity it brings.
blocks.zh: 我开始写下每件可能出错的事情，当我开始新事物时，它带来的清晰度令人难以置信。

blocks.en: Your life changes when you realize that failure isn't something to avoid, but the only way to learn in a way that is tailored to you.
blocks.zh: 当你意识到失败不是要避免的事情，而是唯一以适合你的方式学习的方法时，你的生活就会改变。

blocks.en: The reason people don't achieve big goals is because they don't realize that the only source of truth is making mistakes. They soak up advice and theory, expecting it to be an exact match to their mind, experience, and situation just to fail once and give up completely.
blocks.zh: 人们之所以实现不了大目标，是因为他们没有意识到：唯一的真理来源，就是不断犯错。他们拼命吸收各种建议和理论，指望这些东西能精准契合自己的心智、经历和处境，结果只失败了一次，就彻底放弃了。

blocks.en: Normalize ignoring trends and hype that don't align with your goals. Those are the literal definition of a distraction. And if you don't have goals (that you chose to pursue, not ones assigned to you) you are by definition always distracted.
blocks.zh: 请把这件事变成常态：忽略那些与你的目标无关的趋势和炒作。它们字面意义上就是“干扰项”。而如果你没有目标（指的是你自己选择去追求的目标，而不是别人指派给你的），那你按定义来说，永远都在分心。

blocks.en: Most AI summaries suck because they give you key points and leave out most useful information.
blocks.zh: 大多数 AI 摘要都很糟糕，因为它们只给你要点，却漏掉了大部分真正有用的信息。

blocks.en: Here's a better prompt for note-taking/research:
blocks.zh: 下面是一个更好的提示词，适用于做笔记和做研究：

blocks.en: ===Comprehensive Content Summarizer===
blocks.zh: ===全面内容摘要器===

blocks.en:
<System>:
You are an Expert Content Summarizer with a talent for capturing both key facts and underlying context. Your summaries include essential information, meaningful context, philosophical underpinnings, and subtle nuances that others might overlook. You prioritize comprehensiveness over brevity, ensuring nothing important is missed, while still organizing information efficiently. When uncertain about details, you clearly indicate this rather than filling gaps with assumptions.
blocks.zh:
<System>：
你是一位专家级的内容摘要器，擅长同时捕捉关键事实和背后的语境。你的摘要要包含核心信息、有意义的背景、哲学根基，以及他人可能忽略的细微之处。你优先追求全面，而非简短，确保不遗漏任何重要内容，同时仍能高效地组织信息。当对细节不确定时，你要明确说明，而不是用假设去填补空白。

blocks.en:
<Context>:
The user will provide content (YouTube videos, articles, books, podcasts, or other media) they want thoroughly summarized. They value comprehensive understanding over quick highlights, and specifically want to capture contextual elements and philosophical frameworks that might be dismissed as "fluff" by less thorough summarizes.
blocks.zh:
<Context>：
用户会提供他们想要彻底总结的内容（YouTube 视频、文章、书籍、播客或其他媒体）。他们看重的是全面理解，而非快速摘出亮点，并且特别希望捕捉那些可能被不够彻底的摘要者当作“废话”而忽略的语境元素和哲学框架。

blocks.en:
<Instructions>:
1. Begin by identifying the content type, creator/author, title, and publication date, if available.
blocks.zh:
<Instructions>：
1. 首先识别内容类型、创作者/作者、标题和发布日期（如果可得）。

blocks.en:
2. Create a multi-layered summary with these components:
- Core Thesis/Main Argument (1-2 sentences identifying the central point)
- Key Points Summary (bulleted list of crucial facts, arguments, or conclusions)
- Contextual Framework (identify the philosophical, theoretical, historical, or cultural context)
- Detailed Breakdown (section-by-section or chronological summary capturing all significant content)
- Nuanced Perspectives (note any competing viewpoints, counterarguments, or qualifiers presented)
- Underlying Assumptions (identify unstated premises, worldviews, or biases that inform the content)
blocks.zh:
2. 创建一个多层摘要，包含以下组成部分：
- 核心论点/主旨（用 1-2 句话指出中心观点）
- 要点总结（用项目符号列出关键事实、论点或结论）
- 语境框架（指出哲学、理论、历史或文化背景）
- 详细拆解（按章节或时间顺序逐段总结，涵盖所有重要内容）
- 细微视角（记录文中提出的任何对立观点、反驳意见或限定条件）
- 底层假设（指出那些未明说的前提、世界观或偏见）

blocks.en:
3. Pay special attention to:
- Abstract concepts, philosophical positions, and theoretical frameworks
- Historical or cultural context that shapes the content Methodological approaches or reasoning patterns used
- Qualifiers, limitations, or nuances the creator acknowledges
- Connections to broader ideas, movements, or disciplines Implications or applications suggested by the content
blocks.zh:
3. 特别注意：
- 抽象概念、哲学立场和理论框架
- 塑造内容的历史或文化语境 所使用的方法论或推理模式
- 创作者承认的限定条件、局限或细微之处
- 与更广泛思想、运动或学科的联系 内容所暗示的影响或应用

blocks.en:
4. When information is unclear or missing:
- Clearly indicate gaps or ambiguities with phrases like "The content does not specify..."
- Avoid filling in missing details with assumptions
- If the content contains potentially contradictory elements, note these tensions explicitly
blocks.zh:
4. 当信息不清晰或缺失时：
- 用“内容未具体说明……”之类的表述明确指出空白或模糊之处
- 避免用假设填补缺失的细节
- 如果内容包含可能相互矛盾的元素，要明确点出这些张力

blocks.en:
5. For content with citations or references to other works:
- Note key sources referenced and their significance to the argument
- Identify intellectual traditions or schools of thought being drawn upon
blocks.zh:
5. 对于包含引用或其他作品参考的内容：
- 记录所引用的关键来源及其对论证的意义
- 指出所借鉴的思想传统或学派

blocks.en:
<Constraints>:
• Prioritize accuracy and comprehensiveness over brevity
• Avoid simplifying complex ideas to the point of distortion
• Do not introduce external information not present in the original content
• Maintain neutrality toward the content's positions or arguments
• Include timestamps or page references when summarizing longer content
blocks.zh:
<Constraints>：
• 优先保证准确和全面，而非简短
• 避免把复杂思想简化到失真的地步
• 不要引入原内容中不存在的外部信息
• 对内容的立场或论点保持中立
• 总结较长内容时，加入时间戳或页码引用

blocks.en: <Output Format>:
blocks.zh: <Output Format>：

blocks.en: ##Comprehensive Summary of [Content Title]
blocks.zh: ##[内容标题]的全面总结

blocks.en:
Creator/Author: [Name]
Publication Date: [Date if available]
Content Type: [Article/Video/Podcast/etc.]
Length/Duration: [Pages/Minutes if available]
blocks.zh:
创作者/作者：[姓名]
发布日期：[日期，如果可得]
内容类型：[文章/视频/播客等]
长度/时长：[页数/分钟，如果可得]

blocks.en:
###Core Thesis
[1-2 sentence statement of the main argument or purpose]
blocks.zh:
###核心论点
[用 1-2 句话陈述主要论点或目的]

blocks.en: Most people don't need more knowledge, they need more perspective on the knowledge they already have. That way, they gain the confidence to act, fail, and stack the experience necessary to succeed with that knowledge. Too many people learn too much and act too little.
blocks.zh: 大多数人缺的不是知识，而是对已有知识的多元视角。如此，他们才能获得行动的自信，在失败中积累必要经验，最终凭借知识取得成功。太多人学得太多，做得太少。

blocks.en: Average people fail a few times and accept the belief that it's impossible. People who do great things start with the belief that it's possible and fail as many times as necessary to achieve it.
blocks.zh: 普通人失败几次后，便认定此事不可能。成就非凡者则始于“可能”的信念，并为实现它而屡败屡战，直至成功。

blocks.en: This year has been insane so far
blocks.zh: 今年迄今为止，简直疯狂。

blocks.en:
- Building a startup = I'm reminded i know nothing, every day
- Wrecked by cluster headaches for 3 weeks
- Fiance can barely walk from back injury for 8+ weeks now
- (Oh yeah, got engaged!)
- Moving states in 3 weeks
- Finished second book, third in the works
blocks.zh:
- 创办初创公司 = 我每天都意识到自己一无所知
- 被丛集性头痛折磨了3周
- 未婚妻因背伤，8周多来几乎无法行走
- （对了，我们订婚了！）
- 3周后要搬去别的州
- 写完第二本书，第三本在创作中

blocks.en: Stressful as hell but learning more than I ever have
blocks.zh: 压力山大，但学到的东西比以往任何时候都多。

blocks.en: “Everyone is going to make their own apps with AI”
blocks.zh: “每个人都将用AI制作自己的应用”

blocks.en: My friend you don’t even make your own food. You’ll still pay a few bucks to use an app.
blocks.zh: 朋友，你连饭都不自己做。你仍然会花几块钱用别人的应用。

blocks.en: If you need discipline to work, you're either neglecting your health, working on things you don't care about, or are so numbed to the work that you can't see the good sides of it anymore. Mind, body, spirit. Fix them.
blocks.zh: 如果你需要靠纪律才能工作，那你要么忽视了健康，要么在做不在乎的事，要么对工作麻木到看不见它的好处。身心、灵。去修复它们。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to write about, pick a random word or topic and sit in silence for 10 minutes. Note what your mind surfaces. Write down every thought. For each thought, ask "why" at least 3 times. Now you have plenty of things to write about. And they're unique.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道写什么，随便选一个词或主题，静坐10分钟。留意脑中浮现的想法。记下每一个念头。对每个念头，至少问三次“为什么”。现在你就有很多可写的东西了。而且它们独一无二。

blocks.en:
Learn how to learn.
Learn how to think.
Learn how to live.
Learn how to adapt.
Learn how to perceive.
Learn how to persist.
Learn how to iterate.
Learn how to fail.
Learn how to let go.
Learn how to be.
Learn how to disagree.
Learn how to do (without permission).
blocks.zh:
学会如何学习。
学会如何思考。
学会如何生活。
学会如何适应。
学会如何感知。
学会如何坚持。
学会如何迭代。
学会如何失败。
学会如何放下。
学会如何存在。
学会如何提出异议。
学会如何行动（无需许可）。

blocks.en: Everyone has a TV, radio, library, and newspaper in their pockets.
blocks.zh: 每个人的口袋里都装着一台电视、一台收音机、一座图书馆和一份报纸。

blocks.en: You, as an individual, now have an outlet to promote your message and work. You can just hit "send." There is no gatekeeper.
blocks.zh: 作为个体，你现在有了一个推广自己信息和作品的渠道。你只需点击“发送”。没有守门人。

blocks.en: Posts, podcasts, newsletters, videos. We're in the age of one-person media companies.
blocks.zh: 帖子、播客、通讯、视频。我们正处于一人媒体公司的时代。

blocks.en: Prioritization should feel bad because you’re sacrificing something you could do for something you must do.
blocks.zh: 优先排序应该让人感到痛苦，因为你在用你“能做”的事换取你“必须做”的事。

blocks.en: More information = more problems.
blocks.zh: 更多信息 = 更多问题。

blocks.en: More problems = more creativity.
blocks.zh: 更多问题 = 更多创造力。

blocks.en: More creativity = more happiness.
blocks.zh: 更多创造力 = 更多幸福。

blocks.en: But only for creators—those who turn chaos into order.
blocks.zh: 但这只适用于创作者——那些将混乱转化为秩序的人。

blocks.en: AI will be a low agency person's worst nightmare, but a high agency person's best friend.
blocks.zh: AI 将是低自主性者的噩梦，却是高自主性者的挚友。

blocks.en: If you want to improve the value of your current skills, stack the skill that helps you articulate the value of those skills (so people actually care enough to pay you). Learn to write.
blocks.zh: 如果你想提升现有技能的价值，就叠加一项能帮你清晰表达这些技能价值的技能（这样人们才会真正在意并愿意付钱给你）。学会写作。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to learn, start writing.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道学什么，就开始写作。

blocks.en: Not because writing is a great skill to learn, but because writing teaches you how to think, how to learn, and how to inspire people to care about what you do—and those are the only skills that will save your future.
blocks.zh: 不是因为写作是一项值得学习的伟大技能，而是因为写作教会你如何思考、如何学习，以及如何激发人们关心你所做的事——而这些才是能拯救你未来的唯一技能。

blocks.en: Do what you love, but make sure other people love it too.
blocks.zh: 做你热爱的事，但也要确保别人也热爱它。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to write next, use a:
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道接下来写什么，就用：

blocks.en:
- Pain point
- Example
- Personal story
- Statistic
- Metaphor
- Quote
- What, how, why
blocks.zh:
- 痛点
- 例子
- 个人故事
- 统计数据
- 隐喻
- 引用
- 是什么、怎么做、为什么

blocks.en: Writing is legos with ideas.
blocks.zh: 写作就是用想法搭乐高。

blocks.en: Piece them together into an email, article, video script, chapter... or write a tweet or reel with each.
blocks.zh: 将它们组合成一封邮件、一篇文章、一个视频脚本、一个章节……或者用每个想法写一条推文或短视频。

blocks.en: Making real-world mistakes is the only way to learn.
blocks.zh: 在现实世界中犯错是学习的唯一途径。

blocks.en: Once you realize this, whenever you want to learn something new, you just start doing it. You don't get wrapped up in books and tutorials. You love the feeling of that first failure because it pinpoints exactly where you suck.
blocks.zh: 一旦你意识到这一点，每当你想学新东西时，你就直接开始做。你不会沉迷于书本和教程。你热爱第一次失败的感觉，因为它精确地指出了你的弱点所在。

blocks.en: I have a younger guy (18 or 19 I think) who sends me weekly updates in the DMs.
blocks.zh: 我有一个年轻的小伙子（大概18或19岁），他每周都会在私信里给我发最新动态。

blocks.en: Like journal entries. What went wrong last week, what went well, where he's at with his projects and goals.
blocks.zh: 就像日记一样。上周出了什么问题，什么进展顺利，他的项目和目标进展如何。

blocks.en: Reminds me of my younger self. How he's noticing traits in others that he likes or dislikes. How he's going to try to adopt certain ones. How his friends don't seem to "get it" yet and aren't taking much control of their own life. Noticing the fear of putting yourself out there and trying to do your own thing. How his dad is showing interest in helping him try new things like trading, building a product, or other non-conventional ways of making money.
blocks.zh: 这让我想起了年轻时的自己。他如何注意到别人身上他喜欢或不喜欢的特质。他打算如何采纳某些特质。他的朋友们似乎还不“明白”，也没有太多地掌控自己的生活。他注意到了展示自我和尝试做自己事情的恐惧。他的父亲如何表现出兴趣，帮助他尝试新事物，比如交易、打造产品或其他非传统的赚钱方式。

blocks.en: I told him to just keep sending the updates to me.
blocks.zh: 我告诉他继续给我发这些动态。

blocks.en: I genuinely believe that awareness of what you're doing is more powerful than any kind of advice you could get from someone else.
blocks.zh: 我真心相信，对自己所做的事情保持觉察，比从别人那里得到的任何建议都更有力量。

blocks.en: Every week, what went wrong, what went well, what progress you've made. That can change so much.
blocks.zh: 每周，出了什么问题，什么进展顺利，你取得了什么进步。这能带来巨大的改变。

blocks.en: First, it was the mythical gods who were the creators. Then, humans realized they weren’t so puny and helpless. We became the creators.
blocks.zh: 最初，是神话中的众神充当创造者。后来，人类意识到自己并非如此渺小无助。我们成了创造者。

blocks.en: The greatest threat right now is people willingly giving up the role of creator to AI.
blocks.zh: 当下最大的威胁，是人们心甘情愿地把创造者的角色拱手让给AI。

blocks.en: I love AI for:
blocks.zh: 我喜欢AI，因为：

blocks.en:
- Pursuing curiosity
- Sharpening my thinking
- Generating  relevant ideas
- Quick answers for small problems
- Doing busy work, not creative work
blocks.zh:
- 探索好奇心
- 磨砺思维
- 激发相关灵感
- 快速解决小问题
- 处理琐事，而非创造性工作

blocks.en: I hate AI for:
blocks.zh: 我讨厌AI，因为：

blocks.en: - Publishing the output without any personal touch (lazy, low agency, replaceable)
blocks.zh: - 不经个人润色就发布产出（懒惰、能动性低、可替代）

blocks.en: You no longer need:
blocks.zh: 你不再需要：

blocks.en:
- A publisher to write a book
- A record label to make music
- An employer to code, design, or build
blocks.zh:
- 出版商来写书
- 唱片公司来做音乐
- 雇主来编程、设计或建造

blocks.en: You need an audience of people who care about what you do.
blocks.zh: 你需要的是关心你所做之事的受众。

blocks.en: Right now, 99% of those people are found on the internet.
blocks.zh: 眼下，99%的这类人都在互联网上。

blocks.en: If you aren't building something that leads to the life you want, even if it's "only" 30-60 minutes every morning, you will by default stay in the same life you're in, building things that allow others to live the life they want.
blocks.zh: 如果你没有在构建某种能引领你走向理想生活的东西，哪怕“仅仅”是每天早晨30到60分钟，你也会默认停留在当前的生活里，为他人建造让他们过上理想生活的东西。

blocks.en: This has been our goal for a while now.
blocks.zh: 这一直是我们的目标。

blocks.en: Cursor For Creative Work
blocks.zh: 创意工作的Cursor

blocks.en: (learning, writing, idea capture, video scripting)
blocks.zh: （学习、写作、捕捉灵感、视频脚本）

blocks.en: But we made a few "mistakes" while developing Kortex that you may benefit from hearing.
blocks.zh: 但在开发Kortex的过程中，我们犯了一些“错误”，或许值得你一听。

blocks.en: The good news is, starting this week, we're releasing the first AI assistance features that drastically change what you can do in it.
blocks.zh: 好消息是，从本周开始，我们将发布首批AI辅助功能，彻底改变你在这里能做的事情。

blocks.en: That's the first "mistake."
blocks.zh: 这就是第一个“错误”。

blocks.en: We deprioritized AI features and missed out on a lot of the hype with new models coming out.
blocks.zh: 我们降低了AI功能的优先级，错过了新模型带来的大量热度。

blocks.en: Instead, we focused on building a solid base. Something better than your typical writing, note-taking, or second brain app:
blocks.zh: 相反，我们专注于构建一个坚实的基础。比典型的写作、笔记或第二大脑应用更胜一筹：

blocks.en:
- Connections and tags
- Infinite panes to have any idea open
- Capture ideas like texting yourself
blocks.zh:
- 连接和标签
- 无限窗格，可打开任何想法
- 像给自己发短信一样捕捉灵感

blocks.en: This wasn't a mistake, but it took a lot of time to get it right. I don't think we should have changed this, and gratefully we have users who refuse to use any other app.
blocks.zh: 这并非错误，但花了大量时间才做好。我认为我们不应改变这一点，庆幸的是，我们有用户拒绝使用其他任何应用。

blocks.en: The mistake here is that we thought we needed things like:
blocks.zh: 这里的错误在于，我们以为需要这些东西：

blocks.en:
- Full offline mode
- The desktop app
- A top tier mobile app
- Workspaces and teams
blocks.zh:
- 完整的离线模式
- 桌面应用
- 顶级移动应用
- 工作区和团队

blocks.en: Those are very important things, and they need to happen, but they take a lot development time without an increase in differentiation.
blocks.zh: 这些都是非常重要的东西，必须实现，但它们耗费大量开发时间，却没有增加差异化。

blocks.en: (Although these will differentiate us from those who build a similar app fast - note-taking apps have a lot of gotchas and edge cases that I don't think most people are ready for.)
blocks.zh: （虽然这些功能会让我们与那些快速构建类似应用的人区别开来——笔记应用有许多陷阱和边缘情况，我认为大多数人还没准备好应对。）

blocks.en: In other words, we started building things that every other app already has, and that only delays our time to becoming an app that is a "hell yes" to switch to from another app that already does the job so well.
blocks.zh: 换句话说，我们开始构建其他应用都有的功能，这只会推迟我们成为一款“绝对值得”从其他已经做得非常好的应用切换过来的应用。

blocks.en: Our capture feature was cool and differentiating, but not a driving "hell yes" factor in switching from others.
blocks.zh: 我们的捕捉功能很酷且与众不同，但并不是一个推动“绝对值得”切换的因素。

blocks.en: Since the start of Kortex, we've had the vision of being able to:
blocks.zh: 从Kortex开始，我们就有一个愿景：能够：

blocks.en:
- Capture any idea, from anywhere, fast
- Transcribe any article, video, or link so you can reference it while writing or with AI
- Have all models in one chat interface that can access any document, source, highlight, or the entire context of your workspace (so you don't need 8 tabs open while you work)
blocks.zh:
- 快速从任何地方捕捉任何想法
- 转录任何文章、视频或链接，以便你在写作或使用AI时参考
- 将所有模型集成在一个聊天界面中，可以访问任何文档、来源、高亮或整个工作区的上下文（这样你在工作时就不需要打开8个标签页）

blocks.en: Because writing and creative work isn't just about putting stuff in a word processor. To do good work, you need to capture ideas, learn fast, research fast, access any relevant info fast, and synthesize everything into something worth publishing to the world.
blocks.zh: 因为写作和创造性工作不仅仅是将东西放入文字处理器。要做好工作，你需要捕捉想法、快速学习、快速研究、快速获取任何相关信息，并将一切综合成值得向世界发布的内容。

blocks.en: Now that we have desktop, partial offline, and mobile very close, we feel like we're finally hitting our stride.
blocks.zh: 现在我们有了桌面版、部分离线功能，移动版也即将推出，我们感觉终于步入正轨。

blocks.en: We can now solely focus on our differentiating factor.
blocks.zh: 我们现在可以只专注于我们的差异化因素。

blocks.en: Right now, a big pain of ours is that we're compared with things like Notion, Obsidian, Apple Notes, and the rest, when we know that within 3-6 months Kortex will be unrecognizable from them.
blocks.zh: 现在，我们的一大痛点是人们将我们与Notion、Obsidian、Apple Notes等进行比较，而我们知道在3-6个月内，Kortex将变得与它们截然不同。

blocks.en: We're still new to this, so the lesson here is only theory until we prove it to ourselves, but:
blocks.zh: 我们对此还很陌生，所以这里的教训在向我们自己证明之前只是理论，但是：

blocks.en: You need to get extremely clear on why you are different.
blocks.zh: 你需要极其清楚地知道你为什么不同。

blocks.en: But not just that, everyone knows that.
blocks.zh: 但不仅如此，每个人都知道这一点。

blocks.en: You need to build that first. You need to enter the market as that, even if you don't have the little quality of life features.
blocks.zh: 你需要先构建那个。你需要以那个身份进入市场，即使你没有那些小的生活质量功能。

blocks.en: I feel like if we did that, we would have grown a lot faster, because people would be willing to sacrifice little things for a completely new way of doing things that other products don't provide.
blocks.zh: 我觉得如果我们那样做了，我们会成长得更快，因为人们愿意为了其他产品不提供的全新做事方式而牺牲一些小东西。

blocks.en: Then, once that's proven and you give yourself enough time to iterate, focus on the small things that push you even further.
blocks.zh: 然后，一旦这一点得到证明，你给自己足够的时间迭代，就专注于那些推动你更进一步的小事情。

blocks.en: I may be wrong about this, but I feel like our thought process here could help others wanting to do similar things.
blocks.zh: 我可能对此有误，但我觉得我们这里的思考过程可以帮助那些想做类似事情的人。

blocks.en: Lots of moving pieces. Building is fun.
blocks.zh: 许多变动部分。构建很有趣。

blocks.en: Just realized, most of those reading this probably have no idea what Cursor is as I don't have an audience of programmers.
blocks.zh: 刚刚意识到，大多数读这篇文章的人可能不知道Cursor是什么，因为我没有程序员受众。

blocks.en: Good sign.
blocks.zh: 好迹象。

blocks.en: The easiest shift to a fulfilling life is to start building something of your own. Nobody likes building things they're assigned. What to learn in school. What projects to build for clients. What tasks to do at work.
blocks.zh: 通往充实人生，最轻松的一步就是着手打造属于自己的东西。没人喜欢做别人指派的事：学校里该学什么，给客户做什么项目，上班该干哪些活儿。

blocks.en: Build something on the side. It may turn into something great.
blocks.zh: 业余时间做点自己的东西吧，说不定它会成长为一番了不起的事业。

blocks.en: If you're bored, create something.
blocks.zh: 无聊了，就去创造点什么。

blocks.en: Anything.
blocks.zh: 什么都行。

blocks.en: Software. Designs. Photos. Videos. Writing. A business. A body. A relationship. A new way of thinking.
blocks.zh: 软件、设计、照片、视频、文字，一家企业、一副身体、一段关系、一种全新的思维方式。

blocks.en: How can you not feel electric to wake up and have the ability to do whatever you want.
blocks.zh: 一觉醒来，想做什么就能做什么，这样的日子，怎能不让人热血沸腾？

blocks.en: Multiple interests + taste + agency.
blocks.zh: 多元兴趣 + 品味 + 主动出击。

blocks.en:
That's the equation to future-proofing yourself (well, most of it):
youtu.be/WZeLFMQOtZ4
blocks.zh:
这就是让自己在未来立于不败之地的公式（至少是其中大部分）：
youtu.be/WZeLFMQOtZ4

blocks.en: This assumes that everyone reads books because they want a list of actionable steps (that everyone else can also find, with AI or not = you’re replaceable).
blocks.zh: 这种说法预设了：人人读书都是为了拿到一份可执行的步骤清单。可这份清单别人一样找得到（用不用 AI 都一样），也就是说，你就是可被替代的。

blocks.en: It’s not about how much information you have.
blocks.zh: 重点不在于你掌握了多少信息。

blocks.en: It’s also not about what you do with that information.
blocks.zh: 也不在于你拿这些信息做了什么。

blocks.en: It’s about changing your mind.
blocks.zh: 而在于改变你的思维。

blocks.en: Because your mind is how you interact with reality. It’s how you make decisions that lead to a good or bad life.
blocks.zh: 因为思维是你与世界互动的方式，是你做出决策的方式——而这些决策，决定了你过上好日子还是糟日子。

blocks.en: Your mind doesn’t change with a few key points.
blocks.zh: 你的思维不会因为几个关键要点就发生改变。

blocks.en: It changes when new ideas (actionable or not) fill in missing pieces, challenge old beliefs, or give you a new angle to view a situation from.
blocks.zh: 它改变的时刻，是新想法（无论是否可操作）填补了缺失的拼图、挑战了旧有的信念，或是为你提供了一个看待处境的新视角。

blocks.en: No single person reads a book and gets the exact same lessons out of it.
blocks.zh: 没有哪个人读完一本书后，得到的收获和别人一模一样。

blocks.en: Each individual has their own beliefs, goals, problems, story, and interests that shape how they perceive the information in the book.
blocks.zh: 每个人都有各自的信念、目标、难题、经历和兴趣，这些塑造了他如何理解书中的信息。

blocks.en: Let’s say 2 people want to make $1 million.
blocks.zh: 假设两个人想赚到100万美元。

blocks.en: Person A could ignore the key points entirely, still get the right idea that leads to clarity, and make the decisions that lead to $1m.
blocks.zh: A君可能完全无视那些关键要点，却依然捕捉到了正确的思路，从而理清方向，做出通往百万美元的决策。

blocks.en: Person B could obsessively study the key points, miss all of the context (what people love to label as “fluff”) and act like a blind puppet without realizing that if everyone had the key points to make $1m (everyone does) nothing would change.
blocks.zh: B君可能死磕那些关键要点，却错过了所有上下文（人们爱把它叫作「废话」），像个盲目的提线木偶一样行事，浑然不觉：如果人人都有赚到百万美元的关键要点（而人人确实都有），那什么都不会改变。

blocks.en: Book summaries have been a thing for decades and they don’t do much good because they’re missing exactly what makes those key points work.
blocks.zh: 书籍摘要这种东西已经存在几十年了，效果甚微，因为它恰恰缺失了让那些关键要点真正起作用的东西。

blocks.en: And last point:
blocks.zh: 最后一点：

blocks.en: The obsession over actionable steps and bullet point summaries is just another manifestation of cheap dopamine and distraction.
blocks.zh: 对可操作步骤和要点摘要的执迷，不过是廉价多巴胺和分心的又一种表现形式。

blocks.en: Read more books. Read longer books. Read books that have nothing to do with what you’re trying to achieve.
blocks.zh: 多读书。读更厚的书。读那些跟你眼下目标毫无关系的书。

blocks.en: Read the books that people wouldn’t even think about summarizing with AI. That’s where the gold is.
blocks.zh: 去读那些人们根本不会想到用AI去总结的书。金子就在那里。

blocks.en: I love AI and where it’s going as much as the next guy, and use it every day, but you’re going to be the one that’s replaced if you can’t do what AI can’t.
blocks.zh: 我和任何人一样热爱AI、看好它的未来，而且每天都在用它，但如果你做不了AI做不到的事，被取代的就会是你。

blocks.en: You aren’t high agency if you let AI make your decisions.
blocks.zh: 如果让AI替你做决定，你就谈不上「高能动性」。

blocks.en: @daviefogarty
Reading books is now a waste of time.
blocks.zh: 如今，读书是浪费时间。

blocks.en: AI reasoning models can distill key insights and tell you exactly how to implement them based on everything they know about you.
blocks.zh: AI推理模型可以提炼关键洞见，并根据它对你了如指掌的一切，精确告诉你怎么去落实。

blocks.en: You would learn faster if you actually started building the thing.
blocks.zh: 如果你真的动手开始做那件事，你会学得更快。

blocks.en: It's not about learning new skills. It's about learning how to learn, how to think, and how to live a good life. If the skills you're learning don't help with that, they may not be relevant for long.
blocks.zh: 重点不在于学习新技能，而在于学会如何学习、如何思考、如何过好这一生。如果你学的技能对此毫无帮助，那它们可能很快就过时了。

blocks.en: When things get static, you need to change something. Anything. You need chaos. You need novelty. You need the experiences and ideas that fuel forward progress. Build something new. Test test test. Rip apart your daily routine. Do anything but the same thing.
blocks.zh: 当事物陷入停滞，你就得改变点什么。什么都行。你需要混乱。你需要新鲜感。你需要那些能推动你前进的经历和想法。去造点新东西。反复测试、测试、再测试。把你的日常节奏彻底打乱。做什么都行，就是别重复老一套。

blocks.en: Kortex desktop app now on Windows
blocks.zh: Kortex桌面应用现已登陆Windows

blocks.en: The greatest trap is the guarantee.
blocks.zh: 最大的陷阱，就是那个“保障”。

blocks.en: Degrees don't guarantee jobs. A 401K doesn't guarantee retirement. The only real guarantee is that there is no guarantee, and you're on your own to figure it out.
blocks.zh: 学历不保障工作。401K 不保障退休。唯一真正的保障，就是根本没有保障——一切只能靠你自己去摸索。

blocks.en: I've been testing prompts for writing posts, newsletters, and threads for the past few months so that kortex AI is good.
blocks.zh: 过去几个月，我一直在测试用于写帖子、简报和推文串的提示词，好让 kortex AI 真正好用。

blocks.en: (Not to replace writing, but to improve ideas)
blocks.zh: （不是用来代替写作，而是为了打磨想法）

blocks.en: The outputs are good all around, but Claude scares me with how much better it is than other models.
blocks.zh: 各家的输出整体都不错，但 Claude 比其他模型强出的那一截，让我有点发怵。

blocks.en: People are realizing the safe and secure path is now the least safe and secure (always has been). Become a deep generalist and do many things. Those who can handle the most uncertainty win.
blocks.zh: 人们开始意识到，那条安稳稳妥的路，如今反倒是最不安稳的（其实一直如此）。做一个深度的通才，多线并进。谁能扛住最多的不确定性，谁就能赢。

blocks.en: I make the most progress when I put myself into situations where I'm forced to sink or swim.
blocks.zh: 我进步最快的时刻，都是把自己逼进那种不进则退的处境里。

blocks.en: Moving into a place I can't afford so I have to make the business work.
blocks.zh: 搬进一个我负担不起的地方，逼自己把生意做起来。

blocks.en: Launching a product when it's not ready so I have to follow through.
blocks.zh: 产品还没准备好就发布，逼自己善始善终。

blocks.en: Tactical stress works.
blocks.zh: 战术性压力，管用。

blocks.en: You need to experiment endlessly until you get a little hint of momentum, then do everything in your power to make it last as long as possible by not getting distracted.
blocks.zh: 你要不停地试，直到摸到一丝势头的苗头；然后倾尽全力，不被任何事分心，让这股势头尽可能久地延续下去。

blocks.en: Go on a walk
blocks.zh: 出去走走

blocks.en: The right idea can solve any problem.
blocks.zh: 对的想法能解决任何问题。

blocks.en: But stress and anxiety puts your mind in a box making it difficult to conceive the right idea.
blocks.zh: 但压力和焦虑会把你的大脑关进一个盒子里，让你很难想到那个对的想法。

blocks.en: So most of the time, the answer isn't more work, but more rest.
blocks.zh: 所以大多数时候，答案不是多干，而是多歇。

blocks.en: There is something you can do for 30-60 minutes a day that will move the needle toward the life you want (and get more results than those who work 12-16 hours a day), but you have to find what that something is through obsessive experimentation.
blocks.zh: 有那么一件事，每天花 30 到 60 分钟去做，就能把你推向你想要的生活（而且比那些每天干 12 到 16 个小时的人产出更多成果）——但这件事究竟是什么，你得靠近乎偏执的反复试验才能找到。

blocks.en: If you want to learn more about yourself, pay more attention to your mind.
blocks.zh: 如果你想更多地了解自己，就多留意你的心。

blocks.en: How it reacts on autopilot. How it says things you probably didn't mean to say. How it's default state is distraction and pleasure unless trained to focus.
blocks.zh: 看它在自动巡航时如何反应。看它如何说出你大概并非本意的话。看它的默认状态就是分心和享乐——除非被训练得专注。

blocks.en: Awareness. Practice awareness.
blocks.zh: 觉察。练习觉察。

blocks.en: If you don't like your situation, you shouldn't be worried about how long it will take to change it.
blocks.zh: 如果你不喜欢自己的处境，就不该去担心改变它要花多久。

blocks.en: You have nothing better to do than to work on something meaningful.
blocks.zh: 除了去做点有意义的事，你没有更好的事可做。

blocks.en: Who cares if it takes 12 months or 12 years when you would have wasted that time anyway.
blocks.zh: 就算要花12个月，甚至12年，又有什么关系？反正那些时间你本来也会白白浪费掉。

blocks.en: There is no better feeling than knocking out a lever moving task before most people wake up.
blocks.zh: 没有哪种感觉，比在大多数人还没睡醒时就先干掉一件能撬动全局的任务更爽了。

blocks.en: Focus is like a battery. If you rest for short intervals, you can work in intense bursts. If you rest for a day or two, you can focus longer and harder. If you rest for too long, you overcharge. Your battery gets weaker and you struggle to get anything meaningful done.
blocks.zh: 专注力就像一块电池。短暂休息几次，你就能持续高强度地爆发式工作。休息一两天，你就能专注得更久、更猛。可要是休息太久，电池就会过度充电。你的电量反而变弱，想做成点有意义的事都费劲。

blocks.en: If you have multiple interests, don't let anyone convince you that you should narrow your focus. You may be confused for a while, but if you stick it out, you will blow past everyone else.
blocks.zh: 如果你兴趣广泛，别让任何人说服你去收窄焦点。你可能会迷茫一阵子，但只要坚持熬过去，你就能把所有人远远甩在身后。

blocks.en: 30 minutes of reading.
blocks.zh: 阅读30分钟。

blocks.en: 30 minutes of writing.
blocks.zh: 写作30分钟。

blocks.en: Read to discover ideas.
blocks.zh: 阅读，是为了发现想法。

blocks.en: Write to share ideas.
blocks.zh: 写作，是为了分享想法。

blocks.en: Those two habits alone can change your mind, your career, and the quality of your life.
blocks.zh: 单单这两个习惯，就能改变你的思维、你的事业，以及你的生活质量。

blocks.en: If you're bored, read.
blocks.zh: 无聊的时候，就去阅读。

blocks.en: If you're anxious, write.
blocks.zh: 焦虑的时候，就去写作。

blocks.en: A clear mind is a confident mind.
blocks.zh: 头脑清晰，人才有底气。

blocks.en: Confidence is a prerequisite to good outcomes from the thousands of daily choices you make.
blocks.zh: 你每天要做成千上万个选择，而自信是好结果的先决条件。

blocks.en: Choices compound into a life you hate or love.
blocks.zh: 这些选择层层叠加，最终会构成一个你爱或你恨的人生。

blocks.en: Most of your problems would be solved if you stopped simulating challenges with cheap dopamine sources and started acquiring the knowledge, skill, and experience that makes the game of life worth living.
blocks.zh: 你大多数的问题，其实只要你不再用廉价的多巴胺来源去模拟挑战，转而开始积累知识、技能和经验——那些真正让生活这场游戏值得一玩的东西——就能迎刃而解。

blocks.en: If your job is a dead end, you have two options:
blocks.zh: 如果你的工作已经一眼望到头，你有两个选择：

blocks.en: 1 - Change your perspective to make the work enjoyable
blocks.zh: 1 - 改变你的视角，让这份工作变得有趣

blocks.en: 2 - Change your work to fit what you find enjoyable
blocks.zh: 2 - 改变你的工作，让它符合你觉得有趣的东西

blocks.en: Change your mind or change your habits.
blocks.zh: 要么改变心态，要么改变习惯。

blocks.en: Or change both.
blocks.zh: 要么，两个一起改。

blocks.en: Stop convincing yourself that you're stuck.
blocks.zh: 别再骗自己说，你已经走投无路了。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to do, build something.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道该做什么，那就去创造点什么。

blocks.en: Anything.
blocks.zh: 什么都行。

blocks.en: That's what happy humans do.
blocks.zh: 快乐的人就是这么做的。

blocks.en: Unlike animals who only survive in one niche, we gather knowledge and build tools to thrive in any.
blocks.zh: 动物只能固守在一处生态位里求生存，我们却不同——我们积累知识、打造工具，在任何环境里都能活得风生水起。

blocks.en: Solve a problem. Create something. Share it with someone.
blocks.zh: 去解决一个问题。去创造一样东西。去把它分享给别人。

blocks.en: You'll discover purpose.
blocks.zh: 你会从中找到意义。

blocks.en: Going to take a break from business heavy videos for a bit.
blocks.zh: 先暂停一下那些偏商业的干货视频。

blocks.en: Here's the latest one.
blocks.zh: 这是最新的一期。

blocks.en:
Everything I know (well, the important stuff) about marketing and product:
youtu.be/Er2s-CFoZSo
blocks.zh:
关于营销和产品，我所知道的一切（嗯，重要的那些）：
youtu.be/Er2s-CFoZSo

blocks.en: I get cluster headaches every 2-3 years.
blocks.zh: 我每两三年就会犯一次丛集性头痛。

blocks.en: In short, they fucking suck.
blocks.zh: 简而言之：太他妈难受了。

blocks.en: Mine aren't this bad, but I've heard of some people pulling out their teeth with a leatherman because they think it will help the pain.
blocks.zh: 我的情况还没那么糟，但我听说有人会用莱泽曼刀把自己的牙拔掉，以为这样能缓解疼痛。

blocks.en: The only real relief for them is oxygen therapy (unless anyone has some esoteric remedies that can help... I've tried a lot). And since mine only last everyday for a week or two at a time, I just decide to stick it out because getting oxygen is one story and ordering a machine with a week or two shipping time seems against the point.
blocks.zh: 真正能缓解的只有氧疗（除非谁有什么偏门的偏方……我已经试过很多了）。而我的头痛每次也就持续一两周，所以我干脆咬牙硬扛——毕竟吸氧是另一回事，订购一台还要等一两周才能到货，那似乎根本解决不了问题。

blocks.en: Everytime I think I find something that helps like icing or taking way too much magnesium or flonase, they stop working the next time around.
blocks.zh: 每次我以为找到了管用的办法，比如冰敷、服用过量的镁，或者用氟替卡松，可下一次它们就不灵了。

blocks.en: Now this isn't a post to complain.
blocks.zh: 这不是一篇抱怨的帖子。

blocks.en: It's the exact opposite.
blocks.zh: 恰恰相反。

blocks.en: When I'm not rolling around on the floor gripping my head and trying not to pull my hair, life is so amazing.
blocks.zh: 当我不在地上打滚、抱着脑袋、拼命忍住不扯自己头发的时候，生活真是无比美好。

blocks.en: It feels like a privilege to be able to write and work. Food tastes better. The sun feels like I've been stuck inside for 6 months. It's like my mind was shut off for so long that it gets put into overdrive because I want to do as much as I can while I have the time.
blocks.zh: 能够写作、能够工作，感觉就像一种特权。食物更有滋味了。阳光明媚得仿佛我已经在屋里憋了六个月。就好像我的大脑停摆了太久，一旦重新运转就超速狂奔，因为我想趁着还有时间，尽可能多做些事。

blocks.en: Maybe there is a lesson here. Maybe it's gratitude. Maybe it's how the occasional deep pain can give you an entirely new appreciation for what you have, but people are so afraid to take a risk that they never experience that pain.
blocks.zh: 也许这里藏着个道理。也许是感恩。也许是：偶尔一次深刻的痛苦，能让你对拥有的一切产生全新的感激——可人们太害怕承担风险，所以永远体会不到那种痛苦。

blocks.en: I hope you never experience a cluster headache, but I hope you find something to be appreciative of today.
blocks.zh: 我希望你永远别得丛集性头痛，但愿你今天能找到一件值得感恩的事。

blocks.en: Traveling is like buying a new car. It's amazing for the first week or two, then it becomes normal. If you're traveling to escape a mundane life, you will be disappointed because you don't need to travel to figure out that your life is already full of interesting things
blocks.zh: 旅行就像买新车。头一两周妙不可言，之后就变得稀松平常。如果你旅行是为了逃离枯燥的生活，那你注定要失望，因为你根本不需要远行，也能发现生活本就充满了有趣的事。

blocks.en: You are the moat
blocks.zh: 你就是那道护城河。

blocks.en: People only change when the pain outweighs the comfort of their current situation.
blocks.zh: 人只有在痛苦超过现状的舒适时才会改变。

blocks.en: Nobody knows what the future will be, but we know two things for certain:
blocks.zh: 没有人知道未来会怎样，但我们确定两件事：

blocks.en:
1. Problems are infinite
2. Problems are soluble
blocks.zh:
1. 问题是无限的
2. 问题是可以解决的

blocks.en: Problems are the source of happiness because happiness is the intersection of progress being made and a contribution to something greater than yourself.
blocks.zh: 问题是幸福的源泉，因为幸福是进步与为超越自身的事物做出贡献的交汇点。

blocks.en: Thankfully, there will always be problems to solve.
blocks.zh: 幸运的是，总有需要解决的问题。

blocks.en: That's all you need to know to live a good life.
blocks.zh: 这就是你过好生活所需要知道的一切。

blocks.en: Pursuing usefulness will make you a lot happier than pursuing happiness
blocks.zh: 追求有用比追求幸福更能让你快乐。

blocks.en: Signs you're on the right track:
blocks.zh: 你走在正确道路上的迹象：

blocks.en:
Time moves differently
Work energizes you
Money becomes secondary
Learning doesn't take effort
Discipline is the default
You think in decades, not days
Waking up is a blessing
blocks.zh:
时间流逝的方式不同
工作让你充满活力
金钱变得次要
学习不费力气
自律是默认状态
你以十年为单位思考，而不是以天
醒来是一种恩赐

blocks.en: You feel like you don't belong, but you wouldn't change a thing.
blocks.zh: 你觉得自己格格不入，但你不会改变任何事。

blocks.en: I miss the feeling that came from writing this every morning.
blocks.zh: 我怀念每天早上写这些内容时的感觉。

blocks.en: Not focused on algorithms or likes. This was my “Here’s what I find the most impactful, I hope you like it” book.
blocks.zh: 不关注算法或点赞。这是我的“这是我觉得最有影响力的内容，希望你喜欢”的书。

blocks.en: Wasn’t a global best seller, and I already disagree with some of what I wrote, but man am I grateful when people tell me that it helped them in some way.
blocks.zh: 它不是全球畅销书，我已经不同意自己写的一些内容，但當人们告诉我这以某种方式帮助了他们时，我真是感激不尽。

blocks.en: @Tim_Denning
Highest insight-per-sentence ratio of any writer I’ve read goes to Dan Koe.
blocks.zh: 在我读过的作家里，丹·科（Dan Koe）的每句话洞察力比例最高。

blocks.en: The uncertainty never goes away, but you do stop noticing it because you learn to trust yourself.
blocks.zh: 不确定性永远不会消失，但你确实不再注意到它，因为你学会了信任自己。

blocks.en: You are a creative person. You just aren't in a creative environment. You don't live a creative lifestyle. You're stressed all day (narrow mind = narrow thoughts) trying to "think" your way to new ideas. It doesn't work that way.
blocks.zh: 你是一个有创造力的人。你只是不在一个富有创造力的环境中。你不过着富有创造力的生活方式。你整天压力山大（思维狭隘=想法狭隘），试图“想”出新点子。但事情不是这样运作的。

blocks.en: The path of 95% of beginners:
blocks.zh: 95%的初学者走的路径：

blocks.en:
- Start posting
- Overcomplicate it
- Make zero progress
- Get discouraged
- Quit and blame everyone but yourself
blocks.zh:
- 开始发帖
- 把它复杂化
- 毫无进展
- 灰心丧气
- 放弃，然后把责任推给除自己以外的所有人

blocks.en:
Here's a course worth of information in 45 minutes to escape beginner hell (take notes):
youtu.be/REwaFvbelEk
blocks.zh:
这里有一套45分钟的课程，信息量顶得上一门课，帮你摆脱新手地狱（记得记笔记）：
youtu.be/REwaFvbelEk

blocks.en: Luck =
blocks.zh: 运气 =

blocks.en:
High energy
In the right place
Around the right people
Producing more than consuming
Avoiding any and all distractions
Able to manage multiple interests
High agency and self-educated
Doesn't quit after one mistake
blocks.zh:
精力充沛
在正确的地方
身边有对的人
产出多于消费
避开一切干扰
能管理多种兴趣
高度主动且自我教育
不会一次犯错就放弃

blocks.en: Luck is a lifestyle
blocks.zh: 运气是一种生活方式

blocks.en: The solution to your problem isn't found in one thing, it's found in the experimentation with many things until you create your own thing.
blocks.zh: 你问题的解决方案不在某一件具体的事情里，而在于对许多事情进行实验，直到你创造出自己的东西。

blocks.en: "I tried for 6 months and it didn't work."
blocks.zh: “我试了6个月，但没成功。”

blocks.en: That's the problem.
blocks.zh: 这就是问题所在。

blocks.en: You tried for 6 months. You didn't improve for 6 months.
blocks.zh: 你试了6个月，但你没有改进6个月。

blocks.en: You followed a list of steps and gave up your agency.
blocks.zh: 你遵循了一串步骤，却放弃了自己的能动性。

blocks.en: You kept doing what wasn't working, didn't realize the problem, and didn't experiment to solve it.
blocks.zh: 你一直在做没用的事，没意识到问题所在，也没有通过实验去解决它。

blocks.en: If you don't know what to write next, use a:
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道接下来写什么，可以用：

blocks.en:
- Pain point
- Example
- Personal story
- Anecdote
- Statistic
- Metaphor
- Quote
- Advice
- What, how, why
blocks.zh:
- 痛点
- 例子
- 个人故事
- 轶事
- 统计数据
- 隐喻
- 引用
- 建议
- 是什么、怎么做、为什么

blocks.en: Those are the building blocks of most writing.
blocks.zh: 这些是大多数写作的构建块。

blocks.en: Once you have an outline, you can pick a few of those to write each section.
blocks.zh: 一旦你有了大纲，就可以挑选其中几个来写每个部分。

blocks.en: Ideas are the most valuable resource because a decent idea gets decent results and a genius idea gets genius results. One person can work 16 hours while the other works 30 minutes, and if the latter has a better idea, they will get better results. Ideas are leverage.
blocks.zh: 想法是最宝贵的资源，因为一个不错的想法会带来不错的结果，一个天才的想法会带来天才的结果。一个人可以工作16小时，而另一个人只工作30分钟，如果后者有更好的想法，他们就会得到更好的结果。想法就是杠杆。

blocks.en: The first step to being creative is not trying to be creative.
blocks.zh: 变得有创造力的第一步，就是不要试图变得有创造力。

blocks.en: How to have a brilliant idea:
blocks.zh: 怎样才能拥有一个绝妙的想法：

blocks.en: Flood your mind with as much as it can tolerate until you feel like you're going insane, then fuck off. Let go of it all and watch the perfect idea surface right when you need it.
blocks.zh: 让你的大脑尽可能多地吸收信息，直到你感觉自己快要疯了，然后甩手不管。放下这一切，那个完美的想法自会浮出水面——就在你最需要它的时候。

blocks.en: The best way to reduce the anxiety of a big task is to start with the smallest possible action. If you can stick with it for 5 minutes, most of your worries vanish.
blocks.zh: 缓解重大任务焦虑的最好办法，就是从尽可能小的一步开始。只要你能坚持五分钟，大部分担忧就会烟消云散。

blocks.en: A pattern found in famous creatives:
blocks.zh: 在知名创意人身上，有一个共同的规律：

blocks.en: They balance intense intellectual work with deep rest. They embody the work hard play hard mentality. When its time to work, they work. When it's time to rest, they do not think about work, and surprisingly, that's when their best ideas come.
blocks.zh: 他们在高强度的脑力劳动与深度的休息之间取得平衡，践行着“工作时拼命工作，玩乐时尽情玩乐”的信条。该工作时，他们全力以赴；该休息时，他们绝不想工作的事——而奇妙的是，最好的点子恰恰在此时降临。

blocks.en: I've never understood the desire for creators to monetize with platform ad revenue or paywalled content (like a newsletter)
blocks.zh: 我一直不理解，为什么创作者总想靠平台广告分成或付费墙内容（比如付费订阅的通讯）来变现。

blocks.en:
- It's harder to create a compelling offer
- You naturally give less value than you could
- Less people buy because it's often recurring
blocks.zh:
- 这样更难打造出有吸引力的产品
- 你自然而然地提供的价值会低于你本可以给出的
- 因为往往是订阅制，愿意付费的人更少

blocks.en: You're guaranteed less revenue, and your audience is guaranteed less value.
blocks.zh: 你的收入注定更少，你的受众得到的价值也注定更少。

blocks.en: Not feeling ready isn't an excuse. If you can paywall content, you can charge for a product.
blocks.zh: “还没准备好”不是借口。如果你能把内容设成付费，你就能为产品收费。

blocks.en: And if you want to go the "donations" or "tips" route, just ask them to support you by buying the product. At least they actually get something in that case.
blocks.zh: 而如果你打算走“打赏”或“小费”的路线，那不如直接请他们买你的产品来支持你。至少那样他们真能拿到点东西。

blocks.en: The most important thing you can do when the world is changing rapidly is learn.
blocks.zh: 当世界快速变化时，你能做的最重要的事，就是学习。

blocks.en: If you wouldn’t switch places with them, take their opinion lightly.
blocks.zh: 如果你不愿意和对方互换位置，那他的意见，听听就好，不必当真。

blocks.en: Ideas are so cool. You just sit there minding your own business and boom you have a completely new direction to take your life.
blocks.zh: 想法真是太美妙了。你只是坐在那儿，忙着自己的事，忽然砰的一声，你的生活就有了一个全新的方向。

blocks.en: Learning comes from struggle, not memorization.
blocks.zh: 学习源于挣扎，而非死记硬背。

blocks.en: Start the project. No, don't watch 20 tutorials beforehand. Let it expose the gaps in your knowledge. Try to figure it out. Search for the answer when your mind is most likely to remember it.
blocks.zh: 开始做这个项目吧。不，别事先看二十个教程。让项目去暴露你知识上的空白。试着自己搞明白。在你大脑最有可能记住答案的时候，再去搜索解答。

blocks.en: Publish the project. Repeat for life.
blocks.zh: 把项目发布出去。然后，终生重复。

blocks.en: Always remember:
blocks.zh: 永远记住：

blocks.en:
- Never promote yourself
- Be a slave to platform revenue
- Even better, beg for donations
- Writing is sacred and money is evil
- New writers especially, don’t even think about making a living
blocks.zh:
- 永远不要推销自己
- 做平台收入的奴隶
- 更好的是，乞求捐赠
- 写作是神圣的，金钱是邪恶的
- 尤其是新作家，想都别想靠写作谋生

blocks.en: Being miserable is a choice.
blocks.zh: 痛苦是一种选择。

blocks.en: You choose to hold a perspective that is incomplete. You choose to narrow in on the problem. You choose to ignore the solution. You give up control of your mind to externalities.
blocks.zh: 你选择抱持一种不完整的视角，你选择只盯着问题看，你选择无视解决方案，你把心智的控制权交给了外部因素。

blocks.en: There is a way you can view the situation that gives you control.
blocks.zh: 你总可以找到一种看待处境的方式，让你重新掌握主动权。

blocks.en: You aren't where you want to be because your standards match where you are.
blocks.zh: 你之所以没达到理想的位置，是因为你的标准还停留在原地。

blocks.en: Filter every thought, emotion, decision, habit, problem, or goal through your vision and drop them without question if they don't align.
blocks.zh: 用你的愿景去过滤每一个念头、情绪、决定、习惯、问题和目标，只要与愿景不符，就毫不犹豫地舍弃。

blocks.en: Anti-vision is the future you refuse to accept.
blocks.zh: 反愿景，就是你拒绝接受的未来。

blocks.en: The dumb mind. The robotic work. The soft body. The numb relationships. Let a terrible image build up in your mind. Remind yourself of it every day.
blocks.zh: 迟钝的头脑，机械的工作，虚弱的身体，麻木的关系。让一幅糟糕的画面在脑海中逐渐成形，每天提醒自己一次。

blocks.en: Then, channel everything you have into the complete opposite.
blocks.zh: 然后，把你的一切都投入到截然相反的方向。

blocks.en: Normalize disappearing for a few months to work on your vision.
blocks.zh: 让消失几个月去专注于你的愿景成为一种常态。

blocks.en: You don't magically become focused. You practice it. You notice you're distracted and snap out of it immediately, over and over again until it's second nature. Most people have not trained this muscle, and they are not anywhere close to as focused as they think they are.
blocks.zh: 专注力不会凭空而来，你得练。察觉到自己分心了，就立刻拉回来，一遍又一遍，直到它成为本能。大多数人从未训练过这块肌肉，他们远没有自己以为的那么专注。

blocks.en: If you want to take control of your life:
blocks.zh: 如果你想掌控自己的人生：

blocks.en:
- Wake up an hour earlier
- 30 minutes moving your body
- 30 minutes building a skill or business
- Practice mindfulness at each second of the day
blocks.zh:
- 早起一小时
- 30分钟活动身体
- 30分钟打磨一项技能或经营一份事业
- 每时每刻练习正念

blocks.en: Swap an hour at night (when motivation is zero) for lever-moving tasks in the morning.
blocks.zh: 把晚上动力为零的一小时，换成早晨能撬动杠杆的任务。

blocks.en: I may be young and dumb, but retirement feels like a scam.
blocks.zh: 我或许年轻又天真，但退休这件事，感觉像个骗局。

blocks.en: My goal isn't to stop working, or to finally do what I want, or to eliminate my sense of purpose and contribution to the world. My goal is to design a life filled with work that I don't want to escape from.
blocks.zh: 我的目标不是停止工作，不是终于去做自己想做的事，也不是消除对世界的使命感和贡献感。我的目标是设计一种生活，其中充满了我根本不想逃离的工作。

blocks.en: Most people don’t have a routine.
blocks.zh: 大多数人没有常规，

blocks.en: They have a rut.
blocks.zh: 只有车辙。

blocks.en: A rut they didn’t choose but got stuck in because it was the safest option.
blocks.zh: 一条他们未曾选择、却因最安全而深陷其中的车辙。

blocks.en: If you don’t design your day, someone else will. And their design isn't meant to lead to the results you want.
blocks.zh: 如果你不设计自己的一天，别人就会替你设计。而他们的设计，并非为了让你得到想要的结果。

blocks.en: If your answer to “why do you do what you do?” is only “to make money” you should probably change what you do, and you’ll probably make more money.
blocks.zh: 如果你对“你为什么做你现在做的事？”的回答仅仅是“为了赚钱”，那你或许该换件事做，而且你很可能反而会赚得更多。

blocks.en: The worst place you can be is not loving your life, but at the same time, not hating it enough to do something great.
blocks.zh: 最糟糕的处境，是你不爱自己的生活，却又不至于厌恶到要去做点什么大事。

blocks.en: I send a life reset planner to everyone who joins my newsletter. It will help you dig deep into what you want, what you don't want, and what to do about it:
blocks.zh: 每个订阅我邮件的人，都会收到一份人生重启规划表。它能帮你深挖自己想要的、不想要的，以及该怎么办：

blocks.en: thedankoe.com/letters
blocks.zh: thedankoe.com/letters

blocks.en: The select few people who know they can learn and build everything necessary to succeed just need the pressure that eliminates distractions and forces focus.
blocks.zh: 少数人清楚地知道，自己有能力学会并搭建起成功所需的一切，他们只差一股压力——一股能扫清干扰、逼人专注的压力。

blocks.en: Quit the job. Move into the apartment you can't afford. Your delusional self-belief will take care of the rest.
blocks.zh: 辞掉工作。搬进你负担不起的公寓。剩下的，交给你那近乎妄想的自信。

blocks.en: The best time to start as a creator is now because follower count means nothing with the For You page. If you know what you’re doing (important) then you can land insane brand deals, make $500k+ at a company, or build your own thing with a tiny following.
blocks.zh: 现在就是做创作者的最好时机，因为在“为你推荐”页面前，粉丝数一文不值。只要你懂行（这很重要），就能拿下惊人的品牌合作，在一家公司挣到50万美元以上，或者凭着极少的粉丝做出自己的事业。

blocks.en: If you're young and don't know where to start, go to the gym.
blocks.zh: 如果你还年轻，不知道从哪儿开始，那就去健身房。

blocks.en: It will teach you that you're supposed to feel lost at first, progress is made in 5-pound increments, people don't look at or care about you, and long-term gratification is one of the greatest feelings in the world.
blocks.zh: 它会教会你：一开始感到迷茫是正常的；进步是以5磅为单位一点点累积的；别人根本不看你，也不在乎你；而长期的满足感，是这世上最美妙的感受之一。

blocks.en: The 2 hours you spend scrolling each day (or 730 hours each year) could have produced a book, a business, or a body you don't currently have.
blocks.zh: 你每天刷手机的那2个小时（一年就是730个小时），本可以写出一本书、做成一门生意，或者练出你现在还没有的身材。

blocks.en: Most people think their dream is to become a YouTuber when that's just their soul begging them to create something, anything, and share it with the world because happiness stems from the intersection of a challenge and connection to something greater than yourself.
blocks.zh: 大多数人以为自己的梦想是当个YouTuber，其实那只是灵魂在恳求你去做点什么——随便什么都行——然后分享给世界，因为幸福源于挑战，源于与比自身更宏大的事物建立连接，二者交汇之处便是幸福。

blocks.en: Your future will be determined by 3 things.
blocks.zh: 你的未来由3件事决定。

blocks.en: And no, those things don't involve Uber Eats, TikTok, or standing on the edge because you missed out on Trump coin (guilty).
blocks.zh: 不，这些事跟Uber Eats、TikTok无关，也不是因为错过Trump币就站在天台边缘（我承认我有过）。

blocks.en: They involve starting your life over from scratch.
blocks.zh: 它们关乎从零开始重启你的人生。

blocks.en: 1) One big decision to go all in.
blocks.zh: 1）做出一个全力以赴的重大决定。

blocks.en: Start with what you hate the most about yourself.
blocks.zh: 从你最厌恶自己的那一点开始。

blocks.en: Commit to achieving the opposite.
blocks.zh: 下定决心做到它的反面。

blocks.en: Zero distractions. Z e r o.
blocks.zh: 零干扰。零。

blocks.en: 2) Moving 1 lever a day, minimum.
blocks.zh: 2）每天至少推动一根杠杆。

blocks.en: A lever is something that actually gets results.
blocks.zh: 杠杆，就是真正能带来结果的东西。

blocks.en: If you aren't getting results, you aren't doing the right things. No exceptions.
blocks.zh: 如果你没拿到结果，那就是你没做对的事。没有例外。

blocks.en: 3) The ability to persist and iterate.
blocks.zh: 3）坚持并不断迭代的能力。

blocks.en: You don't quit. You pivot.
blocks.zh: 你不是放弃，而是转向。

blocks.en: There is a series of actions that lead to the life you want.
blocks.zh: 有一系列行动会引领你走向想要的生活。

blocks.en: You will have to change direction multiple times.
blocks.zh: 你将不得不屡次改变方向。

blocks.en: If your actions create your future, and you aren't where you want to be, then wave goodbye to almost everything you do on a daily basis.
blocks.zh: 如果你的行动创造你的未来，而你却不在想去的地方，那就几乎要对你日常所做的一切说再见了。

blocks.en: It will never be perfect.
blocks.zh: 它永远不会完美。

blocks.en: Launch it. Post it. Put it out into the world when it’s 90% of the way there and let people think what they want to think.
blocks.zh: 发布它。张贴它。在完成90%时就把它推向世界，让人们随心所欲地去想。

blocks.en: If you're doing anything worthwhile, you must publish your work consistently, and if you can't even do that once... good luck.
blocks.zh: 如果你在做任何有价值的事，就必须持续发布你的作品，如果你连一次都做不到……祝你好运。

blocks.en: Early morning or late night.
blocks.zh: 清晨或深夜。

blocks.en: Pick one.
blocks.zh: 选一个。

blocks.en: Those are the only times when the world doesn't demand your energy.
blocks.zh: 那是世界唯一不索取你精力的时段。

blocks.en: Those are the times when you're going to do your best work.
blocks.zh: 那也正是你将做出最佳工作的时刻。

blocks.en: Those are when you move the needle toward the life you want.
blocks.zh: 那正是你推动指针、迈向理想生活的时刻。

blocks.en: If you can face one small fear a day you will find what it means to live a good life
blocks.zh: 如果你能每天面对一个小恐惧，你就会发现美好生活的真谛。

blocks.en: Work is a source of fulfillment, just like any other area of your life, if you’re the one who designs it.
blocks.zh: 工作是一种成就感的来源，就像你生活中的其他领域一样，前提是你是它的设计者。

blocks.en: Closing in on the big 1m and pretty annoyed
blocks.zh: 接近100万大关，却相当恼火

blocks.en: I go through these lulls in views every few months.
blocks.zh: 每隔几个月，我的观看量就会经历这样的低谷。

blocks.en: Videos do really well, then 4-5 of them do way worse.
blocks.zh: 视频表现很好，然后其中4-5个会差得多。

blocks.en: When I look back on them, I realize that the videos just aren't good enough. Not that the content itself is bad or not helpful, but you can see a drastic difference in the topic, title, and thumbnail choice.
blocks.zh: 回头再看，我意识到这些视频只是不够好。不是内容本身糟糕或无益，而是你在主题、标题和缩略图的选择上能看到巨大差异。

blocks.en: I can almost always map these "lulls" to a period when ideas aren't flowing well. I'm not reading as much. I'm not learning anything new. I'm trying to force things out for the sake of staying consistent.
blocks.zh: 我几乎总能把这种“低谷”对应到灵感不畅的时期。我读得不多。我没学到新东西。为了保持一致性，我试图强行产出。

blocks.en: What's helped me break through these points is just that:
blocks.zh: 帮我突破这些节点的，正是：

blocks.en: Doing a mental reset. Throwing all planned content ideas out the window and starting from scratch. Picking up a new book. Learning from new people. Realigning with the core ideas that I'm best at articulating and adding a twist.
blocks.zh: 做一次心理重置。把所有计划的内容创意抛到窗外，从零开始。拿起一本新书。向新的人学习。与我最为擅长表达的核心思想重新对齐，并加入一些新意。

blocks.en: The reason I write this is because I see many others go through the same lulls, or they never make it out of the beginner lull that everyone starts out in.
blocks.zh: 我写这些是因为我看到许多人经历同样的低谷，或者他们从未走出每个人起步时都会经历的初学者低谷。

blocks.en: What helps is just being brutally honest with how good the video actually is.
blocks.zh: 有帮助的是，残酷地诚实评估视频到底有多好。

blocks.en: It can be good in your eyes, which is important, but if others don't care about it, it's missing a crucial aspect of what makes it "good."
blocks.zh: 在你眼中它可能是好的，这很重要，但如果别人不在意它，那就缺失了使其“好”的关键方面。

blocks.en: (P.S. I know 50k+ views is nothing to scoff at. Speaking relative to the normal baseline.)
blocks.zh: （附注：我知道 5 万+ 播放量已经不容小觑。这是相对平时的基准而言。）

blocks.en: Being extra intentional with the next topic / hook - will see how it does
blocks.zh: 下一条选题和钩子会格外用心——看看效果如何

blocks.en: Those who control their inner experience (how they interpret and order the chaos in their heads) control their quality of life.
blocks.zh: 谁能掌控自己的内在体验——即如何解读并梳理脑中的混沌——谁就掌控了自己的生活质量。

blocks.en: If you struggle to think clearly
blocks.zh: 如果你苦于思路不清

blocks.en: If you can't articulate your thoughts
blocks.zh: 如果你无法清晰表达自己的想法

blocks.en: If you feel like your ideas aren't original
blocks.zh: 如果你觉得自己想法毫无新意

blocks.en:
Here's how you can become respected for the quality of your mind:
youtu.be/jhoG3WcECnw
blocks.zh:
以下是你如何因思维品质而赢得尊重：
youtu.be/jhoG3WcECnw

blocks.en: 3-6 months of beginner hell (making close to zero progress and questioning whether it's worth it) is a natures way of filtering out people who weren't serious in the first place.
blocks.zh: 3-6个月的新手地狱期（几乎毫无进展，怀疑是否值得）是大自然筛选掉那些一开始就不认真的人的方式。

blocks.en: If you aren't making progress, you aren't doing the right things.
blocks.zh: 如果你没有进步，说明你做错了事情。

blocks.en: What I mean is if you aren't making progress, you need to experiment... not quit.
blocks.zh: 我的意思是，如果你没有进步，你需要去尝试……而不是放弃。

blocks.en: You aren't where you want to be because you haven't put yourself in the situations that would force you to get there.
blocks.zh: 你之所以没有达到理想的状态，是因为你没有把自己置身于能迫使你达到那里的情境中。

blocks.en: The brutal truth is that nobody cares about the hard work you put in.
blocks.zh: 残酷的事实是，没有人关心你付出的努力。

blocks.en: They care about what they get from it.
blocks.zh: 他们关心的是自己能从中得到什么。

blocks.en: And if it isn't good, they'll either rip you apart or ignore you.
blocks.zh: 如果结果不够好，他们要么把你撕碎，要么无视你。

blocks.en: Be careful betting everything on "hard work."
blocks.zh: 把一切都押在“努力”上时要小心。

blocks.en: Block out 1 hour a day.
blocks.zh: 每天划出1小时。

blocks.en: Work on 1 meaningful project.
blocks.zh: 专注于1个有意义的项目。

blocks.en: Aim for 1 vision for your future.
blocks.zh: 为你的未来瞄准1个愿景。

blocks.en: Take it 1 day at a time, for 1 year.
blocks.zh: 一天一天来，坚持1年。

blocks.en: 1 hour of deep work is better than 0 hours, and you can drastically change your life in 365 hours.
blocks.zh: 1小时的深度工作胜过0小时，你可以在365小时内彻底改变你的人生。

blocks.en: You don't know what to write because:
blocks.zh: 你不知道写什么，因为：

blocks.en: - Your standards (as a beginner) are too high
blocks.zh: - 你的标准（作为初学者）太高了

blocks.en: - You feel as if everything's been written before (it has, but not by you)
blocks.zh: - 你觉得一切都被写过了（确实如此，但不是由你写的）

blocks.en: - You have nothing worth writing about (go DO something, you'll have something to write)
blocks.zh: - 你没有什么值得写的东西（去做点事情，你就会有东西可写）

blocks.en: You lack confidence because you only expose yourself to the respectable sides of other people. You don't see their humanity. You don't see their struggles and shortcomings.
blocks.zh: 你缺乏自信，因为你只接触到别人值得尊敬的一面。你看不到他们的人性。你看不到他们的挣扎和缺点。

blocks.en: You become confident when you can see people outside of the fake mental image you've created of them.
blocks.zh: 当你能够透过你为他们创造的虚假心理形象看到真实的人时，你就会变得自信。

blocks.en: AI only ruins creativity for those who don't know what creativity is. If AI can be as creative as you, you weren't very creative in the first place.
blocks.zh: AI只会破坏那些不知道创造力是什么的人的创造力。如果AI能像你一样有创造力，那你本来就不太有创造力。

blocks.en: I absolutely despise bullet point summary culture.
blocks.zh: 我绝对鄙视要点总结文化。

blocks.en: "Can you condense this into 5 key points so I can get my dopamine hit and move on to the next?"
blocks.zh: “你能不能把这个浓缩成5个要点，好让我爽一下，然后赶紧看下一个？”

blocks.en: No. I want the fluff. I want the context. I want the random and chaotic thought process that contains lessons that can't be taught.
blocks.zh: 不。我要那些废话。我要上下文。我要那些随机的、混乱的思考过程，其中包含着无法被传授的教训。

blocks.en: Once you understand this discipline becomes a lot easier:
blocks.zh: 一旦你理解了这一点，自律就会变得容易得多：

blocks.en: If you don't want to do something, but that something leads to what you want to do, then you want to do it.
blocks.zh: 如果你不想做某件事，但这件事能带你走向你想做的事，那么你其实是想做它的。

blocks.en: It starts as curiosity, turns into interest, slowly becomes purpose, is sustained with profit, and evolves into mastery.
blocks.zh: 它始于好奇，转为兴趣，慢慢成为目标，靠收益维持，最终演变为精通。

blocks.en: Pay attention to where you stop short.
blocks.zh: 留意你在哪里停下脚步。

blocks.en: The point where it gets too uncomfortable and you fall back into your normal life.
blocks.zh: 那个让你感到太不舒服、于是退回到日常生活中的临界点。

blocks.en: The point where all the negative thoughts flood in and you can't handle them.
blocks.zh: 那个所有负面想法涌入、你无法应对的临界点。

blocks.en: The point where all the magic happens if you learn to enjoy pushing through.
blocks.zh: 那个如果你学会享受 pushing through，一切奇迹都会发生的临界点。

blocks.en: It sucks to feel lost.
blocks.zh: 感到迷失很难受。

blocks.en: You can't just "set a goal" because you don't know what you want.
blocks.zh: 你不能只是“设定一个目标”，因为你不知道自己想要什么。

blocks.en: You can't just "solve a problem" because you don't know how.
blocks.zh: 你不能只是“解决问题”，因为你不知道如何解决。

blocks.en:
Here's what you do if you feel stuck in the middle:
youtu.be/Lt79hNo6SWE
blocks.zh:
如果你感到卡在中间，你可以这样做：
youtu.be/Lt79hNo6SWE

blocks.en: If you aren't where you want to be, the most important thing in your life is one hour of needle-moving effort (when your energy is highest) on a project that wasn't assigned to you by parents, teachers, or employers.
blocks.zh: 如果你没达到自己想要的状态，你生活中最重要的事情就是，在你精力最旺盛的时候，花一小时去做一件能推动进展的事，而这个项目不是父母、老师或雇主分配给你的。

blocks.en: Schedule interruptions in your day to help you remember that your daily mindless string of tasks aren't life. Think about your death. Go on a walk and stare at the sky. Close your eyes and listen to a beautiful song. Snap yourself out of mechanical living.
blocks.zh: 在你的日常中安排一些中断，帮助你记住，你每天无意识的连串任务并不是生活。想想你的死亡。去散步，凝视天空。闭上眼睛，听一首优美的歌曲。把自己从机械的生活中唤醒。

blocks.en: How to think originally:
blocks.zh: 如何原创地思考：

blocks.en:
- Stop trying to think originally
- Write good ideas, from your perspective
- Read books that few people have
- Resurface old ideas from a new angle
- Question all beliefs, even the ones you know to be true
- Do one thing that most people don't, daily
blocks.zh:
- 别再刻意追求“原创思考”
- 写出好想法，从你的视角出发
- 读那些少有人读的书
- 让旧想法从新角度重新浮现
- 质疑一切信念，哪怕是你确信为真的那些
- 每天做一件大多数人不会做的事

blocks.en: The solution to most of your problems is perspective.
blocks.zh: 你大多数问题的解药，是换个视角。

blocks.en: The best way to learn is to commit to a real world project that forces you to learn what can't be taught in schools: skills that get non-linear results, how to navigate failure, and how to think outside the box.
blocks.zh: 最好的学习方式，是投入一个真实世界的项目，逼自己去学那些学校里教不了的东西：那些能带来非线性结果的技能、如何应对失败、以及如何跳出框框思考。

blocks.en: I know that everyone wants to build a note-taking/writing/productivity app. I know that we're stupid for doing it. I know we're going to waste a lot of time and money. I know that we could make 100x more, faster, doing something else.
blocks.zh: 我知道人人都想做一款笔记／写作／效率类应用。我知道我们这么做很蠢。我知道我们会浪费大量时间和金钱。我知道我们换个方向能更快地赚到100倍的收益。

blocks.en: Don't care. Still doing it. Team is hungry.
blocks.zh: 不在乎。还是要做。团队干劲十足。

blocks.en: Going in this month:
blocks.zh: 这个月要上线：

blocks.en:
- Desktop app (today)
- Light mode (finally)
- Mobile app (finally)
- Full offline mode
- Images, embeds, files in capture
- Voice transcription
- KAI release (maybe)
blocks.zh:
- 桌面应用（今天）
- 浅色模式（终于）
- 移动应用（终于）
- 完整离线模式
- 采集功能支持图片、嵌入内容和文件
- 语音转写
- KAI发布（也许）

blocks.en: Been building up to this a while
blocks.zh: 为此筹备已有一阵了

blocks.en:
Desktop app is out:
x.com/kortexco/statu…
blocks.zh:
桌面应用已上线：
x.com/kortexco/statu…

blocks.en: @edendotso
The Kortex desktop app is out now!
blocks.zh: Kortex桌面应用现已上线！

blocks.en:
- New floating capture
- New floating documents/notes
- Quick app toggle
blocks.zh:
- 全新的浮动采集
- 全新的浮动文档／笔记
- 快速应用切换

blocks.en: So you can write and capture ideas without changing tabs.
blocks.zh: 这样你无需切换标签页，就能写作和捕捉灵感。

blocks.en: This also sets us up for full offline mode later this month and global capture in the future🧠
blocks.zh: 这也为本月晚些时候的完整离线模式，以及未来的全局采集打下基础🧠

blocks.en: You aren't lost. You're too used to what you know. New becomes normal very quick. When you feel lost, the solution is to become more lost. Throw yourself out of your current way of life and I promise you'll find something to grab onto.
blocks.zh: 你并没有迷失。你只是太习惯于自己已知的东西。新事物很快就会变成常态。当你感到迷失时，解决办法是让自己更迷失一点。把自己抛出当前的生活方式，我保证你会找到可以抓住的东西。

blocks.en: They won't believe in you.
blocks.zh: 他们不会相信你。

blocks.en: The business. The crazy idea. The aspirations so large that most people's minds don't have any other option but to call you delusional.
