blocks.zh: 你的事业、那个疯狂的想法、那些宏大到让大多数人别无选择、只能说你痴心妄想的抱负。

blocks.en: And you are, but only if you don't make it happen.
blocks.zh: 你确实是痴心妄想——但前提是你没有把它变成现实。

blocks.en: A plan is an educated guess. A surface area for luck. A mental frame to keep chaos at bay. A lens to notice ideas that lead to progress. A strategy that changes as you act.
blocks.zh: 计划是一种有根据的猜测，是一片承接运气的表面，是一个把混乱挡在门外的思维框架，是一面让你留意到那些能带来进展的想法的透镜，是一套会随着你的行动而不断调整的策略。

blocks.en: A plan is not something you write down once and tell everyone about to feel like you're making progress.
blocks.zh: 计划不是写下来一次、然后昭告天下、好让自己感觉在进步的东西。

blocks.en: You can just start over. You don't need permission. You don't need to wait for the right time. You can stop what you're doing, right now, and move in a new direction. Your mind will do anything to convince you to stay the same, but you don't have to listen.
blocks.zh: 你大可以直接重新开始。你不需要谁的许可，不需要等所谓合适的时机。你可以立刻停下手里的事，转向一个新的方向。你的大脑会想尽一切办法说服你维持原样，但你不必听它的。

blocks.en: The single thing that keeps most people stuck is that they do what they want but never self-reflect and realize they don't actually want that.
blocks.zh: 让大多数人止步不前的唯一原因，是他们只做自己想做的事，却从不自我反思，因此始终没意识到那根本不是自己真正想要的。

blocks.en: Do what you want > reflect on what you don't want > refine what you want > do what you want > repeat until success
blocks.zh: 做你想做的 > 反思你不想要的 > 修正你想要的 > 做你想做的 > 如此循环，直到成功

blocks.en: One of the biggest questions everyone is asking:
blocks.zh: 每个人都在问的一个最大的问题：

blocks.en: How do I stay relevant?
blocks.zh: 我如何才能保持不被时代淘汰？

blocks.en: This is nothing new, we've been asking that since the dawn of time, but a future filled with AI seems different.
blocks.zh: 这不是什么新鲜问题，自人类诞生以来我们就一直在问，但一个被AI充斥的未来似乎又有所不同。

blocks.en:
Here's one way to make sense of it:
youtu.be/6WbZPRzrE4o
blocks.zh:
这里有一种理解它的方式：
youtu.be/6WbZPRzrE4o

blocks.en: Don't look for goals. Look for interesting problems and the right goal will emerge.
blocks.zh: 别去找目标。去找有趣的问题，对的目标自会浮现。

blocks.en: Your goals determine what opportunities you can see, but most people run on a set of unconscious goals installed by their parents and peers, so they never notice the ideas in everyday situations, conversations, books, and content that could change their life.
blocks.zh: 你的目标决定了你能看见哪些机会，但大多数人运行的是一套由父母和同辈植入的无意识目标，所以他们永远注意不到那些藏在日常情境、对话、书籍和内容里、本可以改变他们人生的想法。

blocks.en: If you want to see a quick jump in quality of life start going on a 15 minute walk first thing in the morning, right after you wake up, no matter what the weather is.
blocks.zh: 如果你想快速提升生活质量，那就从早晨一醒来就出门散步15分钟开始，无论天气如何。

blocks.en: When your vision is clear nothing else matters. You drop everything. Books aren't interesting. Routines hold you back. If your mind wants to focus on reaching the next peak, don't slow it down. Let it consume you.
blocks.zh: 当你的愿景足够清晰，其他一切都不重要了。你会放下一切。书变得索然无味，日常规律反而拖你后腿。如果你的头脑想要专注于攀登下一座高峰，就别让它慢下来。让它吞噬你。

blocks.en: If you want to attract people to you, focus on your mission. People gravitate toward those who know what they want.
blocks.zh: 如果你想吸引他人靠近你，就专注于你的使命。人们会被那些清楚自己想要什么的人吸引。

blocks.en: The plan for 2025 is to write, walk, read, build, train, and adapt as usual.
blocks.zh: 2025年的计划一如既往：写作、行走、阅读、构建、训练、适应。

blocks.en: The difference between where you are and where you want to be is knowledge because if you knew how to get there (and actually wanted to) you wouldn't be able to think or do anything else.
blocks.zh: 你现在的位置和你想去的位置之间，差的只是知识。因为如果你知道怎么到那里（而且真心想去），你根本不会有空闲去想或做别的事。

blocks.en: You need to write.
blocks.zh: 你需要写作。

blocks.en: Especially when most people outsource their thinking.
blocks.zh: 尤其是在大多数人都把思考外包出去的当下。

blocks.en: Writing is like placing your thoughts as legos on a table, seeing how ugly they are, and rebuilding them from scratch. You are literally reprogramming how your mind thinks in a tangible form.
blocks.zh: 写作就像把脑子里的想法当作乐高积木摆在桌上，看清它们有多丑陋，然后从头重建。你实际上是在以一种看得见摸得着的形式，重新编程你的大脑如何思考。

blocks.en: It's so much easier to think while on a walk. There's a rhythm your mind falls into with each step. It's like your mind is walking through idea space. When you sit still, you can only grab the ideas that are close to you. Everything else is dark.
blocks.zh: 散步时思考要轻松得多。每走一步，你的大脑都会进入某种节奏。就像你的思绪在观念的空间里漫步。而当你静坐不动，你只能抓到身边的想法，其余的都在黑暗里。

blocks.en: You need a plan.
blocks.zh: 你需要一个计划。

blocks.en: But most people don't understand what a plan is.
blocks.zh: 但大多数人不明白什么叫计划。

blocks.en: A plan is a mental frame to help you focus on the right things.
blocks.zh: 计划是一种心智框架，帮你聚焦在正确的事情上。

blocks.en: It's supposed to change and evolve as you go.
blocks.zh: 它本就该随着你的前行而改变、演化。

blocks.en: What most people think is a plan is just a list of steps that won't be relevant in a week.
blocks.zh: 大多数人以为的计划，不过是一串一周后就不再适用的步骤清单。

blocks.en: It really does all boil down to doing whatever you want and error-correcting along the way.
blocks.zh: 说到底，一切归结为：做你想做的任何事，并在过程中不断纠错。

blocks.en: You don't build an irreplaceable skill stack doing replaceable work.
blocks.zh: 做可替代的工作，建不成不可替代的技能栈。

blocks.en: People see the creator economy as some myopic new job where you "post content" to make a few bucks. When they realize it's a way to create—a fundamental human desire—without permission, they'll understand why it's the future, regardless if it's on what we call "social media."
blocks.zh: 人们把创作者经济看作某种目光短浅的新行当——你"发布内容"，挣几个小钱。等他们意识到这是一种无需许可就能创造的方式——而创造正是人类根本的渴望——他们就会明白为什么它代表着未来，无论它是否发生在我们所谓的"社交媒体"上。

blocks.en: Start wide, try everything.
blocks.zh: 从宽处起步，什么都试一试。

blocks.en: Notice signal, ignore noise.
blocks.zh: 发现信号，忽略噪音。

blocks.en: Go deep, master it.
blocks.zh: 深入钻研，掌握它。

blocks.en: Create something, anything.
blocks.zh: 创造点什么，什么都行。

blocks.en: Share it with others.
blocks.zh: 与他人分享。

blocks.en: Enjoy and repeat.
blocks.zh: 享受其中，周而复始。

blocks.en: Nothing beats having a buildup of meaningful ideas to write about, throwing on headphones, blaring music so you're forced to drown it out, and emptying your mind just to do it all over again. Nothing beats being a vessel for creativity.
blocks.zh: 没有什么比得上这样的感觉：脑海里积攒了一堆有意义的想法等着写出来，戴上耳机，把音乐开到最大，逼着自己淹没其中，清空大脑，然后从头再来一遍。没有什么比成为创造力的容器更美妙的事了。

blocks.en: The answers you're looking for are in the silence you're avoiding
blocks.zh: 你要找的答案，就藏在你一直回避的沉默里。

blocks.en: It's liberating once you realize that the mind can be trained to do anything you want. That most of your lack is no more than a lack of skill, knowledge, action, and the logical sequence of steps it takes to achieve that thing. Unlike muscle on your body, your mind is infinite.
blocks.zh: 一旦你意识到大脑可以被训练去做任何你想做的事，你会感到一种解放。你所谓的匮乏，大多不过是技能、知识、行动上的欠缺，以及对实现目标所需步骤的逻辑顺序不够清晰。与你身上的肌肉不同，你的大脑是无限的。

blocks.en: You don't need more knowledge because you already know what you need to do. You're studying level 5 at level 1 and it's only adding more things to forget about when you decide to start..
blocks.zh: 你不需要更多知识，因为你已经知道该做什么了。你在用一级的水平去研究五级的内容，这只会让你在真正决定开始时，多出一堆要忘掉的东西。

blocks.en: You don't find passion.
blocks.zh: 热情不是找到的。

blocks.en: You become passionate according to the amount of energy you invest in an interest.
blocks.zh: 你投入多少精力到一项兴趣上，你就会变得多有热情。

blocks.en: Your audience doesn't want information.
blocks.zh: 你的受众不想要信息。

blocks.en: They want YOUR perspective on information.
blocks.zh: 他们想要的是你对信息的独特视角。

blocks.en: 10 people can share the same idea. Only one will say it in a way that changes minds.
blocks.zh: 同一个想法，十个人都能讲。但只有一个人能用改变人心的方式说出来。

blocks.en: You didn't start this to become another "personal brand."
blocks.zh: 你开始做这件事，不是为了成为又一个“个人品牌”。

blocks.en: You started because you wanted freedom. Meaningful income. The ability to create work that sets your soul on fire.
blocks.zh: 你开始，是因为你想要自由。有意义收入。有能力去创造让灵魂燃烧的作品。

blocks.en: Take your mind, without the labels, and stream it where anyone can watch.
blocks.zh: 带上你的思想，抛开那些标签，把它播出去，让任何人都能看到。

blocks.en: Most "content creators" are just search engines with profile pictures. Publish work that makes people question their existence.
blocks.zh: 大多数“内容创作者”不过是换了头像的搜索引擎。发布那些能让人们质疑自身存在意义的作品。

blocks.en: how to thrive in the future
blocks.zh: 如何在未来蓬勃发展

blocks.en: I’m bullish on humans
blocks.zh: 我看好人类

blocks.en: You're allowed to be motivated by money.
blocks.zh: 你可以被金钱驱动。

blocks.en: Scratch that, you are motivated by money. But you hide it because someone convinced you to think money is inherently impure.
blocks.zh: 收回这句话，你就是被金钱驱动的。但你藏着掖着，因为有人让你相信金钱天生就是不干净的。

blocks.en: You work, right now, for money, to survive.
blocks.zh: 你现在工作，就是为了钱，为了生存。

blocks.en: Its a modern basic need.
blocks.zh: 这是现代人的基本需求。

blocks.en: Don't apologize for wanting to live well.
blocks.zh: 别为想过好日子而道歉。

blocks.en: If you want to:
blocks.zh: 如果你想：

blocks.en:
- Write a book without a publisher
- Make music without a record label
- Code, design, or market without an employer
blocks.zh:
- 不靠出版商写一本书
- 不靠唱片公司做音乐
- 不靠雇主写代码、做设计或做营销

blocks.en: Or turn any interest into independent work
blocks.zh: 或者把任何兴趣变成独立的事业

blocks.en:
Social capital is what you're missing:
youtu.be/DAgVDVHsApE
blocks.zh:
你缺的是社会资本：
youtu.be/DAgVDVHsApE

blocks.en: The future belongs to those who understand:
blocks.zh: 未来属于那些懂得这些的人：

blocks.en:
- AI needs direction
- Tools need masters
- Data needs insight
- Content needs context
- Success needs vision
blocks.zh:
- AI 需要方向
- 工具需要主人
- 数据需要洞察
- 内容需要语境
- 成功需要愿景

blocks.en: Automation won't save you. Agency will.
blocks.zh: 自动化救不了你。能动性才行。

blocks.en: The greatest lie of modern work:
blocks.zh: 现代工作最大的谎言：

blocks.en: That all hours are created equal.
blocks.zh: 所有时间都是平等的。

blocks.en: That you're the same person at hour 12 as hour 1.
blocks.zh: 第 12 个小时的你和第 1 个小时的你是同一个人。

blocks.en: That quantity beats quality.
blocks.zh: 数量胜过质量。

blocks.en: That busy means valuable.
blocks.zh: 忙碌就等于有价值。

blocks.en: You're not struggling with productivity. You're struggling with not having a project worth being productive for.
blocks.zh: 你纠结的不是效率问题。你纠结的是，没有一个值得你高效投入的项目。

blocks.en: Is it just me or are the holidays extremely boring if you aren't a child or parent. All I want to do is build and people look at me like I'm crazy for not laying on the couch all day.
blocks.zh: 只有我这么觉得吗？如果你既不是小孩也不是家长，假期就无聊得要命。我只想动手做点东西，而别人看我整天不瘫在沙发上，就像看疯子一样。

blocks.en: Don't believe everything you think. Your mind is great at surfacing thoughts that don't matter as a test of your focus.
blocks.zh: 别对你脑子里的每个念头都信以为真。你的大脑很擅长冒出无关紧要的想法，来测试你的专注力。

blocks.en: Don't touch your phone in the morning. Releasing entropy right when you open your eyes is a great way to ruin the rest of your day.
blocks.zh: 早上别碰手机。一睁眼就释放熵，是毁掉接下来一整天的绝佳方式。

blocks.en: It doesn't matter how long it takes. You started something new because you want a sense of zest in your life. The default mindless way of life wasn't cutting it for you. By quitting, you are effectively telling yourself that you aren't worth it.
blocks.zh: 花多久都无所谓。你开始做一件新事，是因为你想给生活添一点激情。那种默认的、无脑的生活方式，对你来说根本不够用。半途而废，其实就是在告诉自己：你不值得。

blocks.en: 4 years of school is fine. But 6-12 months building your own thing is too much? Because you have better things you could be doing? Really? What are those "better things?" More time to lounge around in front of a screen?
blocks.zh: 读 4 年书没问题。但花 6 到 12 个月打造自己的东西就太多了？因为你有更重要的事要做？真的吗？那些“更重要的事”是什么？更多时间瘫在屏幕前闲混？

blocks.en: Gain some fucking perspective.
blocks.zh: 他妈的给我端正一下视角。

blocks.en: There is absolutely nothing more important than avoiding a robotic life.
blocks.zh: 没有什么比避免过一种机器人般的生活更重要。

blocks.en: Writing is more than communication.
blocks.zh: 写作不只是沟通。

blocks.en: Writing is how you practice thinking.
blocks.zh: 写作是你练习思考的方式。

blocks.en: Writing is how you document your development.
blocks.zh: 写作是你记录自己成长的方式。

blocks.en: Writing is how you attract supporters for your work.
blocks.zh: 写作是你为自己的作品吸引支持者的方式。

blocks.en: Writing will only go out of style when you outsource the creative ability of your mind.
blocks.zh: 只有当你不假思索地把头脑的创造力外包出去时，写作才会过时。

blocks.en: You need 4 activities:
blocks.zh: 你需要 4 种活动：

blocks.en: Consume: learn something new.
blocks.zh: 输入：学点新东西。

blocks.en: Create: build a meaningful project.
blocks.zh: 创造：做一个有意义的项目。

blocks.en: Connect: with people and nature.
blocks.zh: 连接：与人、与自然建立联系。

blocks.en: Clear: your mind of rogue thoughts.
blocks.zh: 清理：剔除你脑海中那些杂乱的念头。

blocks.en: Most of your problems stem from a stagnant mind that can be solved with a structure that encourages flow.
blocks.zh: 你的大多数问题都源于思维的停滞，而一个鼓励心流的结构可以解决这个问题。

blocks.en: Everyone should write a book at least once in their lifetime.
blocks.zh: 每个人一生中都至少应该写一本书。

blocks.en: Especially if you want to become a deep and articulate thinker.
blocks.zh: 尤其当你想成为一个思想深刻、表达清晰的人时。

blocks.en: When you write a post or article, your mind expands to fit that context. You catch ideas that help you finish that specific project.
blocks.zh: 当你写一篇帖子或文章时，你的思维会扩展以适应那个语境。你会捕捉到有助于完成那个特定项目的想法。

blocks.en: But a book is different. It's extremely chaotic at first. You spill your subconscious into a blank document and start shaping it into chapters and sections. You create a little world for your mind to operate in.
blocks.zh: 但书不一样。一开始它极其混乱。你把潜意识倾泻到一个空白文档中，然后开始把它塑造成章节和段落。你为你的思维创造了一个小世界，让它在这个世界里运作。

blocks.en: The longer you spend in that world, the more your mind expands to take that shape, and the more connections you start to make. When you're writing a book, you struggle a lot, but you'll find that your brain lights up with interest and excitement more than ever before. Almost any information or conversation you come across gives you an idea.
blocks.zh: 你在那个世界里待得越久，你的思维就越会扩展成那个形状，你开始建立的联系也越多。写书时，你会非常挣扎，但你会发现你的大脑比以往任何时候都更充满兴趣和兴奋。你遇到的几乎任何信息或对话都会给你带来灵感。

blocks.en: You start to realize that your mind is only as perceptive as the project you're working on.
blocks.zh: 你开始意识到，你的思维有多敏锐，只取决于你正在做的项目。

blocks.en: It's scary to admit that everything you believe is a story you've accepted or invented.
blocks.zh: 承认你所相信的一切都是你接受或编造的故事，这很可怕。

blocks.en: If you never contradict yourself, you're probably too attached to a limiting belief, and it's holding you back from reaching the next level.
blocks.zh: 如果你从不自相矛盾，那你很可能执着于一个限制性信念，而这个信念正在阻碍你达到下一个层次。

blocks.en: Learning from a mistake the first time is how you blow past everyone else who spend years in stagnation because their ego is too big to accept their faults.
blocks.zh: 第一次犯错就从中学习，这是你超越其他人的方式——那些人因为自尊心太强、无法接受自己的错误，在停滞中浪费了多年。

blocks.en: Your feelings don't have to dictate your behavior.
blocks.zh: 你的感受不必支配你的行为。

blocks.en: You can do the right thing, and you can do it well, even if you don't feel like doing it.
blocks.zh: 你可以做正确的事，并且把它做好，即使你并不想去做。

blocks.en: This is the ultimate skill you can practice that spills over into the entirety of your life.
blocks.zh: 这是你可以练习的终极技能，它会渗透到你整个生活中。

blocks.en: Your life's work is to reach your potential. Plain and simple. Anything that leads to decay is a distraction that must be wrestled with and eliminated.
blocks.zh: 你一生的工作就是发挥你的潜力。就这么简单。任何导致衰败的事情都是干扰，必须与之搏斗并消除。

blocks.en: The only people who will ultimately be replaced by AI are those who are incapable (or unwilling) to learn how to run a business.
blocks.zh: 最终被AI取代的，只会是那些没有能力（或不愿意）学习如何经营企业的人。

blocks.en: You tried to fit in.
blocks.zh: 你曾试图融入人群。

blocks.en: You tried to follow the crowd.
blocks.zh: 你曾试图随波逐流。

blocks.en: You tried to do the things that people told you would lead to success.
blocks.zh: 你曾试图去做那些别人告诉你能够通向成功的事。

blocks.en:
But you're different. You're observant. You just lack clarity on how to create your own path. This may help:
youtu.be/cG-brqeMrBw
blocks.zh:
但你与众不同。你善于观察。你只是还没想清楚，如何开辟属于自己的路。这或许能帮到你：
youtu.be/cG-brqeMrBw

blocks.en: You can't live a new life with your old actions. Once you finally realize that, you'll stop gripping on so tightly to the pleasures that don't serve you. If you really want to change, you will. Most people just fantasize about a better life as another source of pleasure.
blocks.zh: 用旧有的行动，过不上全新的人生。一旦你真正意识到这一点，就不会再死死抓住那些对你毫无益处的享乐不放。如果你真心想改变，你就一定会改变。大多数人不过是在幻想更美好的生活，把它当作另一种享乐的来源罢了。

blocks.en: If you don't know where to start, start with yourself.
blocks.zh: 如果你不知道从哪里开始，那就从自己开始。

blocks.en:
Your fitness.
Your nutrition.
Your money.
Your skill set.
Your mindset.
blocks.zh:
你的身体。
你的饮食。
你的财务。
你的技能。
你的心态。

blocks.en: Solve one little pain point in your life and I promise you'll know what to do next.
blocks.zh: 解决你生活中的一个小小的痛点，我保证你就会知道下一步该做什么。

blocks.en: Balance is found in the extremes.
blocks.zh: 平衡，藏在极端之中。

blocks.en: Pushing to failure. Prioritizing recovery. Deep focused work. Worry-free rest. Periods of intensity for rapid and rare progress followed by periods of consistency to maintain new baselines.
blocks.zh: 练到力竭。重视恢复。深度专注地工作。无忧无虑地休息。经历一段高强度的时期，以求快速而罕见的突破，随后再用一段稳定坚持的时期，守住新的基准线。

blocks.en: Stuck in the middle is a slow and average death.
blocks.zh: 卡在中间，是一种缓慢而平庸的死亡。

blocks.en: Writing tip to stop overcomplicating it:
blocks.zh: 写作技巧：别再把它搞复杂了：

blocks.en: Think about the essence of what you want to say.
blocks.zh: 想清楚你到底想说什么。

blocks.en: Say it.
blocks.zh: 说出来。

blocks.en: If it's short form, stop there.
blocks.zh: 如果是短内容，到此为止。

blocks.en: If it's long form, back it up with quotes, key points, stories, and anything else that strengthens what you said.
blocks.zh: 如果是长内容，那就用引语、要点、故事，以及任何能强化你观点的东西来支撑它。

blocks.en: It's all a mind game.
blocks.zh: 这一切都是心理游戏。

blocks.en: It's not difficult. It's not overwhelming. It's not negative. Those are interpretations. You can't find the perspective that allows you to gain an advantage over that situation.
blocks.zh: 它不困难。它不令人不堪重负。它不是负面的。那些都是解读。你找不到能让你在那个情境中占据优势的视角。

blocks.en: Master your mind. It's the starting point from which you master anything else.
blocks.zh: 掌控你的心智。这是你掌控其他一切的起点。

blocks.en: Stop giving attention to things you don't want more of in your life.
blocks.zh: 不要再把注意力放在那些你不希望生活中出现更多的东西上。

blocks.en: Negative thoughts. Behavior of other people. Anything you read. Anything you watch. Where you are now is the result of where you placed your attention in the past.
blocks.zh: 负面想法。他人的行为。你读的任何东西。你看的任何东西。你如今所处的位置，是你过去把注意力放在哪里的结果。

blocks.en: Attention amplifies anything it touches, and since it's easy for your mind to get distracted by meaningless things, it's not a surprise why your life takes that shape.
blocks.zh: 注意力会放大它所触及的一切，而你的心智又很容易被无意义的事物分散，所以你的人生呈现出那样的形态，一点也不奇怪。

blocks.en: You aren't disciplined because you keep putting yourself in environments that give you a chance to be undisciplined.
blocks.zh: 你之所以不够自律，是因为你不断把自己置身于那些让你有机会不自律的环境里。

blocks.en: You only encounter mistakes if you're actually doing something.
blocks.zh: 只有当你真正在做事情时，你才会遇到错误。

blocks.en: For most people, they see this as a bad thing. They lack pain tolerance from extended comfort and quit before things start getting good.
blocks.zh: 对大多数人来说，他们把这看作坏事。长期的舒适让他们缺乏对痛苦的耐受，于是在事情开始变好之前就放弃了。

blocks.en: If you're making mistakes in a non-self-destructive direction, have faith for just a bit longer.
blocks.zh: 如果你犯的错误不是自我毁灭方向的，那就再多一点信心，坚持得再久一点。

blocks.en: You're on the right path.
blocks.zh: 你走在正确的路上。

blocks.en: The only thing more difficult than pursuing the best version of yourself is not pursuing the best version of yourself.
blocks.zh: 唯一比追求最好的自己更难的，就是不追求最好的自己。

blocks.en: You need to move.
blocks.zh: 你需要动起来。

blocks.en: Your body. Your mind. Your projects. Your relationships. Your finances. Because if you don't, you don't stay the same, you slowly decay without realizing it until you reach the point where it's much, much harder to dig back out.
blocks.zh: 你的身体。你的心智。你的项目。你的关系。你的财务。因为如果你不动，你不会保持原样，你会在不知不觉中慢慢衰败，直到到达那个再想爬出来就难得多得多的地步。

blocks.en: Entropy waits for no one.
blocks.zh: 熵不等人。

blocks.en: I hate to break it to you, but most of your beliefs are wrong. If you don't look back on your mind 10 years from now and laugh, you are just like that closed minded person you secretly despise. Beliefs are tools. Grip onto them and act, but let go when they don't serve you.
blocks.zh: 我不想打击你，但你大多数信念都是错的。如果十年后你回看自己现在的想法不觉得好笑，那你就和你私下鄙视的那种思想封闭的人一模一样。信念是工具。抓住它们去行动，但当它们不再为你服务时，就放手。

blocks.en: Pain is a great teacher because it helps you realize two things: what's worth suffering for and what you never want to experience again. Pain gives you direction. That's why most people are lost.
blocks.zh: 痛苦是一位伟大的老师，因为它帮你认清两件事：什么值得为之受苦，以及什么是你再也不想经历的。痛苦给你方向。这就是为什么大多数人会迷失。

blocks.en: The best writing isn't about stringing words together in a way that sounds smart. It's about hunting for great ideas, letting them marinate in your subconscious, and synthesizing them into something worth reading.
blocks.zh: 最好的写作，不是把词语串在一起让它听起来很聪明。而是去搜寻伟大的想法，让它们在你的潜意识里慢慢发酵，再把它们综合成值得一读的东西。

blocks.en: Working on a project and need help.
blocks.zh: 正在做一个项目，需要帮助。

blocks.en: Has to do with going on a walk.
blocks.zh: 和散步有关。

blocks.en: How has walking helped with your ideas, creativity, health, relationships, general quality of life, or anything else?
blocks.zh: 散步对你的想法、创造力、健康、人际关系、整体生活质量或其他方面有什么帮助？

blocks.en: What's your "walking" story?
blocks.zh: 你的“散步”故事是什么？

blocks.en: We may reach out to a few of you to dig deeper into the story, so if you're up for it, keep an eye on DMs :)
blocks.zh: 我们可能会联系几个人，深入了解故事，所以如果你愿意，请留意私信 :)

blocks.en: Your life changes when you finally realize that anything is possible (on a long enough time scale) as long as you build the steps that lead to it being possible.
blocks.zh: 当你终于意识到，只要在足够长的时间尺度上构建通往可能性的步骤，一切皆有可能时，你的生活就会改变。

blocks.en: One of the most important skills is how to learn skills fast.
blocks.zh: 最重要的技能之一是如何快速学习技能。

blocks.en: You need to be able to adapt going into a future of AI and automation.
blocks.zh: 你需要能够适应进入AI和自动化的未来。

blocks.en: And learning one skill will only lead to you being replaced.
blocks.zh: 只学习一项技能只会导致你被取代。

blocks.en: But most people don't know how to learn.
blocks.zh: 但大多数人不知道如何学习。

blocks.en: 1) Stop Learning "Skills"
blocks.zh: 1) 停止学习“技能”

blocks.en: The first problem is that people think they learn skills by picking one and studying it.
blocks.zh: 第一个问题是，人们认为学习技能就是选一个然后研究它。

blocks.en: No. That's how you learn the same thing as everyone else and get placed in a job or business that can be replaced in a millisecond.
blocks.zh: 不。那样你学到的东西和所有人都一样，然后被安排到一份毫秒间就能被取代的工作或业务中。

blocks.en: Instead, you learn anything and everything that allows you to achieve your ideal lifestyle. Everything must be filtered through your vision.
blocks.zh: 相反，你要学习任何能让你实现理想生活方式的东西。一切都必须通过你的愿景来过滤。

blocks.en: 2) Start The Project, Then Learn
blocks.zh: 2) 启动项目，然后学习

blocks.en: Most people get trapped in tutorial hell.
blocks.zh: 大多数人都会陷入“教程地狱”。

blocks.en: They watch videos all day and after 3 months they still have no idea what they're doing when they decide to start.
blocks.zh: 他们整天看视频，三个月后真要动手时，却依然一头雾水。

blocks.en: Start a project that will move the needle toward your vision.
blocks.zh: 启动一个能推动你朝愿景迈进的项目。

blocks.en: Start. It. Then, when you hit a roadblock, supplement with education.
blocks.zh: 先动手。真做起来。遇到卡点了，再用学习来补充。

blocks.en: 3) Ship The Project
blocks.zh: 3）把项目交付出去

blocks.en: Post the video. Send the newsletter. Launch the product. Pitch your service. Especially if you're embarrassed.
blocks.zh: 把视频发出去。把邮件通讯寄出去。把产品推上线。把你的服务推销出去。哪怕你羞于启齿，也要做。

blocks.en: The harsh reality is that if you don't have real people using your project, you have no idea if it's valuable. You don't determine its value.
blocks.zh: 残酷的现实是：如果没有真实用户在用你的项目，你根本不知道它有没有价值。它的价值不由你说了算。

blocks.en: If you never hit send, you have no idea if you're moving in the right direction, and you will get lost.
blocks.zh: 如果你从不敢按下“发送”，你就不知道自己是否走在正确的方向上，最终只会迷失。

blocks.en: I'll end with this:
blocks.zh: 最后，我想说：

blocks.en: You can't improve what doesn't exist, therefore you don't actually start learning a thing until you put your project in front of people to judge, criticize, and use.
blocks.zh: 不存在的东西，你无从改进。所以，只有把项目摆到人前，让人评判、批评、使用，你才算真正开始学习。

blocks.en: "But how do I start it?"
blocks.zh: “可我该怎么开始呢？”

blocks.en: You tell me.
blocks.zh: 这得你来告诉我。

blocks.en: Open up the video editor, record a video without overthinking it, start editing, and I guarantee you will find mistakes that you can start improving much faster than if you spent 10 hours studying and not building.
blocks.zh: 打开视频剪辑软件，别想太多，先录一段，然后开始剪辑。我保证你会立刻发现错误，改进起来，比你花十个小时光研究不动手要快得多。

blocks.en: Open a document and braindump some ideas. Write a post and post it even if it's terrible. Just start doing something. Anything. If you aren't moving you are decaying.
blocks.zh: 打开一个文档，把脑子里的想法一股脑倒出来。写一篇文章，哪怕写得很烂也要发出去。总之，动手做点什么。什么都行。不进则退。

blocks.en: If you don't, you're simply delaying the amount of time of getting your first terrible iteration out.
blocks.zh: 否则，你只是在拖延，让那第一版糟糕的作品迟迟不能问世。

blocks.en: Doesn't matter if you spend 5 minutes or 10 years on it.
blocks.zh: 花五分钟还是花十年，都不重要。

blocks.en: The. First. Iteration. Will. Suck.
blocks.zh: 第一。版。一定。很。烂。

blocks.en: Hitting "send" is nature's filter for people who aren't serious about making it.
blocks.zh: 按下“发送”，正是大自然为那些并不真正想做出成绩的人设下的筛子。

blocks.en: figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out figure it out
blocks.zh: 想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚想清楚

blocks.en: Those who struggle with money struggle with awareness.
blocks.zh: 为钱所困的人，实则是被认知所困。

blocks.en: You pay people daily. You do work that pays you some and others more. Your life is filled with items you paid for.
blocks.zh: 你每天都在付钱给别人。你做的工作，让一些人付你钱，让另一些人付你更多钱。你的生活里堆满了你花钱买来的东西。

blocks.en: You're a part of the process but not aware of the process, so you're dependent on it and can't replicate it.
blocks.zh: 你身处这个过程之中，却对它一无所知，所以你依赖它，却无法复制它。

blocks.en: You're overwhelmed because you're holding 1 year's worth of skill acquisition, work, and growth in your head rather than the 1 thing you can do right now to get there.
blocks.zh: 你之所以感到不堪重负，是因为你脑子里装着整整一年的技能学习、工作和成长，而不是此刻你就能迈出的那一步。

blocks.en: You're unhappy because your mind becomes what you pay attention to, and you pay attention to what you think is important, and people have told you what you should think is important your entire life, but you haven't realized that maybe they don't know what they're talking about.
blocks.zh: 你不快乐，是因为你的大脑会变成你关注之物的样子，而你关注的是你认为重要的事，可从小到大，别人一直在告诉你什么该被重视，你却从未意识到，也许他们自己也不知道自己在说什么。

blocks.en: Having a plan B is for people who don't trust their ability to learn, build, and adapt.
blocks.zh: 留一手B计划，是留给那些不信任自己学习、构建和适应能力的人的。

blocks.en: The average person feels cheated by the dream they were sold. School didn't prepare them for this. The job didn't give them enough money, time, or security. Since that's all they were taught, they don't see another way to live, so they drown in anything that will numb the pain.
blocks.zh: 普通人觉得自己被兜售的梦想骗了。学校没教他们怎么应对这一切，工作也没给他们足够的钱、时间或安全感。既然他们只学过这些，就看不到别的活法，于是沉溺于任何能麻痹痛苦的东西。

blocks.en: If you can't solve a problem with hard work, you can probably solve it by going on a walk.
blocks.zh: 如果一个问题靠埋头苦干解决不了，那出门散个步，多半就能解开。

blocks.en: Do whatever you want. When you do, you will make massive mistakes. At that point, you no longer want it, and slowly course correct toward what you really want. If you always do what others want for you, you will never discover what you want.
blocks.zh: 想做什么就去做。做了之后，你会犯下大错。到那时，你就不再想要它了，并会慢慢调整方向，走向你真正想要的东西。如果你总是按别人的期望行事，你就永远发现自己想要什么。

blocks.en: If you struggle with mental clarity:
blocks.zh: 如果你觉得脑子一团乱：

blocks.en:
- Pull out a piece of paper
- Write down all of your thoughts
- Cross out all of the distractions
- Focus on what’s left
blocks.zh:
- 抽出一张纸
- 把脑子里所有的想法都写下来
- 划掉所有让你分心的东西
- 专注于剩下的部分

blocks.en: A clear head can be as simple as putting your mind on paper and organizing it.
blocks.zh: 让头脑清醒，可以简单到只是把思绪落到纸上，再梳理清楚。

blocks.en: You actually can do whatever you want whenever you want, and if you have a decent set of values, you should.
blocks.zh: 你其实随时都可以做任何你想做的事，只要你有一套像样的价值观，就理应如此。

blocks.en: there's nothing stopping you
blocks.zh: 没有什么能拦住你

blocks.en: You are learning every millisecond of the day.
blocks.zh: 你每分每秒都在学习。

blocks.en: Your mind is a sponge soaking in information. Being programmed. Being conditioned. Being told what to do and how to do it. For most people, this is unconscious.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑像一块海绵，不断吸收信息。被编程，被塑造，被灌输该做什么、该怎么做。对大多数人来说，这一切都是无意识的。

blocks.en: If you were to learn, consciously, your life would turn around fast.
blocks.zh: 如果你能有意识地去学习，你的人生会迅速转向。

blocks.en: Dopamine tells you when something is important to your survival-wired brain.
blocks.zh: 多巴胺会告诉你，什么对你的生存本能来说很重要。

blocks.en: Companies exploit this by testing combinations of fat, sugar, salt, fear, pleasure, and conviction to addict you.
blocks.zh: 公司深谙此道，于是测试脂肪、糖、盐、恐惧、快感和信念的各种组合，只为了让你上瘾。

blocks.en: Very few things are important, and it's your duty to discover and pursue them.
blocks.zh: 重要的事情寥寥无几，而你的责任就是发现它们并去追求。

blocks.en: Your past doesn't exist.
blocks.zh: 你的过去并不存在。

blocks.en: It's just an image in your mind. But you decide to live as if that image were your reality. Even worse, you Photoshop that image. You make it worse than it was and it slowly dims the future image you could create.
blocks.zh: 它只是你脑海中的一个影像。但你却决定把那个影像当作现实来生活。更糟的是，你还对这个影像进行了PS。你把它变得比原本更糟，而它又慢慢暗淡了你本可以创造的未来图景。

blocks.en: Most new wealth is being generated in the digital space because its barrier of entry is skill, not money or location.
blocks.zh: 大多数新财富都在数字空间中被创造出来，因为它的准入门槛是技能，而不是金钱或地点。

blocks.en: You aren't fulfilled because your mind makes sense of the world in stories and you stopped living your own.
blocks.zh: 你之所以感到不满足，是因为你的大脑通过故事来理解世界，而你却不再活在自己的故事里。

blocks.en: Go on more walks. Walk for no reason. Walk to solve a problem. Walk to blow off steam. Walk to get outside. Walk to listen, read, and learn. Walk to escape distractions. Walk to improve your health. Walk to think. A simple walking habit can change absolutely everything.
blocks.zh: 多去散步。漫无目的地散步。为解决问题而散步。为发泄情绪而散步。为走到户外而散步。为倾听、阅读和学习而散步。为逃离干扰而散步。为改善健康而散步。为思考而散步。一个简单的散步习惯就能改变一切。

blocks.en: The death of your business happens when you obsess over a website, logo, LLC, and taxes before you actually start getting customers.
blocks.zh: 你的企业之所以失败，是因为你在真正开始获得客户之前，就痴迷于网站、标志、LLC和税务。

blocks.en: If you're okay with 10 cents in your bank account, you won't see that as a problem.
blocks.zh: 如果你对银行账户里只有10美分感到无所谓，你就不会把它看作一个问题。

blocks.en: If you're okay with 20 pounds of extra body fat, you won't do anything to change it.
blocks.zh: 如果你对身上多出20磅脂肪感到无所谓，你就不会采取任何行动去改变它。

blocks.en: Your standards – your settling point – will ruin you if they are absymally low.
blocks.zh: 你的标准——你的妥协点——如果低得离谱，就会毁了你。

blocks.en: Many successful people are born out of an overwhelming amount of negativity that they chose to use as fuel, not an excuse.
blocks.zh: 许多成功人士都诞生于铺天盖地的负面情绪之中，他们选择将其作为燃料，而不是借口。

blocks.en: Building a project will teach you more than watching a tutorial ever will.
blocks.zh: 构建一个项目教给你的东西，远比看教程来得多。

blocks.en: Normalize disappearing for 1 hour a day to build a better future for yourself.
blocks.zh: 把每天消失1小时以便为自己构建更美好的未来这件事常态化。

blocks.en: How to start a billion dollar business:
blocks.zh: 如何开创一家十亿美元的企业：

blocks.en: Don't.
blocks.zh: 别这么做。

blocks.en: Start a one-person business.
blocks.zh: 先从一人企业做起。

blocks.en: Build enough cash flow to leave your job.
blocks.zh: 建立足够的现金流，以便辞掉你的工作。

blocks.en: Build enough of an audience to fuel that dream company you want to start.
blocks.zh: 先积累起足够的受众，才能撑起你想创办的那家梦想公司。

blocks.en: Focus on the skills and interests you can already help people with.
blocks.zh: 专注于你已经能帮到别人的技能和兴趣。

blocks.en: Most people end up 50 years old with the emotional maturity of a 15 year old.
blocks.zh: 大多数人到了50岁，情绪成熟度却还停留在15岁。

blocks.en: If you're in your 20s:
blocks.zh: 如果你正处在20多岁：

blocks.en:
- Experiment with new paths
- Start your business failures now
- Study the opposite of your beliefs
- Challenge yourself with new interests
blocks.zh:
- 尝试新的道路
- 现在就经历创业的失败
- 研究与你信念相反的东西
- 用新的兴趣挑战自己

blocks.en: The worst thing you can do is stop learning, growing, and changing your mind after leaving the school system.
blocks.zh: 最糟糕的事，就是离开学校体系之后就停止学习、停止成长、不再改变自己的想法。

blocks.en: It's okay to disappear and build the thing you've been putting off (that will make you a better person when you come back).
blocks.zh: 消失一段时间，去打造那件你一直搁置的事（等你回来时，它会让你成为更好的人），这没什么问题。

blocks.en: The best sales strategy is being so clear with what they receive that they can't help but buy, and if they don't, it's not a selling problem, it's a product problem.
blocks.zh: 最好的销售策略是清晰说明他们能得到什么，让他们忍不住购买；如果他们不买，那不是销售问题，而是产品问题。

blocks.en: The secret is to be useful.
blocks.zh: 秘诀就是让自己有用。

blocks.en: Create. Design. Build. Write. Sell. Learn. Dissect. Hypothesize. Synthesize. Help.
blocks.zh: 创造。设计。构建。写作。销售。学习。剖析。假设。综合。帮助。

blocks.en: Contribute more value than you take.
blocks.zh: 贡献的价值要大于你索取的价值。

blocks.en: Don't be a leech.
blocks.zh: 别做寄生虫。

blocks.en: Stop trying to find a niche.
blocks.zh: 别再费心去找什么细分市场了。

blocks.en: Instead, ask yourself:
blocks.zh: 反过来，问问自己：

blocks.en:
- Who can I help the most?
- What can I help them achieve?
- Why should they care?
blocks.zh:
- 我能帮助谁最多？
- 我能帮他们实现什么？
- 他们为什么要关心？

blocks.en: Focus solely on helping those people achieve that thing because they're lives wouldn't be the same without it.
blocks.zh: 把全部精力放在帮助这些人实现那件事上，因为少了它，他们的人生会截然不同。

blocks.en: Why doesn't finding the "best" niche work?
blocks.zh: 为什么寻找那个“最佳”细分市场行不通？

blocks.en: Well... just look at how many people don't quit, but there are other reasons.
blocks.zh: 嗯……看看有多少人没能坚持下来就知道了，不过还有别的原因。

blocks.en: 1) By default, you're entering a space that you know nothing about with people you don't care about.
blocks.zh: 1）默认情况下，你闯入的是一个自己一无所知的领域，面对的是一群你根本不在乎的人。

blocks.en: 2) That niche isn't going to be profitable if you don't understand it inside and out.
blocks.zh: 2）如果你对那个细分市场没有透彻的了解，它就不可能为你带来利润。

blocks.en: 3) You are already part of a niche. You already have skill and expertise that's helped you... so it can help someone else.
blocks.zh: 3）你本身就已经身处某个细分市场之中了。你已经拥有帮助过自己的技能和专长……那么它同样能帮助别人。

blocks.en: So, stop trying to "find" a niche.
blocks.zh: 所以，别再试图去“寻找”细分市场了。

blocks.en: Create a niche by attracting the people you can help the most.
blocks.zh: 去创造一个细分市场，通过吸引那些你能帮助最多的人。

blocks.en: Another problem:
blocks.zh: 还有一个问题：

blocks.en: When you focus on a niche, you box yourself in for no reason and limit yourself.
blocks.zh: 当你专注于某个细分市场时，你会毫无必要地把自己框住，限制住自己。

blocks.en: When you focus on pain points, you resonate with anyone with those pain points.
blocks.zh: 而当你专注于痛点时，你会与所有拥有这些痛点的人产生共鸣。

blocks.en: In other words, you gain more leverage and reach without sacrificing the benefits of niching down.
blocks.zh: 换句话说，你能获得更大的杠杆和更广的触达，同时不必牺牲深耕细分的那些好处。

blocks.en: The lesson:
blocks.zh: 教训是：

blocks.en: Focus on one burning pain point.
blocks.zh: 专注在一个火烧眉毛的痛点上。

blocks.en: (This answers the "why should they care" question)
blocks.zh: （这回答了“他们为什么要关心”这个问题）

blocks.en: Create a product or service that resolves it.
blocks.zh: 打造一款产品或服务来解决它。

blocks.en: (This answers the "what can I help them achieve" question).
blocks.zh: （这回答了“我能帮他们实现什么”这个问题）。

blocks.en: Write content around that pain point to attract people that you can help the most.
blocks.zh: 围绕那个痛点来创作内容，吸引那些你最能够帮助到的人。

blocks.en: If you can persist through trial and error, I have no doubt you'll win.
blocks.zh: 只要你能在反复试错中坚持下来，我毫不怀疑你会成功。

blocks.en: Ad (scroll away if you don't like ads):
blocks.zh: 广告（不喜欢广告的话请直接划走）：

blocks.en: By the way, the One-Person Business Launchpad is 50% off until the end of Black Friday weekend.
blocks.zh: 顺便说一下，一人企业启动营（One-Person Business Launchpad）在黑色星期五周末结束前五折优惠。

blocks.en: >> thedankoe.com/get/opbl
blocks.zh: >> thedankoe.com/get/opbl

blocks.en: Grab it here if you want arguably the simplest way to start a modern business.
blocks.zh: 如果你想要一个可以说是最简单的现代创业起步方式，就点这里拿下它。

blocks.en: The more technology advances, the more important it is to be a generalist, polymath, and creator.
blocks.zh: 技术越进步，成为通才、博学者和创作者就越重要。

blocks.en: My creator toolstack:
blocks.zh: 我的创作者工具栈：

blocks.en: Beehiiv for email list and newsletter.
blocks.zh: Beehiiv，用来管理邮件列表和新闻通讯。

blocks.en: Stan for simple products, landing pages and payments.
blocks.zh: Stan，用来做简单产品、落地页和收款。

blocks.en: Kortex for content, writing, planning, and never losing ideas.
blocks.zh: Kortex，用来管理内容、写作、规划，再也不丢想法。

blocks.en: After 5 years and trying every software under the sun, I've simplified everything down to this.
blocks.zh: 五年里我试遍了天下所有软件，最后把一切精简成了这样。

blocks.en: Stop trying to learn "skills."
blocks.zh: 别再试图学习「技能」了。

blocks.en: Nothing valuable is built with ONE skill.
blocks.zh: 没有任何有价值的东西是靠单一技能构建的。

blocks.en: Instead, learn individual techniques that allow you to build a project that others find useful.
blocks.zh: 相反，去学习一个个具体的技术，让你能够构建出对他人有用的项目。

blocks.en: Stack techniques, not skills, and you'll slowly reduce your chances of being replaced.
blocks.zh: 要叠加技术，而不是技能，这样你被取代的几率就会慢慢降低。

blocks.en: The greatest mistake you can make is not making any mistakes.
blocks.zh: 你能犯的最大错误，就是什么错误都不犯。

blocks.en: The mind is always listening.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑时刻都在倾听。

blocks.en: If you're always focused on failure, you will fail. If you're always focused on success, you will succeed.
blocks.zh: 如果你总是关注失败，你就会失败。如果你总是关注成功，你就会成功。

blocks.en: Your mind absorbs information that conditions you to acheive your goals, but most people's goal is to fail, they just aren't conscious of it.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑会吸收信息，从而让你条件反射般地去实现目标，但大多数人的目标其实是失败，只是他们自己没意识到。

blocks.en: If you haven't started the project, most of your learning is a wasteful mental masturbation.
blocks.zh: 如果你还没开始做项目，那你大部分的学习都只是浪费精力的精神自慰。

blocks.en: Your mind is wired for survival.
blocks.zh: 你的大脑天生就是为了生存。

blocks.en: *It remembers things that helps solve a problem, resolve a pain, or connect a pattern.*
blocks.zh: *它会记住那些有助于解决问题、缓解痛苦或连接模式的东西。*

blocks.en: When you build a project and get stuck, THAT'S when your mind wants to remember anything that can help.
blocks.zh: 当你动手做项目并卡住时，那才是你的大脑想要记住一切可能有帮助的东西的时候。

blocks.en: We're addicted to our phones.
blocks.zh: 我们对手机上瘾。

blocks.en: We're disconnected from nature.
blocks.zh: 我们与自然脱节。

blocks.en: Jobs are at the threat of replacement.
blocks.zh: 工作面临被取代的威胁。

blocks.en: Schools and religious ideologies are losing trust.
blocks.zh: 学校和宗教意识形态正在失去信任。

blocks.en: We're going through a meaning crisis.
blocks.zh: 我们正经历一场意义危机。

blocks.en:
Here's how you navigate it:
youtu.be/uy9_bfhfFvQ
blocks.zh:
这是应对之道：
youtu.be/uy9_bfhfFvQ

blocks.en: How I structure my mornings:
blocks.zh: 我如何安排早晨：

blocks.en:
- 3-5 lever moving tasks
- 90-minute time blocks
- 15-30 minute walks between
blocks.zh:
- 3-5 项能撬动全局的任务
- 90 分钟的时间块
- 中间穿插 15-30 分钟的散步

blocks.en: Productivity, creativity, and health in its simplest form.
blocks.zh: 生产力、创造力与健康，最简形式。

blocks.en: Repeat until you can sleep well knowing you laid a puzzle piece for your ideal future.
blocks.zh: 不断重复，直到你能安然入睡——因为你为自己理想的未来，拼上了一块拼图。

blocks.en: The problem isn't that you don't know what to work on. It's that you haven't tried anything outside of what your parents, teachers, and boss have assigned to you. You haven't experimented with life to the point of finding that one thing you can't help but work on.
blocks.zh: 问题不在于你不知道该做什么。而在于，除了父母、老师和老板指派给你的事情之外，你什么都没试过。你还没有在生活里反复试验，直到找到那件你忍不住想做的事。

blocks.en: Social media is the fast food of socialization.
blocks.zh: 社交媒体是社交的快餐。

blocks.en: Porn is the fast food of intimacy.
blocks.zh: 色情是亲密关系的快餐。

blocks.en: Video games are the fast food of achievement.
blocks.zh: 电子游戏是成就感的快餐。

blocks.en: Netflix is the fast food of entertainment.
blocks.zh: Netflix是娱乐的快餐。

blocks.en: Meticulously tested combinations of digital fat, sugar, and salt that trigger your survival instincts.
blocks.zh: 这些经过精心测试的数字脂肪、糖和盐的组合，触发着你的生存本能。

blocks.en: Going on a walk is a micro dopamine detox.
blocks.zh: 散步就是一种微型多巴胺排毒。

blocks.en: If you become your environment, create better environments.
blocks.zh: 既然你会被环境塑造，那就去创造更好的环境。

blocks.en: Broken Windows Theory:
blocks.zh: 破窗理论：

blocks.en: Crime dramatically increases in an area with broken windows (a place where crime would happen). Crime decreases in a clean area.
blocks.zh: 一个地方如果窗户破了（犯罪容易滋生的地方），犯罪率就会急剧上升；而干净整洁的地方，犯罪率则会下降。

blocks.en: The Lesson:
blocks.zh: 这个道理告诉我们：

blocks.en: Your environment influences your behavior more than you think. Your room. Your workspace. Where you hang out.
blocks.zh: 环境对你行为的影响，远超你的想象。你的房间、你的工作空间、你混迹的圈子，都是如此。

blocks.en: If you aren't where you want to be, start by creating an environment that influences you toward your goals, not away from them.
blocks.zh: 如果你还没活成自己想要的样子，那就先从营造一个环境开始——一个能把你推向目标、而非拉你远离目标的环境。

blocks.en: My biggest fear is waking up to live the same life as everyone else over and over again. Doing work I don't care about for people I don't care about. Never understanding, always reacting. No energy or time to think, plan, build, or change. Stuck on the surface as decades pass by.
blocks.zh: 我最大的恐惧，就是日复一日醒来，过着和所有人一样的生活。做着自己不在乎的工作，服务着自己不在乎的人。从不理解，只会反应。没精力也没时间去思考、去规划、去构建、去改变。几十年过去，始终浮在表面。

blocks.en: For my young ones out there who were raised to think that:
blocks.zh: 写给我的年轻朋友们，那些从小被灌输以下观念的人：

blocks.en:
- Investing your allowance
- Saving any leftover money
- Investing in real estate
- Budgeting and hating your life
blocks.zh:
- 拿零花钱去投资
- 把剩下的钱存起来
- 投资房地产
- 做预算，然后痛恨自己的生活

blocks.en:
Were how you become "rich," this video is for you:
youtu.be/EdM9SNf8tFc
blocks.zh:
以为这些就是变“富”的途径——这个视频就是为你准备的：
youtu.be/EdM9SNf8tFc

blocks.en: Do everything in your power to maintain focus on the intersection of what's needed, what matters, and what you feel most drawn to learn and build. If it's not needed, doesn't matter, or you don't care about it, you are wasting your life.
blocks.zh: 竭尽全力，把注意力聚焦在三个圈的交汇处：什么是被需要的、什么是重要的、什么是你最渴望去学习和构建的。如果它不被需要、不重要，或者你根本不在乎，那你就是在浪费自己的生命。

blocks.en: It’s pretty mind blowing.
blocks.zh: 这挺令人震撼的。

blocks.en: What started as a few “esoteric health” accounts on Twitter is turning into a US health reform.
blocks.zh: 最初只是推特上几个“小众健康”账号，如今却正在演变成一场美国健康改革。

blocks.en: There no way in hell RFK got the info from mainstream sources.
blocks.zh: RFK（小罗伯特·肯尼迪）绝不可能从主流渠道获得这些信息。

blocks.en: Passionate individuals have a lot of power if they share their ideas and discoveries.
blocks.zh: 充满热情的人，只要愿意分享自己的想法和发现，就拥有巨大的力量。

blocks.en: "Educated" isn't the right word.
blocks.zh: “受过教育”这个词用得不对。

blocks.en: "Schooled" or "indoctrinated" is.
blocks.zh: “被学校规训”或“被灌输”才是。

blocks.en: This isn't a fight between red and blue. This is a fight between freedom and slavery. Slavery of the mind.
blocks.zh: 这不是红与蓝之争，这是自由与奴役之争。是思想上的奴役。

blocks.en: The difference between schooling and education is the difference between imposed order and emergent order.
blocks.zh: 学校教育与真正的教育之间的区别，就是强加秩序与自生秩序之间的区别。

blocks.en: Schooling offers a narrow and rigid path that serves the dominant social system. If you don't conform to that path by memorizing facts and regurgitating information, you are punished. Bad grades and the threat of not getting a job. Schooling makes you a useful worker.
blocks.zh: 学校教育提供的是一条狭窄而僵化的路径，服务于占主导地位的社会体系。如果你不遵从这条路——死记硬背事实、照搬 regurgitate 信息——就会受到惩罚。成绩差，还有找不到工作的威胁。学校教育把你变成一名有用的工人。

blocks.en: If you understand how the mind works, you understand how large of a trap it is to narrow your mind on one singular path – that you did not willfully choose, but were conditioned to pursue – because it leads to stupidity and dependency on someone else for your survival.
blocks.zh: 如果你懂得心智是如何运作的，你就会明白：把心智窄化到一条你并非自愿选择、而是被训练去追求的单一道路上，是个多大的陷阱——因为它会导致愚昧，并让你在生存上依赖他人。

blocks.en: Think about it.
blocks.zh: 想想看。

blocks.en: You are enticed into going to school because it's the only path you know. You only know that one path because your parents and teachers also went through their own schooling. The teachers learned how to become teachers through other teachers. Your parents survival is probably dependent on the specialist work they were trained into by a system of teachers teaching teachers how to become teachers.
blocks.zh: 你被诱导去上学，因为这是你唯一知道的路径。你之所以只知这一条路，是因为你的父母和老师也经历过他们自己的学校教育。老师们是通过其他老师学会如何当老师的。你父母的生存，很可能依赖于某个体系训练他们从事的专业工作——而这个体系，就是由老师教老师如何当老师构成的。

blocks.en: You want a degree because of status. You want the title because you think it will help you survive. So your mind orients itself with that goal and everything else becomes unimportant. Over the course of 4-12 years, you do almost nothing aside from study a biased curriculum and relieve stress through pleasure when you can. Your mind becomes hardened and reactive by default.
blocks.zh: 你想要一个学位，是为了地位。你想要那个头衔，是因为你认为它能帮你生存。于是你的心智就朝着那个目标定向，其他一切变得无关紧要。在4到12年的时间里，除了学习一套有偏见的课程、以及在可能时通过享乐来缓解压力之外，你几乎什么都没做。你的心智变得僵化，默认状态下只会被动反应。

blocks.en: Education, on the other hand, offers no path. Education is discovery. Education is trial and error toward a goal that you deem meaningful. Education is the process of acquiring the knowledge and skill necessary to create a meaningful life.
blocks.zh: 而教育则不同，它不提供任何路径。教育是发现。教育是朝着你认为有意义的目标进行试错。教育是获取必要知识与技能、以创造有意义人生的过程。

blocks.en: Education comes down to two main topics:
blocks.zh: 教育归结为两个主要议题：

blocks.en:
1) Learning how to learn.
2) Learning how to live.
blocks.zh:
1）学会如何学习。
2）学会如何生活。

blocks.en: Neither of which are taught in the school system. You are told what to learn and how to live rather than discovering it for yourself.
blocks.zh: 这两者在学校体系里都没人教。你被告知该学什么、该如何生活，而不是自己去发现。

blocks.en: As humans, we derive a lot of meaning from how we contribute to the world. Deep down, we all want to do work that matters. We all want to contribute in a meaningful way to our tribe and world.
blocks.zh: 作为人类，我们从自己对世界的贡献中获得大量意义。内心深处，我们都想做重要的工作。我们都想以有意义的方式为自己的群体和世界做出贡献。

blocks.en: If our work is imposed on us, or assigned to us, it's no wonder why we can't find an inherent meaning to our life. That alone explains much of the vocal "blue" behavior. The only meaningful and important thing to them is making sure that others fall in line and conform to the same standards they did because they failed to think for themselves.
blocks.zh: 如果我们的工作是被强加或指派给我们的，那难怪我们找不到人生的内在意义。仅这一点就解释了大量那些嚷嚷着的“蓝调”行为。对他们来说，唯一有意义、重要的事，就是确保别人也循规蹈矩、遵从他们曾遵从的同一套标准——因为他们自己没能独立思考。

blocks.en: There are 2 options here.
blocks.zh: 这里有两条路可选。

blocks.en:
1) Reform the education system.
2) Pursue your own interest-based education.
blocks.zh:
1）改革教育体系。
2）追求你自己基于兴趣的教育。

blocks.en: The first can be influenced by exposing the current systems flaws. It's going to take work, waking people up, and new solutions being built by independent thinkers.
blocks.zh: 第一条路可以通过揭露现行体系的缺陷来施加影响。这需要付出努力，唤醒人们，并由独立思考者构建新的解决方案。

blocks.en: The second can happen at any time.
blocks.zh: 第二条路随时都可以发生。

blocks.en: You simply have to realize that floating through life isn't going to take you anywhere meaningful. In fact, doing nothing by your own desire only leads to people taking advantage of you.
blocks.zh: 你只需意识到：随波逐流地混日子，不会把你带到任何有意义的地方。事实上，只按自己的欲望什么都不做，只会让别人占你便宜。

blocks.en: Question everything. Contemplate your place on this planet. Think deeply about what you want out of life. Pursue the interests that will take you there.
blocks.zh: 质疑一切。思考你在这个星球上的位置。深入思考你想从生活中得到什么。去追求那些能带你到那里的兴趣。

blocks.en: You have access to the internet. If you have the intense desire to learn, build, and adapt, you'll turn out just fine.
blocks.zh: 你能上网。如果你有强烈的渴望去学习、去构建、去适应，你最终会过得不错。

blocks.en: @BasedMikeLee
America’s universities are effective at spreading Marxism
blocks.zh: 美国的大学在传播马克思主义方面很有效

blocks.en: The problem with forcing a narrow (and silently destructive) worldview on the entire population is that eventually, people get sick of it and turn against you, even if they swore they never would.
blocks.zh: 把一种狭隘（且悄然具有破坏性）的世界观强加给全体民众，问题在于：最终人们会厌倦它并转而反对你，即便他们曾发誓绝不会如此。

blocks.en: My timeline is filled with optimism and focus on health, aesthetics, learning, building, thinking, technology, ecology, and economics. As someone who's been immaturely apolitical most of my life, these are values I can heavily get behind. Smells like a new Golden Age.
blocks.zh: 我的时间线充满了乐观，聚焦于健康、美学、学习、构建、思考、技术、生态和经济。作为一个大半辈子都不成熟地不关心政治的人，这些价值观是我能大力支持的。闻起来像是一个新的黄金时代。

blocks.en: If you can predict everything they are going to say, they aren't thinking for themselves.
blocks.zh: 如果你能预测他们要说的一切，那他们就不是在独立思考。

blocks.en: Most people haven't practiced thinking.
blocks.zh: 大多数人从未练习过思考。

blocks.en: When you talk to them, you aren't talking to them. You're talking to the TV. Social media. Their parents. Their teachers. Their insecurities and trauma.
blocks.zh: 当你和他们交谈时，你并不是在和他们交谈。你是在和电视交谈。和社交媒体。和他们的父母。和他们的老师。和他们的不安全感与创伤交谈。

blocks.en: It's very robotic. The definition of inauthentic.
blocks.zh: 这非常机械。不真实的典型定义。

blocks.en: Disconnect and think more.
blocks.zh: 断开连接，多思考。

blocks.en: A meaningful life is found in alignment:
blocks.zh: 有意义的人生，源于三者的协调一致：

blocks.en: Being – soaking in the beauty of reality.
blocks.zh: 存在——沉浸于现实之美。

blocks.en: Doing – contributing to the beauty of reality.
blocks.zh: 行动——为现实之美贡献力量。

blocks.en: Becoming – increasing your capacity for beauty, enhancing both.
blocks.zh: 成长——提升你感知美的能力，让存在与行动相得益彰。

blocks.en: Being influences doing. Doing conditions your mind and influences who you become.
blocks.zh: 存在影响行动。行动塑造你的心智，并影响你会成为什么样的人。

blocks.en: Most people are trapped in doing mode.
blocks.zh: 大多数人被困在行动模式中。

blocks.en: Niching their attention down to menial tasks and pleasures without a second thought of what they lead to.
blocks.zh: 他们把注意力压缩到琐碎的事务和享乐上，全然不去想这些会导向何方。

blocks.en: They rarely allow themselves to be. So their actions are misaligned by default. They create a life they despise without knowing how.
blocks.zh: 他们很少允许自己真正地存在。因此，他们的行动从一开始就是错位的。他们在不知不觉中，创造了一个自己厌恶的人生。
